genres.name: Portraits
genres.blurb: Faces from long ago that still seem to look back at you.

genres.name: Seas & Ships
genres.blurb: Storms, sailors, harbors and endless waves.

genres.name: Faith & Scripture
genres.blurb: Stories from the Bible and sacred traditions.

genres.name: Still Life & Animals
genres.blurb: Flowers, fruit, horses, hounds and more.

genres.name: Dreams & Big Ideas
genres.blurb: Symbols, feelings and wild new ways of seeing.

collections.name: Art for Kids
collections.blurb: The 100 most fun paintings for young explorers: animals, fairy tales, circuses, storms and wonders.
collections.intro: Welcome, young explorers! These 100 paintings are picked for you: tigers in thunderstorms, mermaids, a giant wave, 42 cats and a spinning top. Each one has a little challenge — can you find what the painter hid?

collections.name: Jewish Artists
collections.blurb: Paintings by Jewish artists across Europe and beyond, from Amsterdam to Montmartre to Jerusalem.
collections.intro: These painters came from Jewish families in Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, Russia, France, Italy and beyond. Some painted Jewish life and history; many painted whatever they loved — fishermen, gardens, city streets and friends. Together, they show how much Jewish artists helped shape modern art.

collections.name: Canada
collections.blurb: From Tom Thomson's wild north to Krieghoff's snowy Quebec: Canada's most important early paintings.
collections.intro: Canada's art begins with explorers and Indigenous portraits, grows through the snowy villages of Quebec and ends with the Group of Seven's wild north. Here are the paintings that taught Canadians to see their own land. Some paintings show Indigenous peoples as artists of the time saw them, so it's worth asking whose story is being told.

collections.name: Norway
collections.blurb: Fjords, Vikings, trolls and Munch: the great paintings of Norway.
collections.intro: Norway's painters gave the world dramatic fjords and misty mountains, the Vikings of the sagas, cozy farmhouse lights and the famously haunting art of Edvard Munch. Many of these artists also worked in Denmark and Germany, where Norwegian painters often trained.

collections.name: United States
collections.blurb: Great American paintings: wild landscapes, sea storms, Revolutionary heroes and the artists who made America look like itself.
collections.intro: From the Hudson River School's glowing wilderness to Winslow Homer's stormy seas, from Revolutionary War heroes to Mary Cassatt's quiet rooms, these are the great American paintings from the nation's first 150 years.

collections.name: France
collections.blurb: Impressionists, revolutionaries and the heart of modern art.
collections.intro: France gave us Impressionism, Romanticism and many of history's best-known paintings.

collections.name: Italy
collections.blurb: Italian painters of the last 300 years, from Venice to Milan.
collections.intro: Italy's art after the Renaissance kept going: romantic lovers, sunlit Alpine peaks and shimmering portraits.

collections.name: Spain
collections.blurb: Goya, Sorolla and the painters of Spain.
collections.intro: From Goya's court portraits and dark visions to Sorolla's dazzling beaches.

collections.name: Netherlands
collections.blurb: Van Gogh, the Hague School and Dutch painters.
collections.intro: The land of windmills, canals and Van Gogh's swirling skies.

collections.name: Germany
collections.blurb: Romantic mountains, expressive colors and German painters.
collections.intro: Germany's painters gave us misty Romantic mountains, wild Expressionist colors and dreamlike modern art.

collections.name: United Kingdom
collections.blurb: Turner's storms, Pre-Raphaelite fairy tales and England's great portraits.
collections.intro: British painters loved storms, fairy tales, portraits and the English countryside.

collections.name: Russia
collections.blurb: Giant historical canvases, forests and snowy landscapes from Russia.
collections.intro: Russian painters made huge, emotional pictures of history, forests, rivers and the lives of ordinary people.

collections.name: Poland
collections.blurb: Poland's proud history in paint.
collections.intro: Polish painters kept their country's history alive in huge canvases, countryside scenes and portraits.

collections.name: Sweden
collections.blurb: Midsummer dances, cozy homes and Nordic light.
collections.intro: Sweden's painters made sparkling summer pictures, family homes full of sunlight and scenes from Norse legends.

collections.name: Denmark
collections.blurb: The Danish Golden Age and the artists of Skagen.
collections.intro: Quiet Copenhagen rooms, sunny beaches at Skagen and some of the calmest paintings ever made.

collections.name: Finland
collections.blurb: Finnish heroes, forests and the Kalevala.
collections.intro: Finnish painters turned their national legends and lakeside forests into glowing pictures.

collections.name: Austria
collections.blurb: Vienna's golden age of painting.
collections.intro: Austrian art sparkled in turn-of-the-century Vienna with gold leaf, bold lines and dreamy patterns.

collections.name: Belgium
collections.blurb: Masks, Symbolists and Belgian painters.
collections.intro: Belgium's painters gave us carnival masks, mysterious Symbolist dreams and sunlit gardens.

collections.name: Japan
collections.blurb: Woodblock prints, folding screens and the painters of Japan.
collections.intro: Japan's artists gave the world The Great Wave, golden folding screens, puppies, cats and ghosts. This collection includes woodblock prints as well as paintings, since prints were one of Japan's great art forms.

collections.name: China
collections.blurb: Imperial court paintings from the Qing dynasty.
collections.intro: Huge scrolls, emperors on horseback and bustling cities from the court of the Qing emperors.

collections.name: Middle East
collections.blurb: Painters from Turkey and Iran.
collections.intro: Ottoman and Persian painters who studied European techniques and painted their own world: palaces, courtyards and quiet moments.

collections.name: Mexico
collections.blurb: Volcano landscapes and folk traditions from Mexico.
collections.intro: Mexican painters celebrated their volcanoes, valleys and traditions like the Day of the Dead.

collections.name: Australia
collections.blurb: Sunburnt landscapes, sheepshearers and the Heidelberg School.
collections.intro: Australian painters like Tom Roberts and Arthur Streeton painted the golden bush and the working people of the outback.

Q528460.bio: Jozef Israëls was born into a Jewish family in Groningen, in the Netherlands, and became the leader of the Hague School of painters. He is famous for his tender pictures of fisherfolk and poor families in the dunes. He lived in Amsterdam and The Hague, and spent many summers in the fishing village of Zandvoort. He died in 1911.

Q213973.bio: Johann Heinrich Wilhelm Tischbein was born in Haina, Germany, to a family of painters. He lived in Rome and Naples and became a friend of the poet Goethe. He painted portraits and scenes from mythology. He died in Eutin, Germany, in 1829.

Q664680.bio: Alexander von Kotzebue was a Russian painter born in Königsberg in 1815, the son of the famous German dramatist. He became a battle painter for the Russian tsars and later lived in Munich. He died in Munich in 1889.

Q158062.bio: Max Liebermann was born in Berlin to a wealthy Jewish family and became the leading German Impressionist. He painted workers, beer gardens and gardens, and he served as president of the Prussian Academy of Arts. After the Nazis came to power in 1933, he was forced to give up his positions. He died in Berlin in 1935.

Q727637.bio: Wojciech Kossak was a Polish painter born in Paris in 1856 who lived in Kraków. He painted battle scenes, horses and moments from Poland's history, as part of a family of artists. He died in Kraków in 1942.

Q921230.bio: Johan Thomas Lundbye was a Danish painter born in Kalundborg in 1818. He painted fields, animals and old monuments of the Danish countryside. He died young, at 29, in 1848, during the first Schleswig War.

Q2199553.bio: Laurits Andersen Ring was born in a village in Denmark and became a leading Danish painter. He is known for quiet, thoughtful scenes of country life and portraits of his family. He lived and worked in the Danish countryside. He died in 1933.

Q432826.bio: Saturnino Herrán was born in Aguascalientes, Mexico, in 1887, and moved to Mexico City to study art. He painted Mexican workers, Indigenous people and traditions in a bold, strong style. He helped inspire later Mexican muralists. He died in 1918 at only 31.

Q817668.bio: Benjamin Robert Haydon was an English painter born in Plymouth in 1786. He wanted to be a great painter of history, made huge pictures and also lively group portraits, but was always in debt. He lived in London and died there in 1846.

Q609959.bio: Paul Peel was born in London, Ontario, and studied in Philadelphia and in Paris, where he became a successful painter. His warm, sunny pictures of children won prizes at the Paris Salon. He died young, in Paris, at the age of 31.

Q193064.bio: Ivan Shishkin was born in the town of Yelabuga, in Russia, and became the great poet of the Russian forest. He lived in Saint Petersburg and traveled into the countryside to sketch trees in incredible detail. His pine and birch forests are among the most loved Russian paintings. He worked up until the day he died at his easel in 1898.

Q6682.bio: Gustave Doré was a French artist born in Strasbourg in 1832. He became the most famous book illustrator of his time, drawing scenes for the Bible, Dante's Inferno, Don Quixote and fairy tales. He lived in Paris and died there in 1883.

Q5716922.bio: Henry Mayer, nicknamed Hy Mayer, was a cartoonist born in Worms, Germany, in 1868. He moved to the United States, where he became a popular cartoonist for Puck magazine and a pioneer of animated cartoons. He lived in New York and died in 1954.

Q3133062.bio: Henry Sandham was born in Montreal and became a leading Canadian painter, illustrator and a founding member of the Royal Canadian Academy. He later lived in Boston and London. His landscapes and harbor scenes were widely admired. He died in London in 1910.

Q175130.bio: Alfred Sisley was born in Paris to English parents and was one of the key Impressionist painters. He painted quiet landscapes along the Seine River and in small villages near Paris. He lived most of his life in France but remained a British citizen. He died in Moret-sur-Loing in 1899.

Q192544.bio: Henryk Siemiradzki was born in what is now Ukraine to a Polish family and studied in Saint Petersburg, Munich and Rome. He lived mainly in Rome, where he painted giant, sunny pictures of ancient Greece and Rome. He was one of the most successful painters in Europe. He died in 1902.

Q453972.bio: John Collier was born in London and studied art in London, Paris and Munich. He painted portraits and scenes from history and legend, often with strong feelings. He also wrote about art and science. He died in London in 1934.

Q3182324.bio: John Quidor was born in New Jersey and worked in New York City. He made humorous, wild illustrations of stories by Washington Irving, such as 'Rip Van Winkle' and 'Sleepy Hollow'. He was not widely known in his lifetime. He died in Jersey City in 1881.

Q2065760.bio: Władysław Podkowiński was born in Warsaw, Poland, and was a leading Impressionist and Symbolist painter. He studied in Warsaw and Paris, and he is remembered for the shocking 'Frenzy of Exultations.' He died young, at 29, in 1895.

Q720035.bio: Nicolaas Pieneman was born in Amersfoort, in the Netherlands, and became a portrait and history painter in Amsterdam. He painted royalty, battle scenes and a famous picture of the arrest of the Javanese prince Diponegoro. He died in Amsterdam in 1860.

Q2090815.bio: Jean Leon Gerome Ferris was an American painter born in Philadelphia in 1863. He painted a series of scenes of American history, from the Pilgrims to the Revolution, and his pictures were published in many schoolbooks. He died in Philadelphia in 1930.

x-workshop-of-matthaus-merian.bio: Matthäus Merian was a Swiss-born engraver who lived in Frankfurt, Germany, and published famous books of city views and the news of the Thirty Years' War. This engraving is from his workshop, which kept making prints after he died in 1650.

Q346483.bio: Maurice Cullen was born in St. John's, Newfoundland, and grew up in Montreal. He studied in Paris, and became known for his glowing paintings of snowy Montreal and the St. Lawrence River. In World War I he served as an official Canadian war artist. He died in 1934.

Q552440.bio: Constantin Meunier was a Belgian sculptor and painter born in Etterbeek in 1831. He is famous for his dignified pictures and statues of coal miners, steelworkers and dockers, and he lived in Brussels, where he died in 1905.

Q184212.bio: Théodore Géricault was born in Rouen, France, and grew up in Paris, where he fell in love with horses and dramatic subjects. He studied wounded soldiers and even hospital patients so he could paint with truth. He rose to fame with 'The Raft of the Medusa' at 27. A passionate horse rider, he died in Paris at only 32, partly after riding accidents.

Q2775516.bio: James Wilson Morrice was born in Montreal and spent most of his life in Paris, where he became a friend of Matisse. He painted quiet landscapes and city scenes in bright, simple colors, and also traveled to North Africa and the Caribbean. He is regarded as Canada's first modern painter. He died in Tunis in 1924.

x-arthur-rothstein.bio: Arthur Rothstein was an American photographer born in New York City in 1915. He was the first photographer hired by the government's Farm Security Administration, capturing the Dust Bowl, and later worked for Look magazine. He died in New Rochelle in 1985.

Q3196514.bio: Suzuki Kiitsu was born in Edo (Tokyo) and studied under Sakai Hōitsu. He painted flowers, plants and scenes of nature in the Rinpa style, with bold colors and graceful shapes. He is admired for his modern-looking designs. He died in 1858.

Q315102.bio: Alexander Roslin was born in Malmö, Sweden, and became a leading portrait painter at the French court. He lived in Paris, where he painted queens, kings and the leading minds of the day. His specialty was the shimmer of silks and satins. He died in Paris in 1793.

x-anonymous-illuminator-french-chronicle.bio: This picture comes from a medieval French royal chronicle, painted by an illuminator whose name was not recorded. Manuscripts like this were made by workshops of artists in the 1300s and 1400s for kings and nobles.

Q18289401.bio: Eugène Romain Thirion was a French painter born in Paris in 1839. He painted religious and historical scenes and portraits, and is best known for his poetic picture of Joan of Arc. He lived in Paris and died there in 1910.

Q1969461.bio: Thomas Fearnley was born in Halden, Norway, in 1802 and studied in Copenhagen and Stockholm. He traveled widely in Europe and was a friend of J. C. Dahl and J. M. W. Turner. He painted landscapes in Italy, Switzerland and Norway. He died young in Munich in 1842.

Q1161631.bio: Daniel Maclise was an Irish painter born in Cork in 1806. He moved to London, where he painted big scenes from history and literature, including huge murals in the Houses of Parliament, and was close friends with Charles Dickens. He died in Chelsea in 1870.

Q448189.bio: Jacek Malczewski was born in Radom, Poland, and became a leading Symbolist painter. He studied in Kraków and Paris and often painted himself in dreamlike scenes full of Polish folklore and history. He lived in Kraków, where he later taught. He died there in 1929.

Q4568470.bio: Joachim Frich was a Norwegian landscape painter born in Bergen in 1810. He studied in Dresden with Johan Christian Dahl. He painted the fjords and mountains of Norway. He died in Christiania in 1858.

Q1342328.bio: Michiel Sweerts was a Flemish painter born in Brussels in 1618. He worked in Rome, where he painted busy city scenes, and later in Brussels and Amsterdam, before joining a missionary journey to Asia. He died in Goa, India, in 1664.

Q585323.bio: Franz von Lenbach was a German painter born in Schrobenhausen in 1836. He became the most fashionable portrait painter in Munich and was famous for his many portraits of Otto von Bismarck and of the pope and emperors. He died in Munich in 1904.

x-works-progress-administration-poster-a.bio: This poster was made by an artist working for the Works Progress Administration, a New Deal program that hired thousands of artists in the 1930s to make posters, murals and prints for the public.

Q170068.bio: Akseli Gallen-Kallela was born in Pori, Finland, and became the country's most famous painter. He painted scenes from the Kalevala, Finland's national epic, and studied in Paris. He lived in Finland and traveled to Africa and the United States. He died in Stockholm in 1931.

Q2959390.bio: Charles Huot was born in Quebec City and studied painting in Paris. He became one of Quebec's most important history painters, creating large murals for the Quebec Legislature. He also taught drawing and illustrated books. He died in 1930.

Q310437.bio: Alexandre Cabanel was born in Montpellier, France, and became a star of the French Academy. He lived in Paris, where he taught at the École des Beaux-Arts. He painted classical and historical subjects, as well as portraits of the rich. Napoleon III admired him and bought his work.

Q20017223.bio: Merle De Vore Johnson was an American illustrator born in Oregon City in 1874. He drew posters and magazine covers and later became a well-known collector of rare books. He lived in New York and died there in 1935.

Q270658.bio: Jacob Jordaens was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1593 who lived there all his life. He worked alongside Rubens and became famous for lively scenes with big, rosy figures, including feasts and proverbs. He died in Antwerp in 1678.

Q37140565.bio: Julian O. Davidson was an American marine painter born in Cumberland, Maryland, in 1853. He lived in New York, painting sea scenes and naval battles of the Civil War for popular prints. He died in 1894.

Q4768.bio: Karl Bryullov was born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, into a family of artists. He lived for many years in Italy, where he painted his huge masterpiece 'The Last Day of Pompeii.' He returned to Russia as a celebrity and was admired by writers like Pushkin. He died in Italy in 1852.

Q922483.bio: William Orpen was born near Dublin, Ireland, and became a leading portrait painter in London. He served as an official war artist in World War I and painted the Paris Peace Conference. He died in London in 1931.

Q3048418.bio: Edvard Isto was born in northern Finland and became a painter who studied in Helsinki and Paris. He is best known for 'The Attack,' which became a symbol of Finnish resistance. He died in Helsinki in 1905, at the age of 40.

Q127017.bio: Vasily Vereshchagin was born in Cherepovets, Russia, and traveled to Central Asia, India and the Balkans. He painted battlefields to show the true horror of war, sometimes as a war correspondent. His anti-war art shocked many viewers. He died in 1904 when a warship he was aboard struck a mine.

Q1346539.bio: Lars Hertervig was born on an island near Stavanger, Norway, and studied in Düsseldorf. He struggled with mental illness, was often poor, and was little understood in his lifetime. His glowing, dreamy landscapes are now seen as among the finest in Norwegian art. He died in Stavanger in 1902.

Q381299.bio: Louis-Michel van Loo was born in Toulon, France, to a family of painters. He worked in Paris and also in Spain as the court painter to King Philip V. His portraits show silk, lace and royal splendor. He died in Paris in 1771.

Q1805696.bio: Sébastien Leclerc was a French engraver born in Metz in 1637. He worked in Paris for Louis XIV, making many prints of the king's science and military projects. He died in Paris in 1714.

Q61064.bio: Wassily Kandinsky was born in Moscow and trained as a lawyer before becoming a painter at age 30. He lived in Russia, Germany and later France. He is considered one of the first artists to paint truly abstract works, using color and shape like music. He died in Neuilly-sur-Seine, near Paris, in 1944.

Q452733.bio: Amaldus Nielsen was a Norwegian landscape painter who painted the wild mountains and fjords of Norway. He studied in Düsseldorf and Munich. He lived to the age of 94 and died in Oslo in 1932.

Q5854655.bio: Axel Ender was a Norwegian painter born in 1853 in Asker. He studied in Germany and painted landscapes and folk scenes. He lived in Christiania (Oslo). He died in 1920.

Q1415196.bio: Jean-Jacques Scherrer was a French painter born in Lutterbach in Alsace in 1855. He worked in Paris, painting historical and patriotic pictures, especially of Joan of Arc, at a time when she was a national symbol after the war of 1870. He died in Paris in 1916.

Q1661665.bio: John Vanderlyn was born in Kingston, New York, and studied art in Paris. He was one of the first American painters to be trained in Europe, and painted large panoramas and history pictures. He painted 'Landing of Columbus' for the U.S. Capitol. He died in Kingston in 1852.

Q189117.bio: Jan Matejko was born in Kraków, Poland, and became the nation's great painter of history. He made huge canvases of Poland's glories and heartbreaks, at a time when Poland was no longer an independent country. He lived most of his life in Kraków, where he later directed the School of Fine Arts. He's a national hero for keeping Polish memory alive.

Q182664.bio: Giovanni Antonio Canal, known as Canaletto, was born in Venice and painted its canals, palaces, and festivals with great precision. His views were popular with wealthy British visitors on their tours of Italy, and he lived in London for several years. His paintings are still the way many people picture Venice. He died in Venice in 1768.

Q1494309.bio: Alphonse de Neuville was a French painter born in Saint-Omer in 1835. He became known for realistic scenes of the Franco-Prussian War, in which he had served, and for illustrating books. He lived in Paris and died there in 1885.

Q333323.bio: Pietro da Cortona was an Italian painter and architect born in the town of Cortona in 1596. He lived in Rome and became one of the leading artists of the Baroque, painting giant ceilings such as the one at the Palazzo Barberini. He died in Rome in 1669.

Q365891.bio: Adolphe Yvon was a French painter born in Eschviller in 1817. He painted large battles for the French army, including the Crimean and Italian campaigns, and spent his life in Paris, where he died in 1893.

Q310715.bio: Henri Fantin-Latour was born in Grenoble, France, and spent most of his life in Paris. He was a friend of Manet and the Impressionists, though his own style was more traditional. He painted lovely flowers and group portraits of artists and musicians. He died in 1904.

Q213163.bio: Élisabeth Louise Vigée Le Brun was born in Paris, the daughter of a painter, and became a famous portraitist at only 20. She painted Queen Marie Antoinette and fled France during the Revolution, working in Italy, Austria, Russia and England. She was one of the most successful women artists in history. She died in Paris in 1842.

x-english-school-formerly-attributed-to-.n: English School (formerly attributed to George Gower)
x-english-school-formerly-attributed-to-.bio: The Armada Portrait was painted by an unknown English artist in 1588. It was once thought to be by George Gower, Queen Elizabeth's Serjeant-Painter, but experts now believe it came from a workshop of several painters, and it exists in a few versions.

Q1543513.bio: Eugène Lenepveu was a French painter born in Angers in 1819. He won the Prix de Rome, directed the French Academy in Rome for several years, and painted a famous series of scenes from the life of Joan of Arc in the Panthéon in Paris. He died in Paris in 1898.

Q28867.bio: Juan Luna was born in the Philippines and studied art in Manila, Madrid and Rome. His enormous painting 'Spoliarium' won a gold medal in Madrid in 1884, and made him a hero to Filipinos. He lived in Spain and France and supported Philippine independence. He died in Hong Kong in 1899.

Q3123472.bio: Martin Johnson Heade was born in Pennsylvania and traveled widely. He is famous for his misty salt marshes, stormy skies, and his paintings of hummingbirds and orchids in Brazil. He settled in Florida late in life. He died in St. Augustine in 1904.

Q452321.bio: Emanuel Leutze was born in Schwäbisch Gmünd, Germany, and moved to the United States as a child. He later studied in Düsseldorf, Germany, and lived there for years while painting American history scenes. He returned to the U.S. in 1859 and worked in Washington, D.C. His painting of Washington crossing the Delaware became a national icon.

x-english-school-attributed-to-marcus-gh.n: English School (attributed to Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger)
x-english-school-attributed-to-marcus-gh.bio: The Rainbow Portrait of Elizabeth I was painted by an unknown English artist around 1602. It is sometimes attributed to Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger, a leading court portrait painter of the time, but experts are not sure.

Q1936604.bio: Reinier Nooms, also called Zeeman, was a Dutch painter and etcher born in Amsterdam around 1623. He had been a sailor, and he made detailed pictures of ships, harbors and sea battles. He died in Amsterdam in 1664.

Q7173913.bio: Peter F. Rothermel was an American painter born in Nescopeck, Pennsylvania, in 1812. He worked in Philadelphia, where he painted huge canvases of historical subjects, including the Battle of Gettysburg for the state of Pennsylvania. He died in Linfield, Pennsylvania, in 1895.

Q3340395.bio: Nicolas-Guy Brenet was a French painter born in Paris in 1728. He studied in Rome and became a history painter, painting scenes from ancient and national history for the French royal court. He died in Paris in 1792.

Q3786446.bio: Homer Watson was born in Doon, Ontario, near what is now Kitchener, and taught himself to paint. He became known for his dramatic pictures of fields, skies and rivers, and was admired by Oscar Wilde. He is considered a pioneer of Canadian landscape painting. He died in Kitchener in 1936.

Q2408093.bio: Charles-Nicolas Cochin was a French engraver and draftsman born in Paris in 1715. He was an official artist for Louis XV and the keeper of drawings at the Louvre, and he drew the frontispiece of the Encyclopédie. He died in Paris in 1790.

Q9319.bio: Jacopo Tintoretto was an Italian painter born in Venice in 1519. He lived in Venice all his life and painted huge, fast, dramatic canvases for churches and palaces, including the Doge's Palace. He died in Venice in 1594.

Q727643.bio: Paul Nash was an English painter born in London in 1889. He was an official war artist in both World Wars and painted haunting landscapes of broken trees and battlefields. He died in Boscombe, England, in 1946.

Q1827276.bio: Lionel Royer was a French painter born in Château-du-Loir in 1852. He studied in Paris and painted large pictures of French history and legend, which were popular in the years after France's defeat in the war of 1870. He died in Neuilly-sur-Seine in 1926.

Q928734.bio: Anicet Charles Gabriel Lemonnier was a French painter born in Rouen in 1743. He worked in Paris and was the director of the royal Gobelins tapestry works. He painted the Salon of Madame Geoffrin and died in Paris in 1824.

Q118810.bio: Marie-Guillemine Benoist was born in Paris and studied with Vigée Le Brun and Jacques-Louis David. She was one of the leading women painters of her time and exhibited at the Paris Salon. Her 'Portrait of Madeleine' is one of the most celebrated works of the French Revolution era. She died in Paris in 1826.

Q4661858.bio: Aaron Bohrod was an American painter born in Chicago in 1907. He served as an official US Army war artist in World War II in the Pacific and Europe and later became the University of Wisconsin's first artist in residence. He died in Madison in 1992.

x-unknown-artist.bio: The artist of this work is not known. Many early portraits, prints and manuscripts were made by artists whose names were never recorded or have since been lost.

Q69708.bio: Charles de Steuben was a German-born French painter born in Bauerbach in 1788. He moved to Paris as a child and became a leading painter of dramatic history pictures, including many for the palace of Versailles. He died in Paris in 1856.

Q5337451.bio: Edgar Samuel Paxson was an American painter born in 1852. He moved to Montana as a young man, worked as a scout and mailman, and painted detailed pictures of the Western frontier, especially of the Battle of the Little Bighorn. He died in Missoula in 1919.

Q1387579.bio: Otto Sinding was a Norwegian painter born in Kongsberg in 1842, who studied in Munich. He painted dramatic mountain landscapes and scenes of folk life. He lived in Munich and in Norway. He died in 1909.

Q186202.bio: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was born in Venice and became the greatest Italian painter of the 1700s. He painted huge, airy ceilings full of angels, gods and clouds in churches and palaces in Italy, Germany and Spain. His light, bright colors defined the last great age of Venetian painting. He died in Madrid in 1770.

Q334001.bio: Thomas Cole was born in England and moved to the United States as a teenager, settling near the Hudson River in New York. He founded the Hudson River School, a group of artists who painted America's wild landscapes. His paintings often carried messages about nature and civilization. He died in Catskill, New York, in 1848.

Q265665.bio: Pierre Auguste Cot was born in the south of France and became a popular painter in Paris. He studied with Bouguereau and painted romantic and mythological subjects. His paintings were very popular in America. He died in 1883.

Q547055.bio: Carl Bloch was born in Copenhagen, Denmark, and became one of the country's most beloved painters of history and religious scenes. He spent years studying in Italy. His pictures of Bible stories are reproduced all over the world. He died in Copenhagen in 1890.

x-currier-and-ives.bio: Currier and Ives was a famous American printmaking firm based in New York, founded by Nathaniel Currier and James Ives, which published cheap hand-colored lithographs from 1857 to 1907. They sold millions of prints of news events, landscapes and everyday life.

Q347220.bio: Fujishima Takeji was born in Kagoshima, Japan, and became one of the first Japanese painters to master Western oil painting. He studied in Paris and Rome. He later taught art in Tokyo. He died in Tokyo in 1943.

Q164961.bio: Adolph von Menzel was born in Breslau (now Wrocław, Poland) and lived most of his life in Berlin. He was Germany's greatest realist painter and an amazing draftsman. He painted history scenes, factories and daily life. He was a very short man who worked until his death in 1905.

Q1700176.bio: John Gast was a painter and lithographer born in Berlin, Germany, who worked in Brooklyn, New York. He is known for his 1872 painting 'American Progress', which became a symbol of westward expansion. He died in Brooklyn in 1896.

Q215100.bio: Mikhail Vrubel was born in Omsk, Siberia, and studied in Saint Petersburg. He lived in Russia and Ukraine, creating glittering, mosaic-like paintings and designs for theaters. He is best known for paintings of the Demon, a moody figure from a Russian poem. He lost his sight in later life and died in Saint Petersburg in 1910.

Q5599.bio: Peter Paul Rubens was born in Siegen, Germany, in 1577 and grew up in Antwerp, which became his home. He was the most famous Baroque painter of northern Europe, ran a huge workshop, and also worked as a diplomat for Spain. He died in Antwerp in 1640.

Q324288.bio: Jan van Huchtenburgh was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1646. He specialized in battle scenes and made paintings for Prince Eugene of Savoy and King William III. He lived in Amsterdam and died there in 1733.

Q2335336.bio: Charles Édouard Armand-Dumaresq was a French painter born in Paris in 1826. He painted military subjects and the French army, including scenes of the Franco-Prussian War. He lived and worked in Paris and died there in 1895.

Q120993.bio: Amedeo Modigliani was born in Livorno, Italy, and moved to Paris in 1906. He painted and sculpted people with long necks, almond-shaped eyes, and elegant simplified faces. He was poor and ill throughout his short life and died in Paris at 35. Only after his death did his fame explode. Modigliani was born into a Sephardic Jewish family in Italy and was proud of his heritage all his life.

Q5669.bio: Sandro Botticelli was an Italian painter born in Florence in 1445. He worked for the Medici family and painted graceful, flowing pictures such as The Birth of Venus and Primavera. He lived in Florence all his life and died there in 1510.

Q214074.bio: Claude Lorrain was a French painter born in Chamagne in 1600. He moved to Rome as a young man and spent his life there painting glowing landscapes and harbors in golden light, which influenced painters for centuries, including Turner. He died in Rome in 1682.

Q253446.bio: Anna Ancher was born in Skagen, Denmark, the daughter of an innkeeper. She became one of the greatest painters of the Skagen artists' colony, known for her use of light, and for her portraits and interiors. She married the painter Michael Ancher and lived her whole life in Skagen. She died there in 1935.

Q173223.bio: Mary Cassatt was born near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and moved to Paris as a young woman. She was the only American to join the French Impressionists, and she specialized in tender pictures of mothers and children. She lived in France most of her life, and she also encouraged American collectors to buy Impressionist art. She died at her country home in France in 1926.

Q2938914.bio: Carl Frederik von Breda was a Swedish painter born in Stockholm in 1759. He spent nine years in England, where he painted portraits, including one of the antislavery campaigner Thomas Clarkson, and later became court painter in Sweden. He died in Stockholm in 1818.

Q2573180.bio: George Henry Boughton was a painter born in Norwich, England, in 1833, who was brought up in Albany, New York, and then lived in London. He painted gentle scenes of the Pilgrims and of early America and became a member of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1905.

Q1284465.bio: Charles Conder was born in England and raised in Australia. He became a member of the Heidelberg School at a young age. He later moved to Paris and London and painted silk fans and delicate landscapes. He died in London in 1909.

Q2272816.bio: Peder Balke was born on an island in Norway and became a painter who started out as a house painter. He traveled to Norway's far north and painted bold, simple pictures of the sea and mountains. His work went unnoticed in his lifetime but is admired today. He died in Christiania (Oslo) in 1887.

x-peter-of-eboli.bio: Peter of Eboli was an Italian poet who lived in the south of Italy and Sicily around 1196. He wrote a long poem about the emperor Henry VI and illustrated it with lively colored drawings, including scenes of the capture and ransom of Richard the Lionheart.

Q466639.bio: Olga Boznańska was born in Kraków, Poland, and studied in Munich and Paris, where she lived for much of her life. She became one of the most important Polish painters, with a soft, gray-toned style, and she painted many portraits. She was widely admired in Paris. She died there in 1940.

Q1374436.bio: Henry Ossawa Tanner was an African American painter born in Pittsburgh in 1859. He moved to Paris in 1891, became famous for his quiet religious paintings and was the first Black artist to win wide international fame. He died in Paris in 1937.

Q938058.bio: Jean Germain Drouais was a French painter born in Paris in 1763. He was a favorite pupil of Jacques-Louis David, won the Prix de Rome at 21, and became one of the most promising artists of his generation, but he died of smallpox in Rome in 1788 at the age of 24.

Q260166.bio: Marc-Aurèle de Foy Suzor-Coté was born in Arthabaska, Quebec, and studied in Paris. He painted both traditional pictures and bright landscapes of the snowy Quebec countryside. He also made sculptures. He died in Florida in 1937.

Q1627994.bio: Horatio Walker was born in Listowel, Ontario, and became a famous painter of rural Quebec. He lived much of the year on Île d'Orléans near Quebec City and painted farmers and animals in a soft, glowing light. His paintings sold well in the United States. He died in Quebec in 1938.

x-kurz-and-allison.bio: Kurz and Allison was an American printing firm in Chicago that made colorful lithographs of famous battles and historical scenes in the 1880s and 1890s. Their prints brought the Civil War into many homes.

Q604107.bio: Wilhelm von Kaulbach was a German painter born in Arolsen in 1805. He worked in Munich, where he became head of the art academy and painted huge murals of history and legend for the king of Bavaria. He died in Munich in 1874.

Q983492.bio: Mårten Eskil Winge was born in Stockholm and became a leading Swedish history painter. He studied in Düsseldorf and Paris and painted subjects from Norse mythology. He died in Enköping in 1896.

Q3127237.bio: Harada Naojirō was born in Edo (now Tokyo) and studied painting in Germany. He was one of the first Japanese artists to learn Western oil painting abroad, and he painted some of Japan's early oil paintings. He died in 1899.

Q380706.bio: Vilhelm Hammershøi was born in Copenhagen and became famous for his quiet, gray pictures of empty rooms and of his wife Ida. His soft colors and calm mood are unforgettable. He lived and worked in Copenhagen all his life. He died in 1916.

Q1391078.bio: John Frederick Lewis was an English painter born in London in 1805. He traveled to Spain and the Middle East, lived in Cairo from 1841 to 1851, and became famous for detailed scenes of Eastern life. He died in Walton-on-Thames in 1876.

Q97603495.bio: Henry Brueckner was a painter who worked in the United States in the 1800s. He painted historical scenes, such as the marriage of Pocahontas, for patrons in the New World.

Q274909.bio: Émile Bayard was a French painter and illustrator born in La Ferté-sous-Jouarre in 1837. He is best known for illustrating books such as Les Misérables, including the famous drawing of the young Cosette with her broom. He died in Cairo, Egypt, in 1891.

Q1383289.bio: John de Critz was a painter born in Antwerp around 1551 who moved to London as a boy. He became Serjeant-Painter to King James I, painting portraits and decorating royal buildings. He lived in London until he died in 1642.

Q652305.bio: Johann Moritz Rugendas was a German painter born in Augsburg in 1802. He traveled and lived in Brazil, Mexico and Chile, producing many sketches of landscapes, daily life and the lives of enslaved people. He died in Weilheim an der Teck in 1858.

Q241732.bio: Rosa Bonheur was born in Bordeaux, France, and grew up in Paris, where she studied animals at farms and markets. She became one of the most famous women artists of the 1800s, painting horses, cattle and sheep. She even got official permission to wear trousers in public so she could work. She died at her château in Thomery, near Paris, in 1899.

Q4583808.bio: Carl Sundt-Hansen was born in Stavanger, Norway, in 1841, and spent much of his life in Denmark. He painted scenes of Norwegian and Danish peasant life. He died in Stavanger in 1907.

Q5541159.bio: George Jones was an English painter born in London in 1786. He served in the army and then painted battle scenes and historical subjects, becoming a member and later the Keeper of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1869.

Q594345.bio: Samuel Hirszenberg was born in Łódź, Poland, to a Jewish family and studied in Kraków, Munich and Paris. His large paintings show the suffering and hopes of Jewish people in Eastern Europe. In 1907 he moved to Jerusalem to teach at the new Bezalel art school. He died there the next year.

Q601609.bio: Antonio Ciseri was born in Switzerland to Italian parents and worked in Florence. He painted religious subjects and portraits with great realism. His 'Ecce Homo' is his best-known work. He died in Florence in 1891.

Q3101368.bio: George Agnew Reid was born in Ontario and trained in Philadelphia and Paris. He was a leading Toronto painter, a teacher, and the president of the Ontario College of Art. During World War I he painted Canadian factory workers and street scenes. He died in 1947.

Q334200.bio: Christian Krohg was born near Christiania (now Oslo) and was a painter, writer and a leader of the Realist movement in Norway. He studied in Germany and France and painted fishermen, poor people and the sea. He supported social change and caused controversy with his novel and paintings. He died in Oslo in 1925.

Q702700.bio: Joseph-Nicolas Robert-Fleury was a French painter born in Cologne in 1797. He worked in Paris, painted scenes from history and the Reformation, and served as director of the French Academy in Rome. He died in Paris in 1890.

Q4562720.bio: Gustav Lærum was a Norwegian painter born in 1870, who painted portraits and landscapes. He studied in Norway and Paris. He worked in Oslo. He died in 1938.

Q548914.bio: Philipp Veit was born in Berlin and became a painter in the Nazarene movement, a group who admired the art of medieval and Renaissance Germany and Italy. He lived in Rome, Frankfurt and Mainz. He was also a museum director. He died in Mainz in 1877.

Q359506.bio: Mark Gertler was born in London to Jewish immigrants from Poland and grew up in the poor neighborhood of Spitalfields. He studied at the Slade School of Art and became a friend of many writers and artists of his time. He is best known for his bold, rounded paintings, such as 'Merry-Go-Round'. He died in London in 1939.

Q728712.bio: Mór Than was a Hungarian painter born in 1828 in Bečej, then part of Hungary. He studied in Vienna, joined the Hungarian national cause of 1848 and later painted many scenes of Hungarian history. He died in Trieste in 1899.

Q436726.bio: Ary Scheffer was a French painter born in Dordrecht in the Netherlands in 1795. He moved to Paris as a young man and became a popular Romantic painter of literary and religious scenes, also teaching drawing to the royal family. He died in Argenteuil in 1858.

Q2048640.bio: Alonzo Chappel was an American painter and engraver born in New York City in 1828. He made hundreds of portraits and historical scenes of American history for books and prints. He lived and worked in New York and died in 1887.

Q983949.bio: Józef Chełmoński was born in a village in Poland and became one of the country's most beloved painters. He studied in Warsaw and Munich and lived in Paris for some years. He painted the Polish countryside, wide skies, horses and birds. He died in 1914.

Q325835.bio: Frederick Arthur Verner was born in Ontario and became famous for paintings of the Canadian plains, with buffalo and Indigenous camps at sunset. He spent his later years in England, where he continued to paint Canadian scenes. He died in London in 1928.

x-anonymous-illuminator-st-albans-chroni.bio: This picture of the Battle of Agincourt comes from the St Albans Chronicle, an English history written by the monk Thomas Walsingham. The illustrator is not known, but the manuscript was made soon after the events it shows, in the early 1420s.

Q939197.bio: Rik Wouters was a Belgian painter and sculptor born in 1882 in Mechelen. He painted his wife Nel in bright, happy colors. He died young, in Amsterdam, at 33, in 1916, after fleeing the war.

Q211763.bio: William Holman Hunt was born in London and, with Millais and Rossetti, founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood in 1848. He traveled to the Middle East to paint biblical scenes with realistic backgrounds. His most famous painting is 'The Light of the World'. He died in London in 1910.

Q1498652.bio: Solomon Alexander Hart was born in Plymouth, England, to a Jewish family and trained in London. In 1840 he became the first Jewish member of the Royal Academy. He painted history scenes, portraits and pictures of Jewish life. He died in London in 1881.

Q207447.bio: Jean-Baptiste-Siméon Chardin was born in Paris, the son of a cabinet-maker. He became one of the greatest painters of still lifes and quiet scenes of everyday life in 1700s France. He worked slowly and carefully with a soft touch. He spent his entire life in Paris.

Q5660541.bio: Agustín Arrieta was born in Chiautempan and worked in Puebla, Mexico. He painted still lifes and kitchen scenes with great skill, as well as portraits. His paintings show details of everyday Mexican life. He died in 1874.

Q94297287.bio: Jacques Bertaux was a French painter born in Harcy in the 1740s. He worked in Paris, and is best remembered for a vivid painting of the storming of the Tuileries Palace on August 10, 1792, which he made while the events were fresh.

Q206697.bio: Santi di Tito was an Italian painter born in Sansepolcro in 1536 who lived in Florence. He painted clear, natural religious scenes and portraits, including the best-known portrait of Niccolò Machiavelli. He died in Florence in 1603.

Q15407085.bio: Louis Bombled was a French painter and illustrator born in Chantilly in 1862. He specialized in military subjects and painted battle scenes for books and magazines. He died in Pierrefonds in 1927.

Q18125545.bio: Hervey Smythe was a British army officer born in 1734. He served under General Wolfe at Quebec in 1759 and made drawings of the campaign, then served as an adviser on military matters. He died in 1811.

Q251967.bio: Ángel Zárraga was born in Durango, Mexico, and lived in Paris for many years. He mixed Mexican themes with the modern styles of Europe, including Cubism. He painted large murals as well as portraits. He died in Mexico in 1946.

Q2059687.bio: Paul Fürst was a German engraver and publisher born in Nuremberg in 1608. He made popular prints, including the famous image of a plague doctor in a beaked mask, and lived in Nuremberg until he died in 1666.

Q780102.bio: Wyndham Lewis was a painter and writer, born in 1882 on a yacht off the coast of Nova Scotia. He lived mostly in London, where he led Vorticism, a British avant-garde movement, and served as an artillery officer and official war artist in World War I. He died in London in 1957.

Q3286980.bio: Robert Gibb was a Scottish painter born in Edinburgh in 1845. He painted battles and military scenes, became the Painter and Limner to the Queen in Scotland and was Keeper of the National Gallery of Scotland. He died in Edinburgh in 1932.

Q168659.bio: Franz Xaver Winterhalter was born in a small village in Germany's Black Forest and became one of the most famous painters of royalty in Europe. He worked for Queen Victoria, Napoleon III and many royal courts in Paris, London and Germany. His portraits show glittering silks and graceful poses. He died in Frankfurt in 1873.

Q28470603.bio: Zacharie Vincent was a Huron-Wendat painter from Wendake, near Quebec City. He is considered the first Indigenous painter in Quebec, and he often signed his portraits 'Zacharie Vincent Telariolin, the last of the Hurons'. He painted himself and his family in traditional dress. He died in 1886.

Q346808.bio: Gerard ter Borch was a Dutch painter born in Zwolle in 1617. He traveled widely, including to Münster where he painted the signing of the treaty of 1648, and was famous for quiet indoor scenes with beautifully painted satin dresses. He lived in Deventer and died there in 1681.

Q9011444.bio: Jennie Augusta Brownscombe was an American painter born in Honesdale, Pennsylvania, in 1850. She became famous for her warm pictures of American history, especially the Pilgrims and Thanksgiving, and she lived and worked in New York. She died in Queens in 1936.

Q1534936.bio: Josse Lieferinxe was a painter from the town of Enghien in what is now Belgium who worked in Marseille in southern France between about 1493 and 1508. He painted scenes of the life of Saint Sebastian, who was prayed to during the plague, and little else is known of his life.

Q1674765.bio: Issachar Ber Ryback was born in Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire, to a Jewish family. He studied art in Kyiv and was part of a group that tried to create a modern Jewish art. In 1926 he moved to Paris, where he stayed until his death in 1935. He painted and drew Jewish village life.

Q2711324.bio: Alejo Fernández was a Spanish painter born in Córdoba around 1470 who worked mostly in Seville. He painted altarpieces in a style that mixed Gothic and Renaissance, including a famous picture of the Virgin of the Navigators. He died in Seville in 1545.

Q43136084.bio: Richard Rummell was an English-born American painter, born in 1848. He painted watercolor views of American college campuses and other buildings, and lived and worked in New York. He died in 1924.

Q18325079.bio: Léon Sabatier was a French painter and lithographer born in Paris in 1800. He traveled widely, made views of cities and landscapes and recorded the burning of Paris in 1871. He died in Paris in 1887.

Q215305.bio: Giulio Romano was an Italian painter and architect born in Rome in 1499. He was Raphael's best pupil and finished many of his works after Raphael's death, then moved to Mantua, where he designed the colorful Palazzo Te. He died in Mantua in 1546.

Q148475.bio: Jean-Baptiste Camille Corot was born in Paris and spent much of his life painting the French countryside and trips to Italy. His silvery, misty landscapes influenced Impressionist painters such as Monet and Pissarro. He was known as a kind and generous man. He died in Paris in 1875.

Q344838.bio: Winslow Homer was born in Boston and became one of America's greatest painters. He started as an illustrator and covered the Civil War for a magazine. Later, he lived on the rocky coast of Maine, where he painted the sea, fishermen and storms. He died at his home at Prouts Neck in 1910.

Q1291901.bio: Tom Roberts was born in England and moved to Australia as a teenager. He was one of the leaders of the Heidelberg School, and he painted some of the most famous pictures of Australian life, including 'Shearing the Rams'. He died in 1931.

Q527191.bio: Laura Muntz Lyall was born in England and raised in Canada. She studied in Toronto and in Paris and became known for gentle, soft pictures of mothers and children. She was one of the leading women painters of her time. She died in Toronto in 1930.

Q167132.bio: George Bellows was born in Columbus, Ohio, and moved to New York City, where he became a leading painter of city life. He painted boxing matches, tenements and the construction of Penn Station. He died young, in 1925, at 42.

Q21995307.bio: Sidney Simon was an American painter and sculptor born in Pittsburgh in 1917. He was a combat artist for the US Army in World War II and painted the Japanese surrender in Tokyo Bay. He died in 1997.

Q534279.bio: Ogata Kenzan was born in Kyoto and was a famous potter and painter. He was the younger brother of the painter Ogata Kōrin, and together they made some of the most beautiful objects of their time. He decorated ceramics with simple, beautiful designs. He died in Edo (Tokyo) in 1743.

Q158840.bio: James Ensor was born in Ostend, Belgium, and lived there nearly his whole life. He painted bizarre carnival masks, skeletons, and crowds in bright, shocking colors. His strange work was ahead of its time, and he became a hero for modern artists. He died in Ostend in 1949.

Q548205.bio: Hubert Robert was a French painter born in Paris in 1733. He spent years in Italy and became known as 'Robert of the Ruins' for his pictures of crumbling Roman monuments, and he later served as a keeper of the Louvre. He was imprisoned for a time during the French Revolution and died in Paris in 1808.

Q2576609.bio: Ludvig Karsten was a Norwegian painter born in Christiania in 1876. He lived a free, bohemian life, traveling in Europe and painting in bold, bright colors. He died in Paris in 1926.

Q1470796.bio: Frederick Sandys was born in Norwich, England, and became a painter and illustrator associated with the Pre-Raphaelites. He was famous for detailed portraits of beautiful women. He lived in London, and he died there in 1904.

Q169311.bio: Johann Friedrich Overbeck was born in Lübeck, Germany, and moved to Rome, where he led the Nazarenes, a group of artists inspired by medieval and early Renaissance painting. He lived in a former monastery with his friends. He stayed in Rome the rest of his life and died there in 1869.

Q207929.bio: Jacopo Pontormo was an Italian painter born in the village of Pontorme near Empoli in 1494. He worked in Florence for the Medici and became a leading Mannerist, known for his elegant, twisting figures and bright, unusual colors. He died in Florence in 1557.

Q250194.bio: Anselm Feuerbach was a German painter born in Speyer in 1829. He studied in Düsseldorf, Munich and Paris and lived for many years in Italy, where he painted calm scenes from classical antiquity. He died in Venice in 1880.

Q2856626.bio: Antoine Plamondon was born near Quebec City and studied painting in Paris in the 1830s. He became one of the most important portrait painters in Quebec, painting priests, nuns and political leaders. He taught many younger artists. He died in 1895.

Q7422343.bio: Sarah Goodridge was born in Templeton, Massachusetts, and taught herself to paint miniature portraits. She worked in Boston, where she was a well-known painter of tiny portraits on ivory. She painted the great statesmen of her day, including Daniel Webster and Gilbert Stuart. She never married and ran her own successful art business.

Q3514329.bio: Takeuchi Seihō was born in Kyoto and became one of the leading painters of Japan in the early 1900s. He studied Western painting during trips to Europe and mixed it with Japanese styles. He is known for animals, such as his famous 'Tabby Cat'. He died in 1942.

Q821537.bio: Karl Friedrich Lessing was a German painter born in Breslau in 1808. He worked in Düsseldorf, where he painted dramatic scenes from the Reformation and medieval history, and later directed the art gallery in Karlsruhe. He died in Karlsruhe in 1880.

Q172911.bio: Ilya Repin was born in a small town in Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire. He trained in Saint Petersburg and traveled to Paris before becoming Russia's most celebrated realist painter. He lived much of his later life in a country house near the Finnish border, now a museum. His huge paintings of people, history, and ordinary life made him a national treasure.

Q17325127.n: Master of the Battle of Anghiari
Q17325127.bio: The Master of the Battle of Anghiari is the name given to an unknown Italian painter active in Florence around 1470. He is named after a painted chest panel of the Battle of Anghiari, and made colorful painted wooden chests that were given at weddings.

x-english-school.bio: This painting was made by an unknown English artist around 1590. Many paintings of the Armada were made soon after the battle, and the painters of these often did not sign their works.

Q203643.bio: James McNeill Whistler was born in Lowell, Massachusetts, in the United States, and spent his childhood partly in Russia. He moved to Europe as a young man and lived in Paris and London, where he became one of the most famous (and sharp-tongued) artists in the world. He titled paintings like pieces of music, such as 'Nocturne' and 'Arrangement.' He died in London in 1903.

Q296.bio: Claude Monet was born in Paris but grew up on the coast of Normandy, where he learned to paint outdoors. He was a leader of Impressionism, and he lived in places like Argenteuil and, for his last 43 years, Giverny, where he built a famous garden with a pond of water lilies. He painted the same scenes again and again at different times of day to capture changing light. He kept painting until he was 86, even as his eyesight faded.

Q556681.bio: Dmitry Levitzky was a Russian painter born in Kyiv in 1735. He became the leading portrait painter in Saint Petersburg during the reign of Catherine the Great, painting nobles and thinkers, including Diderot. He died in Saint Petersburg in 1822.

Q3588762.bio: Émile Signol was a French painter born in Paris in 1804. He won the Prix de Rome in 1830 and painted large religious and historical pictures, including some for the palace of Versailles. He died in Enghien-les-Bains in 1892.

Q41406.bio: Edvard Munch was born in Norway and grew up in Christiania (now Oslo), in a family troubled by illness and loss. He traveled in Europe, especially Germany and France, and used paint to express anxiety, love and loneliness. His most famous work, 'The Scream', is among the best-known images ever. He spent his last decades at his estate Ekely near Oslo and died in 1944.

Q275018.bio: Uemura Shōen was born in Kyoto, and became one of Japan's greatest women painters. She was best known for beautiful pictures of women in traditional style. She was the first woman to receive the Order of Culture, Japan's high honor, in 1948. She died in 1949.

Q13489405.bio: Andrew Carrick Gow was an English painter born in London in 1848. He painted battles and scenes from English history and became a member and later Keeper of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1920.

Q965809.bio: Frederick McCubbin was born in Melbourne and became a leading painter of the Heidelberg School. He painted the Australian bush and the pioneers with great feeling. He taught at the National Gallery school. He died in Melbourne in 1917.

Q2695615.bio: Thorolf Holmboe was a Norwegian painter born in 1866 who painted landscapes and winter scenes. He studied in Norway and in Paris. He lived most of his life in and around Christiania (now Oslo). He died in 1935.

x-joseph-gary-sheahan.bio: Joseph Gary Sheahan was an American combat artist who painted watercolors of the US Army during World War II, including a view of Utah Beach in Normandy in 1944.

Q455133.bio: George Catlin was born in Pennsylvania and trained as a lawyer before becoming a painter. In the 1830s he traveled across the American West to paint portraits of Native Americans and their lives. He hoped to preserve a record of cultures he feared would disappear. He died in New Jersey in 1872.

Q18575166.bio: Martin Borgord was born in Gausdal, Norway, in 1869, and became a painter of history and portraits. He studied in Germany and spent time in the United States. He died in 1935.

Q434575.bio: Arthur Hughes was born in London and was an English painter linked to the Pre-Raphaelites. He is best known for glowing, romantic scenes of young lovers and medieval stories. He worked in London and in the countryside, and he also illustrated children's books. He died in 1915.

x-stephen-h-randall.bio: Stephen H. Randall was an American artist who served as a combat artist with the US Army's Vietnam combat art team in 1968. His watercolors of helicopters, soldiers and daily life are in the US Army art collection.

Q323498.bio: Friedrich Georg Weitsch was a German painter born in Brunswick in 1758. He worked in Berlin as a painter for the Prussian court and painted many portraits, including one of the scientist Alexander von Humboldt. He died in Berlin in 1828.

Q380494.bio: Charles Demuth was born in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, and studied art in Philadelphia and Paris. He was a leading American modernist known for crisp, precise paintings of buildings and factories. He lived with diabetes for most of his adult life. He died in Lancaster in 1935.

Q192720.bio: Thomas Gainsborough was born in Sudbury, a small town in England, and moved to London as a teenager to study art. He became one of Britain's most fashionable portrait painters, working in Bath and London. He secretly preferred painting landscapes, and he loved music. His elegant, feathery brushstrokes made his sitters seem alive.

Q214062.bio: Joseph Wright of Derby was born in Derby, England, and spent nearly his whole life there. He was famous for painting scenes lit by a single candle or lamp, often showing scientific experiments. His friends included inventors and scientists of the Industrial Revolution. He's often called the first painter to capture the spirit of the Age of Science.

Q3174641.bio: Jean-Simon Berthélemy was a French painter born in Laon in 1743. He worked in Paris, where he painted large history pictures for the royal court and, later, for the Revolution and Napoleon. He died in Paris in 1811.

Q163543.bio: François Gérard was a French painter born in Rome in 1770. He studied under Jacques-Louis David, became a favorite portrait painter of Napoleon's court, and was later made a baron. He lived in Paris and died there in 1837.

Q134741.bio: Camille Pissarro was born on the island of St. Thomas in the Caribbean and moved to France as a teen. He was the oldest of the Impressionists and a father figure and teacher to many younger painters, including Cézanne. He painted farms, villages and city streets in France. He died in Paris in 1903. Pissarro came from a Sephardic Jewish family, and his background shaped his lifelong sympathy for ordinary working people.

Q561916.bio: Henry Raeburn was born in Stockbridge, near Edinburgh, Scotland, and became Scotland's best-known portrait painter. He painted writers, lawyers and clan chiefs with a lively, confident brush. He was knighted in 1822. He lived and worked in Edinburgh until his death in 1823.

Q2975556.bio: Clarence Gagnon was born in Montreal and studied in Paris. He is best known for his bright, colorful paintings of Quebec villages in winter, and also for illustrating the novel 'Maria Chapdelaine'. He lived part of his life in France and part in Quebec. He died in Montreal in 1942.

Q2834961.bio: Alfred Bastien was a Belgian painter born in 1873. He painted huge panoramas, then during World War I he was a war artist for the Canadian War Memorials, making large paintings of the front at Passchendaele. He lived in Brussels and died in Uccle in 1955.

Q41513.bio: William Blake was born in London and lived there nearly his entire life. He was a poet, painter and printmaker who claimed to see angels and visions, and he created magical books mixing words and pictures. Few people understood him while he lived, and he was poor. Today he's honored as one of the greatest imaginations in British art and literature.

Q260135.bio: Édouard Castres was a Swiss painter born in Geneva in 1838. He volunteered as a Red Cross helper in the Franco-Prussian War and later painted the huge panorama of the Bourbaki army's retreat into Switzerland. He died in Annemasse, France, in 1902.

Q2837691.bio: Aaron Allan Edson was born in Quebec and became a Canadian landscape painter who painted the forests and mountains of the east. He lived in Montreal and worked in Quebec and New England. His quiet, glowing landscapes were very popular. He died in 1888.

Q46373.bio: Edgar Degas was born in Paris to a well-to-do family and lived there almost all his life. He's linked to the Impressionists, but preferred to work indoors, painting ballet dancers, racehorses, and women at their daily routines. He loved to catch unusual angles, as if a camera had snapped the scene. In old age his eyesight failed and he turned to sculpture.

Q773855.bio: Alfred Stevens was born in Brussels and settled in Paris, where he became a leading painter of elegant women in fashionable rooms. He was a friend of Manet and Degas. He died in Paris in 1906.

Q458671.bio: Giuseppe Castiglione was born in Milan, Italy, and became a Jesuit brother, traveling as a missionary to China. He took the name Lang Shining and served as a court painter for three Chinese emperors. He blended European realism with Chinese styles. He died in Beijing in 1766.

Q17169.bio: Giovanni Bellini was a Venetian painter, born in Venice around 1430 into a family of painters. He was the teacher of Giorgione and Titian and led Venetian painting into the High Renaissance with his glowing colors and quiet, thoughtful Madonnas. He worked in Venice all his life and died there in 1516.

Q14198216.bio: Philippe de Mazerolles was an illuminator who worked in Bruges in the 1400s, painting books for Burgundian nobles. He was admired for his lively pictures in chronicles and books of hours.

Q553258.bio: Francisco Pradilla y Ortiz was born in a small village in Aragón, Spain, and trained in Madrid and Rome. He became famous for large history paintings of kings and queens. He served as director of the Prado Museum. He died in Madrid in 1921.

Q180932.bio: François Boucher was born in Paris and became the favorite painter of Madame de Pompadour, the French king's companion. He lived in Paris and was the leading figure in the Rococo style, with its pastel colors and playful, romantic scenes. He painted, designed tapestries and decorated palaces. He died in Paris in 1770.

Q4974655.bio: Sofie Ribbing was born in Sweden and became a painter and teacher who lived in Sweden, Denmark, and Norway. She studied in Copenhagen and was known for scenes of children and family life. She was one of the notable Scandinavian women painters of her era. She died in 1894.

Q33477.bio: Eugène Delacroix was born near Paris and became the leading painter of the Romantic movement in France. He lived mostly in Paris, but a trip to Morocco in 1832 filled his sketchbooks with bright colors and scenes that inspired him for life. He believed color and emotion mattered more than perfect outlines. Later artists like Monet and Van Gogh studied his work closely.

Q149571.bio: Carl Blechen was a German painter born in Cottbus in 1798. He lived in Berlin, traveled to Italy, and painted romantic landscapes and some of the earliest pictures of factories and industry in German art. He died in Berlin in 1840.

x-british-school.bio: This painting is by an unknown English artist working in the 1540s. Many English paintings of the time were made by artists whose names have not survived, and later experts label them with the name 'British School' or 'English School'.

Q2370524.bio: Vasily Timm was a Russian painter and illustrator born in Riga in 1820. He worked in Saint Petersburg, painted historical scenes and published an illustrated magazine, and later lived in Germany. He died in Berlin in 1895.

Q1278282.bio: Eastman Johnson was an American painter born in Lovell, Maine, in 1824. He studied in Düsseldorf and The Hague, lived in New York and painted warm scenes of American life, including pictures related to the Civil War. He died in New York City in 1906.

Q372277.bio: Alexey Bogolyubov was a Russian painter born in 1824 in the Novgorod region. He painted seas and ships, served as a painter for the Russian navy, and lived for many years in Paris, where he died in 1896.

Q212499.bio: Jean-Léon Gérôme was born in Vesoul, France, and became one of the most successful painters and teachers in Paris. He traveled to Egypt and the Middle East and painted lively scenes from ancient and modern life. He was also a sculptor. His students came from around the world.

Q2286906.bio: Joseph-Siffred Duplessis was a French painter born in Carpentras in 1725. He became one of the best portrait painters in Paris, painting Louis XVI and the American Benjamin Franklin, and he was the curator of the royal paintings at Versailles. He died there in 1802.

Q1550144.bio: Thomas Jones Barker was an English painter born in Bath in 1815. He painted Crimean War scenes and popular pictures of the British army, and lived in London, where he died in 1882.

Q381698.bio: John Michael Wright was a painter born in London in 1617, of Scottish descent. He lived in Rome as a young man and returned to England, where he painted portraits of King Charles II and his court. He died in London in 1694.

Q313275.bio: Boris Kustodiev was a Russian painter born in Astrakhan in 1878. He lived in Saint Petersburg and painted colorful scenes of Russian merchants and festivals, and after the revolution made pictures of it despite being paralyzed and working from a wheelchair. He died in 1927.

x-stepan-mukharsky.bio: Stepan Mukharsky was a Russian artist who made posters for the Soviet government during and after the Russian Civil War. His bright, cartoon-like posters were made to explain the revolution to people who could not read.

Q3187562.bio: Juan Antonio de Ribera was a Spanish painter born in Madrid in 1779. He studied in Paris under Jacques-Louis David and became a leading Neoclassical painter, later working for King Ferdinand VII of Spain. He died in Madrid in 1860.

Q1065418.bio: Charles Marion Russell was an American painter born in St. Louis in 1864. He moved to Montana as a teenager, worked as a cowboy and lived among the Blackfeet, then became the most famous painter of the Old West. He lived in Great Falls, where he died in 1926.

Q22583666.bio: Carl Kahler was born in Linz, Austria, and emigrated to the United States, where he worked in San Francisco. He painted landscapes, horses and animals. His giant painting of 42 cats made him famous, and he took three years to complete it. He died in 1906.

Q187506.bio: Honoré Daumier was born in Marseille, France, and grew up in Paris. He was famous for his satirical cartoons that poked fun at politicians, and he created thousands of prints. He also painted sympathetic pictures of working people. He lost his sight late in life and died in 1879.

Q18507975.bio: Carl Frithjof Smith was born in Christiania (Oslo) in 1859 and trained in Germany, where he lived in Weimar for much of his life. He painted quiet scenes of family life and portraits. He died in Weimar in 1917.

Q363308.bio: Walker Evans was an American photographer born in St. Louis in 1903. He photographed poor farm families for the government during the Depression, and his plain, honest style shaped documentary photography. He lived in New York and died in New Haven in 1975.

Q740396.bio: Václav Brožík was a Czech painter born in Trhová Kamenice in 1851. He studied in Prague, Dresden and Munich, and moved to Paris, where he painted big scenes from Czech and European history. He died in Paris in 1901.

Q673615.bio: Peter Snayers was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1592. He became the court painter to the Archduke in Brussels and was famous for his panoramic battle scenes, often showing real battles of the Thirty Years' War. He died in Brussels in 1667.

Q1398809.bio: Fausto Zonaro was an Italian painter born in Masi, near Padua, in 1854. He moved to Constantinople in 1891 and became court painter to the Ottoman sultan Abdul Hamid II, painting scenes of the city and its history. He returned to Italy and died in Sanremo in 1929.

Q353014.bio: Peter Nicolai Arbo was a Norwegian painter born in 1831 who studied in Düsseldorf and Munich. He painted Norse myth and Viking history, making them familiar to Norwegians. His 'Wild Hunt of Odin' is his most famous painting. He died in Christiania in 1892.

Q16228969.bio: Xu Yang was a court painter in China in the 1700s, born in Suzhou. He painted big, detailed scrolls recording life in the city and the Qianlong Emperor's travels. His pictures are treasured as history. He lived and worked in the Qing court.

Q9440.bio: Paolo Veronese was an Italian painter born in Verona in 1528. He moved to Venice, where he became famous for huge, colorful pictures of feasts and ceremonies full of costumes and architecture. He died in Venice in 1588.

x-nasa.bio: NASA, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, was created in 1958 and organized the American space program, including the Mercury, Gemini and Apollo missions. Its photographs, made by employees of the US government, belong to the public.

Q2833597.bio: Alexandre Desgoffe was born in Paris and trained as a landscape painter under Ingres's circle. He spent his career in Paris, where he became known for classical landscapes in the Italian style. He exhibited for decades and received several honors. He died in Paris in 1882.

Q369263.bio: John Trumbull was born in Lebanon, Connecticut, and served as an officer in the American Revolution. Afterwards he studied painting in London with Benjamin West. He is best known for paintings of key events in the Revolution, such as the signing of the Declaration of Independence. He died in New York City in 1843.

x-nasa-photograph-by-william-anders.bio: William Anders, born in Hong Kong in 1933, was an American astronaut who flew on Apollo 8, the first mission to orbit the Moon, in December 1968. His photograph Earthrise, taken on that flight, became one of the most famous images of the 1900s. He died in 2024.

Q130777.bio: Kazimir Malevich was born near Kyiv, in what is now Ukraine, to a family of Polish origin. He lived in Moscow and Saint Petersburg and founded Suprematism, an art of pure shapes and colors. He also taught, wrote, and designed. After the Russian government turned against modern art, he was forced to return to simple realist styles before his death in 1935.

Q6308657.bio: Julien Binford was an American painter born in Powhatan County, Virginia, in 1908. He painted for the US Army Air Forces in World War II and later taught art at Mary Washington College in Fredericksburg, Virginia. He died in 1997.

Q323144.bio: Ambroise Louis Garneray was a French painter born in Paris in 1783. He went to sea as a boy, was a prisoner of the British during the Napoleonic wars, and later became a famous painter of ships and sea battles. He died in Paris in 1857.

Q33522534.bio: Alanson Fisher was an American portrait painter born in 1807. He lived mainly in New York, painting portraits of well-known people, including the author Harriet Beecher Stowe. He died in 1884.

Q691796.bio: Abanindranath Tagore was born in Kolkata (Calcutta), India, into a famous family that included the poet Rabindranath Tagore. He founded the Bengal School of art, which revived Indian painting styles. His work inspired the movement for India's independence. He died in Kolkata in 1951.

Q4027439.bio: Harald Slott-Møller was born in Denmark, near Copenhagen, and was a painter and designer. He is known for dreamy Symbolist pictures and portraits. He lived in Copenhagen and was married to the painter Agnes Slott-Møller. He died in 1937.

Q5598.bio: Rembrandt van Rijn was born in Leiden in 1606 and moved to Amsterdam in 1631, where he became the most famous painter in Holland. He painted portraits, Bible stories and over eighty self-portraits, and went bankrupt later in life. He died in Amsterdam in 1669.

Q203768.bio: Abdülmecid II was born in Istanbul in 1868 and was the last caliph of the Ottoman family. He was also a talented painter and music lover. After Turkey became a republic, he was forced into exile. He died in Paris in 1944.

Q3034741.bio: Domenico Induno was an Italian painter born in Milan in 1815, the older brother of Gerolamo Induno. He painted scenes of everyday life and portraits of Risorgimento heroes. He lived in Milan and died there in 1878.

Q446631.bio: Master Theodoric was a Bohemian painter active in Prague between about 1348 and 1381. He was the court painter of Emperor Charles IV and painted the holy figures for the walls of Karlštejn Castle, which are among the best-known paintings of medieval central Europe.

Q561205.bio: Raphael was an Italian painter born in Urbino in 1483. He worked in Florence and then in Rome, where he painted the Vatican's famous rooms, and with Leonardo and Michelangelo he is counted among the three giants of the High Renaissance. He died in Rome in 1520 at the age of only 37.

Q176694.bio: Antonis Mor was a Dutch painter born in Utrecht in about 1517. He became the court portrait painter to the Habsburgs and painted Philip II of Spain and Queen Mary I of England, working in Brussels, Madrid and London. He died in Antwerp in about 1577.

Q3325858.bio: Benedito Calixto was a Brazilian painter born in 1853 in Itanhaém, near São Paulo. He painted history, religious subjects and the coast. He was also an historian. He died in São Paulo in 1927.

Q156889.bio: Suzanne Valadon was born in a small town in France and moved to Paris as a girl. She worked as a circus performer and an artist's model for Renoir and Toulouse-Lautrec before teaching herself to paint. She became the first woman admitted to the French National Society of Fine Arts. She lived in Montmartre and died in Paris in 1938.

x-nasa-apollo-17-crew.bio: The Blue Marble was taken by the crew of Apollo 17, Eugene Cernan, Ronald Evans and Harrison Schmitt, on their way to the Moon in December 1972. It was the last Apollo flight to the Moon.

Q75527.bio: Heinrich Leutemann was a German painter and illustrator born near Leipzig in 1824. He was known for lively book illustrations of animals, travel and history, and lived in Leipzig and nearby Saxony. He died in 1905.

Q311398.bio: Jean Fouquet was a French painter born in Tours around 1420. He became the leading painter at the court of King Charles VII, painted portraits and illuminated manuscripts, and visited Italy, which influenced his style. He worked in Tours and died there around 1478.

Q454945.bio: Charles Willson Peale was born in Maryland and became one of the best-known American painters of the Revolution. He painted George Washington many times, fought in the war, and also founded a museum in Philadelphia. He lived in Philadelphia and died there in 1827.

Q3526663.bio: Théophile Hamel was born near Quebec City and studied in Europe in the 1840s. He became one of the most important portrait painters in Canada, painting political leaders and church figures. He lived in Quebec City. He died there in 1870.

Q39931.bio: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was born in Limoges, France, and started his working life painting designs on porcelain. In Paris he became a founding Impressionist, famous for glowing scenes of friends, dancing, and sunshine. Later in life he lived in the warm south of France, and he kept painting even when arthritis twisted his hands, with a brush strapped to his fingers. He left thousands of cheerful paintings.

x-attributed-to-robert-peake-the-elder.bio: Robert Peake the Elder was an English painter born around 1551 who worked in London. He was the Serjeant-Painter to King James I and painted portraits of the court, including the royal family, in a bright, detailed style. He died in London in 1619.

Q380704.bio: Bartholomeus van der Helst was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1613. He moved to Amsterdam, where he became one of the most successful portrait painters of his time, rivaling Rembrandt. He died in Amsterdam in 1670.

Q17790.bio: The Kangxi Emperor was the second Qing emperor of China, and he ruled for 61 years, from 1661 to 1722, longer than any other Chinese emperor. He was interested in science, art, poetry and calligraphy, and also painted himself. He lived in Beijing and the Imperial Summer Palace.

x-elizabeth-thompson-lady-butler.bio: Elizabeth Thompson, later Lady Butler, was a British painter born in Lausanne, Switzerland, in 1846. She became one of the most popular battle painters of Victorian Britain, starting with her Roll Call in 1874. She married a general, lived in Ireland, and died in 1933.

Q365544.bio: Adolph Tidemand was born in Mandal, Norway, and trained in Copenhagen and Düsseldorf.
