He lived much of his life in Germany and Norway, painting scenes of Norwegian farmers and folk traditions. He helped create the image of Norwegian national identity in the 1800s. He died in Christiania in 1876.

Q161145.bio: Horace Vernet was a French painter born in Paris in 1789. He painted many battles of Napoleon and the French army, and lived in Rome and Paris, where he died in 1863.

Q369776.bio: David Roberts was a Scottish painter born in Stockbridge, Edinburgh, in 1796. He started as a theater scene painter, traveled through Egypt and the Holy Land, and made famous views of ancient monuments. He lived in London and died there in 1864.

x-ferdinand-pauwels-attributed.bio: Ferdinand Pauwels was a Belgian painter born in Eeklo in 1830. He became a professor at the art academy in Dresden, Germany, and painted large scenes from the history of the Reformation. This picture is attributed to him, which means experts think but cannot prove that he painted it. He died in Dresden in 1904.

Q13604459.bio: José María Jara was a Mexican painter born in 1866 who studied at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. He painted scenes of Mexican life, with a special interest in customs and traditions. He died in 1939.

Q2880664.bio: Baldassare Verazzi was an Italian painter born in Caprezzo in 1819. He lived in Milan and painted historical pictures related to the Italian struggle for independence, including the Five Days of Milan. He died in Lesa in 1886.

Q718020.bio: Hans Heyerdahl was born in Norway, to a family of Norwegian-Swedish roots, and studied in Copenhagen, Munich and Paris. He painted portraits and religious paintings with a clear, quiet realism. He became one of the leading Norwegian painters of his generation. He died in Oslo in 1913.

Q538350.bio: Maarten van Heemskerck was a Dutch painter born in the village of Heemskerk in 1498. He lived in Haarlem but traveled to Rome from 1532 to 1536, where he drew the ancient ruins, and these drawings are now an important record of Renaissance Rome. He died in Haarlem in 1574.

Q5423992.bio: Felix Octavius Carr Darley was an American illustrator born in Philadelphia in 1822. He illustrated books by Washington Irving and Charles Dickens and made many pictures of the Civil War. He died in Claymont, Delaware, in 1888.

Q185850.bio: C. R. W. Nevinson was an English painter born in London in 1889. He painted the war in the dynamic style of Futurism and was an official war artist in World War I. He lived in London and died in Hampstead in 1946.

Q146691.bio: Alphonse Mucha was born in Ivančice, in what is now the Czech Republic. He moved to Paris and became world-famous for his elegant Art Nouveau posters. Later in his life he returned to Prague and painted a huge series of paintings called the Slav Epic. He died in 1939.

Q211356.bio: Isaac Levitan was born in Lithuania to a Jewish family and grew up in Moscow, where he studied painting. He became one of Russia's greatest landscape painters, known for his poetic scenes of rivers, forests and quiet villages. He often painted along the Volga River. He died in Moscow in 1900, at age 39. Levitan was born into a poor Jewish family in Lithuania, and he rose to become one of the most beloved painters in Russia.

Q525092.bio: Erik Werenskiold was born in Kongsvinger, Norway, and was one of the leading Norwegian painters of his generation. He is famous for his realistic scenes of Norwegian life and for illustrating Norwegian folk tales with Theodor Kittelsen. He also painted portraits of famous Norwegians. He died in Oslo in 1938.

Q142420.bio: Edmund Blair Leighton was born in London and became famous for painting romantic scenes from the Middle Ages and the Regency period. He studied at the Royal Academy and lived in London. His paintings of knights and ladies are widely reproduced. He died in 1922.

Q360724.bio: Stanhope Forbes was an Irish-born English painter born in Dublin in 1857. He settled in Newlyn in Cornwall, where he painted fishermen and villagers in the open air, and founded an art school. He died in Newlyn in 1947.

Q2757568.bio: Thomas Pollock Anshutz was a painter and teacher born in Kentucky and active in Philadelphia. He taught at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts, where his students included Robert Henri and Charles Demuth. He died in 1912.

Q1591928.bio: John Gilbert was an English painter and illustrator born in Blackheath in 1817. He became famous for drawings of Shakespeare's plays and for lively paintings of knights and battles, and he served as president of the Royal Watercolour Society. He died in London in 1897.

Q483992.bio: William-Adolphe Bouguereau was born in La Rochelle, on France's Atlantic coast, and studied in Paris and Rome. He became the most celebrated painter of the French Academy, famous for smooth, glowing figures from myths and everyday life. He taught thousands of students. When Impressionism rose, he fell from fashion, but his technical skill is again widely admired.

Q2534502.bio: Thomas Hill was an English-born American painter born in Birmingham in 1829. He grew up in Massachusetts and moved to California, where he painted huge landscapes of Yosemite and the Sierra Nevada. He died in Raymond, California, in 1908.

Q7300143.bio: Rea Irvin was an American artist born in San Francisco in 1881. He drew magazine covers and cartoons, and designed the first cover of The New Yorker in 1925, featuring the dandy Eustace Tilley. He lived in New York and died in the Virgin Islands in 1972.

Q18735046.bio: Thomas Falcon Marshall was an English painter born in Liverpool in 1818. He lived in London and painted historical and storytelling pictures, many of them about the English Civil War and Mary Queen of Scots. He died in Kensington in 1878.

Q3499926.bio: A. Y. Jackson was a Canadian painter born in Montreal in 1882. He was a founding member of the Group of Seven, an official war artist in World War I, and one of the painters who made rugged northern landscapes famous. He died in Kleinburg, Ontario, in 1974.

Q110228.bio: Vasily Surikov was born in Krasnoyarsk, in Siberia, and moved to Moscow and Saint Petersburg. He painted huge history scenes of Russia's past with crowds of vivid individuals. His paintings are among Russia's most loved. He died in Moscow in 1916.

Q1355256.bio: Eugène Lami was a French painter and lithographer born in Paris in 1800. He painted elegant scenes of the court and big battle pictures for King Louis-Philippe, and moved easily between fashion and war. He died in Paris in 1890.

Q214666.bio: Léon Bakst was born in Grodno, then part of the Russian Empire, to a Jewish family. He became a star of the Ballets Russes in Paris, designing the vivid costumes and sets that astonished audiences. He also painted portraits and illustrated books. He died in France in 1924.

Q5592.bio: Michelangelo was born in Caprese, Italy, in 1475 and worked in Florence and Rome. He was a sculptor, painter and architect who made the statue of David and painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel. He died in Rome in 1564, almost 89 years old.

Q2596759.bio: Kitty Kielland was born in Stavanger, Norway, and was one of the first Norwegian women to become a leading landscape painter. She lived in Germany and France for many years. Her atmospheric pictures of Norwegian summer light are admired today. She died in 1914.

Q1239404.bio: José Salomé Pina was a Mexican painter born in Mexico City in 1830. He studied at the Academy of San Carlos, where he later taught, and painted historical and portrait scenes. He died in Tacubaya, near Mexico City, in 1909.

Q15998924.bio: Nina Evans Allender was an American cartoonist born in Auburn, New York, in 1873. She was the official cartoonist of the National Woman's Party and drew hundreds of cartoons for the fight for women's right to vote. She lived in Washington, D.C., and died in Plainfield, New Jersey, in 1957.

Q2832922.bio: Alex Colville was a Canadian painter born in Toronto in 1920. He was an official Canadian war artist in World War II, painting the Netherlands and the liberation of Bergen-Belsen, and later became famous for calm, mysterious pictures. He lived in Nova Scotia and died in Wolfville in 2013.

x-bayeux-tapestry-embroiderers.bio: The Bayeux Tapestry was stitched in the 1070s, probably in England and perhaps ordered by Bishop Odo of Bayeux, William the Conqueror's half-brother. Its embroiderers are not known by name, though they were most likely skilled English needlewomen. It is about 70 meters long and now hangs in Bayeux, France.

Q2112365.bio: Jean Duplessis-Bertaux was a French engraver and painter born in Paris in 1747. He is known for his lively prints of the events of the French Revolution and the Napoleonic wars. He lived in Paris and died there in 1818.

x-grigory-shukaev.bio: Grigory Shukaev was a Russian painter of the 1800s who made a picture of the Siege of Sevastopol in 1856, soon after the end of the Crimean War. Not much is known about his life.

Q3370554.bio: Paul Balze was born in Rome to French parents and became a painter and student of Ingres. He lived and worked mostly in Paris, and was known for careful, classical work. He also copied works of the old masters. He died in Paris in 1884.

Q11478804.bio: Kawamura Kiyoo was a Japanese painter born in Edo in 1852. He studied Western-style painting in Italy and helped bring oil painting to Japan. He painted historical scenes and legends. He died in 1934.

Q7779204.bio: Thure de Thulstrup was a Swedish-born American illustrator born in Stockholm in 1848. He served in the French army, moved to the United States and became famous for his illustrations of battles of the Civil War. He died in New York City in 1930.

Q708498.bio: Gerolamo Induno was an Italian painter born in Milan in 1825. He fought for Italian independence in the 1840s and 1850s, joined Garibaldi and painted scenes of battles and ordinary people during the Risorgimento. He died in Milan in 1890.

Q44007.bio: Paul Klee was born near Bern, Switzerland, to a musical family and was also a talented violinist. He taught at the Bauhaus, a famous art school in Germany, and later fled the Nazis to Switzerland. His playful, imaginative paintings use lines, colors and symbols as if they were music. He died in Switzerland in 1940.

Q5075054.bio: Charles Alexander Smith was a Canadian painter born in Galt, Ontario, in 1864. He painted historical scenes and portraits. He later lived in London, England, where he died in 1915. His painting of the 'Assembly of the Six Counties' recorded an important event in Quebec history.

Q297.bio: Diego Velázquez was a Spanish painter born in Seville in 1599. He moved to Madrid as a young man and became the court painter to King Philip IV, painting portraits such as Las Meninas that are among the greatest in the world. He died in Madrid in 1660.

Q152797.bio: Umberto Boccioni was born in Reggio Calabria, Italy, and became the leader of Futurism, a movement that celebrated speed and machines. He worked in Milan and Rome, painting and making sculptures full of motion. He died at 33 after falling from a horse during military training in 1916.

Q3469342.bio: Sakai Hōitsu was born in Edo (Tokyo) to a samurai family and became a leading painter of the Rinpa school. He admired Ogata Kōrin and worked to revive his style. He painted flowers, birds and the seasons. He died in 1828.

Q15520500.bio: Thomas Davies was a British army officer and artist born in Shooter's Hill, near London, in 1737. He served in Canada and the American colonies and made watercolors of what he saw, which are some of the earliest views of North America. He died in Blackheath in 1812.

Q958927.bio: Aleksander Gierymski was born in Warsaw, Poland, and studied in Germany and Italy. He painted moonlit city scenes, with great honesty about everyday life. He lived in Warsaw and later in Rome, where he spent his last years. He died in 1901.

Q931356.bio: Konishi Hirosada was a Japanese printmaker who lived in Osaka from about 1810 to 1864. He is known for woodblock prints of kabuki actors. His prints were collected by fans like trading cards. He lived in the city's theater district.

Q76824158.bio: Guadalupe Carpio was a Mexican painter born in Xalapa in 1828, and one of the first women to study at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. She painted portraits and scenes of daily life. She died in 1892.

Q29405091.bio: Francisco Maura y Montaner was a Spanish painter born in Palma de Mallorca in 1857. He studied in Madrid and Rome, painted history pictures that won prizes at national exhibitions, and spent his later years in the Basque Country. He died in Irun in 1931.

Q134150.bio: Marie Spartali Stillman was born in London to a Greek family and became one of the few women to be a respected Pre-Raphaelite painter. She studied with Ford Madox Brown. She modeled for other artists, too. She lived in London and Italy and died in 1927.

Q20127345.bio: Joseph Kyle was an American portrait painter born in Ohio in 1815. He worked in New York City, painting many portraits of his time, including the Quaker minister Lucretia Mott. He died in 1863.

Q171344.bio: William Hogarth was born in London and became one of Britain's best-known painters and engravers. He made funny, sharp pictures about the follies of society, often in sets of prints that tell a story. He also championed the rights of artists. He died in London in 1764.

Q187310.bio: Carl Larsson was born in Stockholm to a poor family and became one of Sweden's best-loved painters. He is famous for his watercolors of his own home and family in Sundborn, which show happy children, flowers and sunshine. He also painted large murals. He died in 1919.

Q29032736.bio: Elisabeth Sinding was a Norwegian painter born in 1846, and one of the earlier women painters in her country. She painted landscapes and portraits. She lived in Oslo until her death in 1930.

Q381728.bio: George Stubbs was born in Liverpool, England, and taught himself to paint. He studied horse anatomy by dissecting horses and published a famous book about it. He became Britain's finest painter of horses and other animals. He died in London in 1806.

Q5580.bio: Albrecht Dürer was a German artist born in Nuremberg in 1471. He was a painter, but he is most famous for his woodcuts and engravings, which made him known across Europe, and for traveling to Italy to learn from Renaissance artists. He lived mostly in Nuremberg and died there in 1528.

Q217128.bio: Valentin Serov was born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, to a musical family. He studied under Repin and became Russia's most sought-after portrait painter, painting writers, musicians, and even the tsar. He lived mostly in Moscow. His portraits are admired for being fresh, sunny and natural.

Q583015.bio: Jacques Amans was born in Maastricht, in the Netherlands, and worked as a portrait painter in France and the United States. He lived in New Orleans for several years in the 1830s and painted many local families. He returned to Paris, where he died in 1888.

Q512648.bio: Reinier Vinkeles was a Dutch engraver and draftsman born in Amsterdam in 1741. He made prints of history and portraits, including scenes of the French Revolution for Dutch audiences. He lived in Amsterdam and died there in 1816.

Q405444.bio: Maruyama Ōkyo was born into a farming family near Kyoto and became one of the most important Japanese painters of the 1700s. He taught himself to paint from nature and was famous for his realistic animals and plants. He founded the Maruyama school. He died in Kyoto in 1795.

Q37974034.bio: John Ward Dunsmore was an American painter born in Ohio in 1856. He studied in Paris and became known for paintings of events of the American Revolution, which were used in schoolbooks. He died in 1945.

Q353628.bio: Arkhip Kuindzhi was born in a poor family in the Mariupol area of Ukraine and trained in Saint Petersburg. He was famous for using light in his landscapes to create a nearly glowing effect, as in his moonlit nights. He lived in Saint Petersburg, where he taught and gave money to young artists. He died there in 1910.

Q736379.bio: Jean Colombe was a French manuscript painter born in Bourges around 1430. He worked for the Duke of Savoy and finished the famous Très Riches Heures, and he painted beautiful illustrated histories for noble patrons. He lived in Bourges and died there around 1493.

Q1528580.bio: Giuseppe Pellizza da Volpedo was born in Volpedo, in northern Italy, and lived there much of his life. He painted in the style of dots and fine brushstrokes of pointillism. His masterpiece 'The Fourth Estate' shows workers marching for their rights. He died in 1907 at age 39.

Q2159499.bio: Roberto Ferruzzi was born in what is now Croatia and lived in Italy, mostly in Venice and nearby. He painted people and village scenes. His painting 'Madonnina' made him a celebrity when it won a prize in 1897. He died in 1934.

Q3680885.bio: Francis William Edmonds was an American painter born in Hudson, New York, in 1806. He was a banker who painted in his spare time, making charming scenes of everyday life. He lived in New York and died in Bronxville in 1863.

Q727060.bio: Victor Meirelles was born in Florianópolis, Brazil, and studied in Rio de Janeiro and Europe. He painted large pictures of the history of Brazil, such as 'The First Mass in Brazil'. He died in Rio de Janeiro in 1903.

Q148458.bio: Jean-François Millet was born into a farming family in Gruchy, on the coast of Normandy, France. He moved to the village of Barbizon near Paris, where he painted peasants at work in the fields. He treated farm laborers with dignity at a time when few artists did. His paintings moved Van Gogh and many others.

Q366212.bio: Frederic Edwin Church was born in Hartford, Connecticut, and studied with Thomas Cole. He traveled to South America, the Arctic and the Middle East, painting giant landscapes full of wonder. He became one of the most famous artists in the United States. He built a Persian-style mansion called Olana on the Hudson River.

Q598030.bio: George Caleb Bingham was born in Virginia and raised in Missouri. He painted the life of the Missouri and Mississippi rivers, from flatboatmen to election days. He also served in Missouri politics. He died in Kansas City in 1879.

Q369366.bio: Matthew Paris was an English monk and chronicler born around 1200. He lived at the abbey of St Albans, where he wrote and illustrated long histories of England and the world, with lively drawings of battles and kings. He died at St Albans in 1259.

Q1371063.bio: Timothy H. O'Sullivan was an American photographer born in Ireland or New York around 1840. He photographed the Civil War, including the dead at Gettysburg, and later made photographs of the American West. He died in New York in 1882.

Q312096.bio: Thomas Lawrence was an English painter born in Bristol in 1769. He became the most fashionable portrait painter of his time, painting kings, generals and beautiful ladies, and was president of the Royal Academy. He lived in London and died there in 1830.

Q164735.bio: Johan Christian Dahl was born in Bergen, Norway, and became known as the father of Norwegian landscape painting. He lived most of his life in Dresden, Germany, where he was a friend of Caspar David Friedrich. He painted clouds, mountains and fjords with great realism. He died in Dresden in 1857.

Q3897020.bio: Pasquale Cati was an Italian painter born in Jesi in about 1550. He worked in Rome, where he painted frescoes and altarpieces for churches in the style of the Catholic Counter-Reformation. He died there in 1620.

Q263025.bio: Harriet Backer was born in Holmestrand, Norway, and became one of the country's greatest painters. She studied in Munich and Paris and became famous for her glowing pictures of rooms and churches. She also ran a painting school that trained many young artists. She died in Oslo in 1932.

Q1854159.bio: The Master of Saint Giles was a French painter whose name is not known, active in Paris around 1500. He is named after a famous altarpiece showing the Mass of Saint Giles, now in the National Gallery in London, and he painted richly detailed religious scenes.

Q7345286.bio: Robert Harris was born in Wales and raised in Prince Edward Island. He studied in London and Paris and became one of Canada's leading portrait painters, and the president of the Royal Canadian Academy. He is best known for his painting of the Fathers of Confederation. He died in Montreal in 1919.

Q324622.bio: Henri Félix Emmanuel Philippoteaux was a French painter born in Paris in 1815. He made large battle paintings and giant circular panoramas, including a famous one of Gettysburg. He died in Paris in 1884.

Q34661.bio: Gustav Klimt was born near Vienna, Austria, the son of a gold engraver, which may be why gold glitters in so many of his paintings. He lived his entire life in and around Vienna and co-founded the Vienna Secession, a group of artists who broke from tradition. He painted beautiful portraits, murals, and landscapes. He died in 1918 at age 55 after a stroke.

Q1240575.bio: Itō Jakuchū was born in Kyoto, Japan, the son of a vegetable seller. He ran the family shop for years before devoting himself to painting, and kept chickens in his garden so he could study them. His colorful and detailed pictures of birds, plants and animals are among the most beloved in Japan. He died in 1800.

Q3136027.bio: Hippolyte Bellangé was a French painter and lithographer born in Paris in 1800. He painted soldiers and battle scenes, many from Napoleon's armies, and later served as curator of the museum in Rouen. He died in Paris in 1866.

Q78893573.bio: Antonio Cotti was an Italian painter born in Craveggia, in northern Italy, in 1840. He painted historical and literary scenes in a polished style, including a famous picture of the poet Dante in Verona. He died in 1929.

Q209050.bio: Jan Brueghel the Elder was a Flemish painter born in Brussels in 1568, the son of the famous Pieter Bruegel the Elder. He lived in Antwerp, was a friend and partner of Rubens, and became known as 'Velvet' Brueghel for his soft, delicate paintings of landscapes and flowers. He died in Antwerp in 1625.

Q2559361.bio: Jean-François Pierre Peyron was a French painter born in Aix-en-Provence in 1744. He won the Prix de Rome, worked in Rome and became an important early Neoclassical history painter and later a director of the Gobelins tapestry works. He died in Paris in 1814.

Q35548.bio: Paul Cézanne was born in Aix-en-Provence in southern France and lived there for much of his life, painting its hills, orchards, and the mountain Sainte-Victoire. He studied with the Impressionists in Paris, but then went his own way, building forms from blocks of color. He is often called the father of modern art, and both Picasso and Matisse praised him. He died in 1906 after catching a chill while painting outside.

Q1056862.bio: Cesare Maccari was an Italian painter born in Siena in 1840. He worked in Rome, where he painted large frescoes of ancient and national history, including one in the Italian Senate. He died in Rome in 1919.

Q381458.bio: Christen Købke was born in Copenhagen and was a leading painter of the Danish Golden Age. He painted views of the city, the shore and portraits of friends with a light, delicate touch. He died in 1848, at 37.

Q347139.bio: Jean-Baptiste Greuze was born in Tournus, France, and moved to Paris, where he became famous for sentimental paintings of family life and young girls with moral messages. He was admired by the philosopher Diderot. His popularity faded after the French Revolution. He died in Paris in 1805.

Q6394591.bio: Vasily Pukirev was born in the Tula region of Russia and became a painter and teacher in Moscow. His most famous painting, 'The Unequal Marriage,' criticized forced marriages. It was a sensation, and he later taught at the Moscow School of Painting. He died in 1890.

Q473813.bio: Georg Bleibtreu was a German painter born in Xanten in 1828. He lived in Berlin and became a leading painter of the Prussian wars of the 1860s and 1870s, depicting them in huge canvases. He died in Charlottenburg in 1892.

Q313498.bio: Benjamin West was born near Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and moved to Europe in his twenties. He settled in London, where he became the history painter to King George III and later President of the Royal Academy. He taught many American painters. He died in London in 1820.

Q6800323.bio: McClelland Barclay was an American illustrator born in St. Louis in 1891. He became famous for his magazine and poster art, then joined the US Navy as an artist in World War II. He disappeared at sea in 1943 when his ship was sunk.

x-john-of-kastav.bio: John of Kastav, in Croatian Ivan iz Kastva, was a painter from the town of Kastav in what is now Croatia, active in the late 1400s. In 1490 he painted the Dance of Death wall painting in the church of Hrastovlje in Slovenia, and very little else is known of his life.

Q65317.bio: Godfrey Kneller was a German-born painter, born in Lübeck in 1646. He moved to England and became the most successful portrait painter in London, painting eight kings and queens as well as Isaac Newton. He died in London in 1723.

Q1441399.bio: Francis Bicknell Carpenter was an American painter born in Homer, New York, in 1830. He lived for six months at the White House in 1864 to paint Abraham Lincoln and his cabinet, and he died in New York City in 1900.

Q689388.bio: Franz Anton Maulbertsch was an Austrian painter born in Langenargen on Lake Constance in 1724. He lived in Vienna and became the greatest painter of the Austrian Rococo, famous for his colorful ceiling paintings in churches and palaces. He died in Vienna in 1796.

Q2035136.bio: Tom Thomson was born in Ontario and worked as a commercial artist in Toronto before devoting himself to painting. He spent his summers in Algonquin Park, making small colorful oil sketches of lakes, trees and skies. His friends who later formed the Group of Seven were inspired by him. He drowned in Canoe Lake in 1917, and his death is still a famous mystery.

Q11996965.bio: Ragnhild Keyser was a Norwegian painter born in Oslo in 1889, who studied in Norway and Paris. She painted still lifes and landscapes with a quiet, careful style. She died in Oslo in 1943.

Q1554716.bio: Gunnar Berg was a Norwegian painter born in 1863 in the Lofoten region, known for his scenes of fjords and northern Norway. He studied in Germany. He died young, at 29, in Berlin in 1893.

x-anonymous-artist.bio: This work was made by an artist whose name was not recorded. Many historical paintings and prints, especially from the time of the events themselves, were made by anonymous artists.

Q54454217.bio: Frederick Thwaites Bush was an English artist born in Market Harborough in 1887. He made lithographs of scenes of the front, including Vimy Ridge, during World War I. He died in Greenwich in 1985.

Q1567177.bio: Michele Gordigiani was an Italian painter born in Florence in 1835. He became a popular portrait painter, painting the English poet Robert Browning and Italian politicians such as Cavour. He lived in Florence and died there in 1909.

Q958052.bio: Konstantin Savitsky was born in Taganrog, Russia, and studied at the Imperial Academy of Arts in Saint Petersburg. He was a member of the Peredvizhniki, or 'Wanderers,' a group who took realistic art to ordinary people around Russia. He was known for paintings of people and animals. He died in 1905 in Penza.

Q505758.bio: Karl von Piloty was a German painter born in Munich in 1826. He became director of the Munich art academy and was famous for huge, dramatic scenes from history, which he taught to dozens of students. He died near Munich in 1886.

Q2926650.bio: Bruno Bobak was a Canadian painter born in Poland in 1923. He grew up in Canada and served as an official Canadian war artist in World War II, then taught art in Fredericton, New Brunswick, where he lived until his death in 2012.

x-paul-revere.bio: Paul Revere was born in Boston in 1735 and became a silversmith, engraver and patriot. He is best known for his midnight ride in April 1775 to warn colonists that British soldiers were coming. He made the engraving of the Boston Massacre, and died in Boston in 1818.

Q380052.bio: Mariano Fortuny Marsal was born in Reus, Spain, and became one of the best-known Spanish painters of the 1800s. He traveled to Morocco and painted bright, detailed scenes. He lived in Rome and Madrid, and died young in Rome in 1874, at age 36.

Q351746.bio: Joaquín Sorolla was born in Valencia, Spain, and became known as the 'master of light' for his sparkling paintings of beaches and sunshine. He worked in Madrid and traveled to Paris and the United States, where he was very popular. His house in Madrid is now a museum. He died in Spain in 1923.

Q1356488.bio: Richard Bergh was born in Stockholm in 1858 and became one of Sweden's leading painters of the 'Nordic light'. He was also a director of the National Museum. He died in 1919.

Q937096.bio: John Martin was born in Northumberland, England, and made huge, dramatic paintings of disasters from the Bible and history. His work was hugely popular in London in the 1820s and 1830s, as thrilling as a movie. He also designed engineering schemes for his city. He died on the Isle of Man in 1854.

Q3290532.bio: John Steuart Curry was born on a farm in Kansas and became one of the main painters of the Regionalist movement, which celebrated the American Midwest. He painted farm life, storms and big moments from history. He also painted murals for the Kansas State Capitol. He died in Wisconsin in 1946.

Q981441.bio: Wilhelm Bendz was born in Odense, Denmark, and studied in Copenhagen. He painted lively portraits of his artist friends and finely detailed scenes of daily life. He died of an illness at only 28 in Vicenza, Italy, in 1832.

Q13422424.bio: Fredrik Borgen was a Norwegian landscape painter born in 1852, known for paintings of winter scenes and evening light. He studied in Germany. He died in Christiania in 1907.

Q443199.bio: Isaak Brodsky was a Russian painter born in 1884 in what is now Ukraine. He trained in Odessa, Saint Petersburg and Italy, and after the revolution became a leading Soviet painter, known for his portraits of Lenin. He died in Leningrad in 1939.

Q365682.bio: Gordon Parks was an American photographer born in Fort Scott, Kansas, in 1912. He started as a government photographer, then worked for Life magazine, wrote books and directed the film Shaft. He lived in New York and died there in 2006.

Q737635.bio: Childe Hassam was born near Boston and became a leading American Impressionist. He painted the streets and parks of New York, and a famous series of flag paintings. He also painted on the coast of Maine and at Appledore Island. He died in East Hampton, New York, in 1935.

Q1963206.bio: William Frederick Yeames was an English painter born in Taganrog, Russia, in 1835, where his father was British consul. He moved to London and painted historical pictures, becoming a member of the Royal Academy. He died in Teignmouth in 1918.

Q13434144.bio: Karl Uchermann was a Norwegian painter born in the Lofoten region in 1855. He painted scenes of Northern Norway and of animals, particularly dogs. He lived in Oslo. He died in 1940.

Q186748.bio: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was born in London to an Italian family of poets and scholars. He co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood and painted dreamy, romantic women. He was also a poet, and often paired paintings with verses. He lived in London and died in 1882.

Q365068.bio: P. S. Krøyer was born in Stavanger, Norway, and grew up in Copenhagen, Denmark. He was the central figure of the Skagen Painters, an artist colony in northern Denmark. His paintings capture the beautiful blue light of summer evenings by the sea. He died in Skagen in 1909.

Q468772.bio: Anne Vallayer-Coster was born in Paris and became famous for lifelike still-life paintings of flowers, fruit and musical instruments. She was admitted to the French Royal Academy at 26 and also painted portraits. She worked for Queen Marie Antoinette. She died in Paris in 1818.

Q363968.bio: Fritz von Dardel was a Swedish artist born in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, in 1817. He moved to Stockholm and became a court painter, also known for lively cartoons and sketches of events of his day. He died in Stockholm in 1901.

Q1970087.bio: Philip James de Loutherbourg was an artist born in Strasbourg in 1740. He moved to London in 1771, where he designed spectacular theater scenery for the actor David Garrick and painted dramatic landscapes, battles and industrial scenes. He lived in Hammersmith and died in Chiswick in 1812.

Q328369.bio: Edwin Landseer was born in London and showed an extraordinary talent for drawing animals as a child. He became Queen Victoria's favorite animal painter, and he created the bronze lions at the base of Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square. He painted dogs, horses, and stags with great warmth. He died in London in 1873.

Q6171629.bio: Severin Segelcke was a Norwegian painter born in Christiania in 1867. He painted landscapes and portraits and lived part of his life in Norway's countryside. He died in 1940.

Q876701.bio: Ludwig Thiersch was a German painter born in Munich in 1825. He lived mostly in Munich and painted religious and historical pictures, spending some time in Greece, which inspired his scenes of the ancient world. He died in Munich in 1909.

Q363823.bio: Christoffer Wilhelm Eckersberg was born in southern Denmark and became the 'father of Danish painting.' He studied in Paris and Rome and taught many painters in Copenhagen. He painted portraits, ships, and clear, bright scenes of Rome. He died in Copenhagen in 1853.

Q214905.bio: Thomas Eakins was born in Philadelphia and lived there nearly all his life. He studied anatomy and photography so his paintings of people, rowers and surgeons would be true to life. His honest realism upset some people, but is now praised. He taught art in Philadelphia and died there in 1916.

x-robert-walker.bio: Robert Walker was an English portrait painter born around 1599 who worked in London. He painted many portraits of Oliver Cromwell and other leaders of the Parliamentary side in the English Civil War. He died in London around 1658.

Q515879.bio: Alexey Venetsianov was a Russian painter born in Moscow in 1780. He is considered the founder of Russian paintings of peasant life, and started a school at his country estate. He died in 1847 in an accident when his horse bolted.

Q5588070.bio: William Blair Bruce was born in Hamilton, Ontario, and lived in Europe for most of his career, in France and Sweden. He painted landscapes and dramatic scenes. His paintings and sculptures are now in a museum he planned in his hometown. He died in Stockholm in 1906.

Q1516217.bio: Isidor Popper was a German lithographer and cartoonist born in Hildesheim in 1816. He worked in Hamburg, where he made satirical prints, including some about the revolution of 1848. He died in Hamburg in 1884.

x-dorothea-lange.bio: Dorothea Lange was an American photographer born in Hoboken, New Jersey, in 1895. She moved to San Francisco, and during the Great Depression worked for the government photographing the lives of poor farm families, creating the famous Migrant Mother. She died in San Francisco in 1965.

Q4129638.bio: Oscar Wergeland was born in Christiania in 1844 and became a Norwegian painter of history. His huge painting of the Norwegian constitution of 1814 is one of Norway's best-known pictures. He died in 1910.

x-giovanni-villani-nuova-cronica.bio: The Nuova Cronica was written by Giovanni Villani, a Florentine merchant and historian born around 1276, who died in the Black Death in Florence in 1348. The surviving manuscripts of his chronicle were illustrated by artists whose names are not known.

Q271676.bio: Charles Le Brun was a French painter born in Paris in 1619. He became First Painter to King Louis XIV and directed the decoration of the palace of Versailles and the Gobelins tapestry works. He died in Paris in 1690.

Q223725.bio: Francesco Hayez was born in Venice, Italy, and later became the leading painter in Milan. He painted history scenes that stirred Italian pride during the fight for unification of Italy. He also made fine portraits. He lived to be 91, long enough to see Italy become one country.

Q285423.bio: Sebastiano del Piombo was an Italian painter born in Venice around 1485. He moved to Rome and became a friend of Michelangelo, painting powerful portraits that mixed Venetian color with Roman grandeur. He died in Rome in 1547.

Q160141.bio: Chaïm Soutine was born into a poor Jewish family in a small village in what is now Belarus. He moved to Paris in 1913, where he lived and painted in a crowded artists' colony and became close friends with Modigliani. His wild, twisting paintings of waiters, pastry cooks and landscapes made him famous. He died in Paris in 1943, during the German occupation.

Q709280.bio: Arthur Streeton was born in Victoria, Australia, and became a leading painter of the Heidelberg School, a group of artists who painted outdoors. He is best known for golden, sunny landscapes. He later lived in London and returned to Australia. He died in 1943.

Q1290058.bio: Eduard Steinbrück was a German painter born in Magdeburg in 1802. He worked in Berlin and Düsseldorf and painted historical and religious scenes and portraits. He died in Lądek-Zdrój, now in Poland, in 1882.

Q570172.bio: Gaspar de Crayer was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1584 who worked in Brussels and Ghent. He painted altarpieces and portraits in the Baroque style and was a respected rival of Rubens. He died in Ghent in 1669.

Q984242.bio: Louis-Maurice Boutet de Monvel was a French artist born in Orléans in 1850. He became famous as an illustrator of children's books, including a beautiful book about Joan of Arc in 1896, and also painted portraits in Paris, where he died in 1913.

Q77324.bio: Anton von Werner was a German painter born in Frankfurt an der Oder in 1843. He lived in Berlin, where he became director of the art academy and the leading painter of the Prussian court, recording events such as the proclamation of the German Empire. He died in Berlin in 1915.

Q2090482.bio: Alfred Jacob Miller was an American painter born in Baltimore in 1810. In 1837 he traveled west to the Rocky Mountains and made the first paintings of the fur trade and Native American life there. He lived in Baltimore and died there in 1874.

Q1293506.bio: Edward Savage was born in Massachusetts and was an American painter and engraver. He painted George Washington from life and made popular prints of his work. He lived in Philadelphia, New York and Boston. He died in 1817.

Q130531.bio: Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch painter, born in the town of 's-Hertogenbosch around 1450. He lived there all his life and painted strange, crowded visions of heaven, hell and human foolishness filled with monsters and tiny details. He died in 's-Hertogenbosch in 1516.

x-benjamin-moran.bio: Benjamin Moran was the artist who designed the cover of the official program for the Woman Suffrage Procession in Washington on March 3, 1913, showing a woman on a white horse in front of the Capitol.

Q207758.bio: Ivan Kramskoi was born in Ostrogozhsk, Russia, and worked in Saint Petersburg. He was a leader of the Wanderers, artists who rebelled against stuffy academic rules. He painted deeply felt portraits of writers, scholars and ordinary people. He also wrote and taught about art, and he inspired a generation of Russian painters.

x-remigio-legat.bio: Remigio Legat was an Italian painter of the 1800s who painted scenes from the Risorgimento, the movement that united Italy. His picture of the Battle of Calatafimi was painted in 1860, soon after Garibaldi's victory.

Q316016.bio: John Singleton Copley was born in Boston and became America's finest portrait painter before the Revolution. He painted merchants and patriots, like Paul Revere. In 1774 he moved to England as war loomed, and spent the rest of his life in London. He died there in 1815.

Q34618.bio: Gustave Courbet was born in Ornans, in eastern France, and moved to Paris to become an artist. He led the Realism movement, insisting on painting real people and real life instead of myths. He was outspoken and got into political trouble, and he fled to Switzerland in the end. He died there in 1877.

Q354786.bio: Ernest Meissonier was a French painter born in Lyon in 1815. He became famous for tiny, extremely detailed pictures, and later for big scenes of Napoleon's armies and the siege of Paris, where he served as an officer. He lived in Paris and Poissy and died in Paris in 1891.

Q1043318.bio: Carlos de Haes was born in Brussels and moved to Spain as a young man. He became the leading Spanish landscape painter, introducing a realistic, outdoor style. He taught at the Academy in Madrid. He died there in 1898.

Q739176.bio: Eilif Peterssen was born in Christiania and studied in Munich, Paris and Italy. He painted historical scenes, portraits and landscapes, and helped bring the Realist style to Norway. He lived in Oslo and in Lysaker. He died in 1928.

Q10319762.bio: Laureys a Castro was a marine painter born in Antwerp around 1644 who later moved to England. He painted sea battles and ships, and he is known as one of the Flemish artists who brought the Dutch style of sea painting to Britain. He died in England around 1700.

Q13099283.bio: Frédéric Théodore Lix was a French illustrator born in Strasbourg in 1830. He drew news pictures for magazines, such as L'Illustration, and recorded the war of 1870 and the Paris Commune. He lived in Paris and died there in 1897.

Q289624.bio: Emily Carr was born in Victoria, British Columbia, and studied art in San Francisco, London and France. She became famous for her paintings of the forests, totem poles and Indigenous villages of the Pacific coast. She was also a writer and lived with many pets. She died in Victoria in 1945.

Q13583490.bio: Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger was a painter born in Bruges in 1561 who moved to England as a child. He became one of the leading portrait painters of the court of Queen Elizabeth I, painting rich clothes and jewels in fine detail. He lived in London and died there in 1636.

x-ronald-a-wilson.bio: Ronald A. Wilson was an American artist who served as a combat artist with the US Army in Vietnam in 1967. His moody, colorful paintings of night operations and helicopters are in the US Army art collection.

Q3385390.bio: Pierre Gustave Staal was a French illustrator born in Vertus in 1817. He made lithographs and engravings of costumes and portraits, including a well-known portrait of Pocahontas, and lived in Paris, where he died in 1882.

Q27028228.bio: John Rose was a painter in the late 1700s who lived in the Colony of South Carolina. His watercolor 'The Old Plantation' is one of the earliest paintings to show the lives of enslaved African Americans. Little else is known about him.

Q2627916.bio: Ulpiano Checa was a Spanish painter born in Colmenar de Oreja in 1860. He moved to Paris, where he became famous for dynamic pictures of chariots, horses and battles, and later lived in France. He died in an automobile accident in Dax, France, in 1916.

Q2777444.bio: Marquard Wocher was born in Germany in 1760 and settled in Basel, Switzerland. He is remembered for his huge circular painting of Thun and the Alps, one of the oldest panoramas in the world. He died in 1830.

Q4348982.bio: David Milne was born in Ontario and lived in New York, then returned to the Ontario woods in 1930. He painted with a delicate touch, using watercolors and thin oils to capture cities, flowers and woods. He is considered one of Canada's greatest modern painters. He died in 1953.

Q2460318.bio: Edmund Charles Tarbell was born in Massachusetts and was a leading Boston painter. He taught at the Museum School in Boston and painted graceful pictures of women in sunlit rooms. He later lived in New Hampshire. He died in 1938.

Q83155.bio: Jacques-Louis David was born in Paris and became the greatest painter of the Neoclassical style, inspired by ancient Greece and Rome. He supported the French Revolution and later became Napoleon's official painter. After Napoleon fell, he was forced into exile and spent his last years in Brussels, Belgium. He taught many famous students and shaped French art for generations.

Q11680193.bio: Benet Mercadé was a Spanish painter born in La Bisbal d'Empordà in Catalonia in 1821. He worked in Rome, where he joined the Nazarene group of painters, and later in Barcelona, where he became a respected teacher. He died in Barcelona in 1897.

Q390904.bio: Luc-Olivier Merson was a French painter born in Paris in 1846. He won the Prix de Rome in 1869 with his picture of the runner of Marathon, then taught at the École des Beaux-Arts and also designed banknotes and stamps. He lived and worked in Paris until he died in 1920.

Q3568797.bio: Will Longstaff was an Australian painter born in Ballarat in 1879. He served in World War I and then painted memorials to the missing, including Menin Gate at Midnight, which toured Australia and Britain. He died in Littlehampton, England, in 1953.

Q979541.bio: Martinus Rørbye was born in Drammen, Norway, and moved to Denmark as a child. He was a leading painter of the Danish Golden Age and traveled to Italy, Greece, and Turkey. He painted precise scenes of streets, interiors and windows. He died in Copenhagen in 1848.

Q127171.bio: Jean-Honoré Fragonard was born in Grasse, in the south of France, and moved to Paris as a boy. He studied in Italy and became a star of the Rococo style, painting playful, romantic scenes for the nobility. After the French Revolution, his style fell out of fashion, and he spent his last years nearly forgotten in Paris. Today we again admire his speed and charm.

Q191748.bio: Lucas Cranach the Elder was a German painter born in Kronach in 1472. He became court painter to the rulers of Saxony in Wittenberg, was a close friend of Martin Luther, and ran a busy workshop that made portraits, religious scenes and the first Protestant images. He died in Weimar in 1553.

Q658162.bio: Wilhelm Camphausen was a German painter born in Düsseldorf in 1818. He specialized in battle and military scenes, painted the wars of Prussia, and lived in Düsseldorf, where he died in 1885.

Q540219.bio: Pedro Américo was a Brazilian painter born in 1843 in Paraíba. He studied in Paris and painted huge history pictures, including 'Independence or Death!' He also wrote books and was a politician. He died in Florence, Italy, in 1905.

Q11571471.bio: Kanō Eigaku was a Japanese painter of the Kanō school, a family of artists that painted for Japan's rulers for hundreds of years. He worked in the late Edo and Meiji periods. He was famous for traditional pictures of Japanese life. He died in 1867.

Q104884.bio: Caspar David Friedrich was born in the Baltic port of Greifswald, Germany, and later settled in Dresden. He painted quiet, mysterious landscapes of mountains, fog, ruins, and seashores, often with a tiny figure seen from behind. He believed nature was a way of feeling something divine. He became a hero of German Romanticism, though he was nearly forgotten for decades before being rediscovered.

Q979534.bio: Isaac Israëls was born in Amsterdam, the son of the famous painter Jozef Israëls, in a Dutch Jewish family. He painted lively scenes of Amsterdam streets, fashion houses and beaches in a loose, fast Impressionist style. He lived in Amsterdam, Paris, and The Hague, and he traveled to Indonesia and elsewhere. He died in The Hague in 1934.

Q318393.bio: Vasily Polenov was born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, and became a leading landscape painter and teacher. He traveled in Europe and the Middle East. He built an estate on the Oka River that is now a museum. He died in 1927.

Q1778899.bio: Asta Nørregaard was born in Christiania (now Oslo) and was one of Norway's first professional women painters. She studied in Munich and Paris and painted portraits, including one of Edvard Munch. She was an important supporter of other artists. She died in 1933.

Q44054.bio: Franz Marc was born in Munich, Germany, and loved painting animals as a symbol of purity. He co-founded the Blue Rider group with Wassily Kandinsky, and he used bold colors like blue and yellow to express feelings. He lived in Bavaria. He died in World War I in 1916 at age 36.

Q1606486.bio: Henry Bacon was an American painter born in Haverhill, Massachusetts, in 1839. He fought in the Civil War, then lived in Paris for most of his life, painting scenes from American history and Egypt. He died in Cairo in 1912.

Q5582.bio: Vincent van Gogh was born in a small village in the Netherlands and worked as a teacher and art dealer before becoming a painter at age 27. He lived in the Netherlands, Belgium, Paris, and finally the sunny south of France, where his colors grew brighter and bolder. He painted more than 800 paintings in about a decade, yet sold almost none while alive. After his death at 37, his brother's family helped make him one of the most loved artists in history.

Q48319.bio: Hans Holbein the Younger was a German painter born in Augsburg in about 1497. He worked in Basel and then in London, where he became court painter to King Henry VIII and painted portraits that made the Tudors famous. He died in London in 1543, probably of the plague.

Q2582642.bio: James Pollard was an English painter born in London in 1792. He specialized in lively pictures of stagecoaches, inns and early railways, and he lived in London, where he died in 1867.

Q8017377.bio: William Raphael was born in Poland, then part of Prussia, and moved to Montreal as a young man. He painted the streets, markets and views of Montreal and Quebec in the 1860s. His pictures record the city as it was. He died in Montreal in 1914.

Q64633.bio: George Peter Alexander Healy was born in Boston and became a portrait painter who worked in Paris, Rome, Chicago and Washington. He painted American presidents and the kings and queens of Europe. He lived long in Europe before settling in Chicago. He died there in 1894.

x-charles-alfred-stothard.bio: Charles Alfred Stothard was an English artist and antiquarian born in London in 1786. He made careful drawings of medieval tombs and of the Bayeux Tapestry, which he copied in the 1810s for the Society of Antiquaries. He died in 1821 after falling from a ladder while sketching a stained-glass window in a church in Devon.

Q208993.bio: Nicholas Roerich was a Russian painter born in Saint Petersburg in 1874. He painted scenes from ancient Russian history and legend, designed ballet sets, and after the revolution left Russia, traveling through Asia and finally settling in northern India. He died in Kullu, India, in 1947.

Q443136.bio: Maurycy Gottlieb was born in Drohobych, in Galicia, to a Jewish family and studied art in Kraków, Vienna and Munich. He was a student of the great painter Jan Matejko and painted striking pictures of Jewish life and history. He died in Kraków in 1879 at only 22. His few works are treasured today.

Q360679.bio: Joseph-Noël Sylvestre was a French painter born in Béziers in 1847. He studied in Paris and painted large history scenes, especially of the fall of ancient Rome, some of which hang in French museums. He died in Paris in 1926.

Q319843.bio: Ford Madox Brown was born in Calais, France, to English parents and trained in Belgium before settling in London. He was a close friend of the Pre-Raphaelites, though he never formally joined them. He painted history, literature and scenes of modern working life, including the famous 'Work'. He died in London in 1893.

Q432296.bio: Werner Holmberg was a Finnish landscape painter born in Helsinki in 1830. He studied in Düsseldorf in Germany, where he died of illness at only 30. His paintings of Finnish forests and fields were important for Finnish art.

Q156386.bio: Henri Rousseau was born in Laval, France, and worked as a tax-and-toll collector, earning the nickname 'Le Douanier' (the customs officer). He taught himself to paint and began exhibiting in his forties. His jungle scenes, painted from visits to the Paris botanical garden, were mocked at first but later admired by Picasso and others. He died in Paris in 1910.

Q911575.bio: Paul Baudry was born in La Roche-sur-Yon, France, and trained in Paris and Rome. He painted elegant portraits and murals, including the ceiling of the Paris Opera foyer. His work was admired by the Emperor Napoleon III. He died in Paris in 1886.

Q322582.bio: Paul Delaroche was born in Paris and became one of France's most popular painters of dramatic history scenes. He worked and taught in Paris, where he trained many future artists. His paintings often show famous tragedies, such as the death of royalty. He died in Paris in 1856.

Q47551.bio: Titian was an Italian painter born in Pieve di Cadore around 1490. He worked in Venice and became the most famous painter in Europe, painting portraits for the Emperor Charles V and King Philip II of Spain with rich color and loose brushwork. He lived to a great age and died in Venice in 1576.

Q2555178.bio: Nicolas Mignard was a French painter born in Troyes in 1606. He worked for many years in Avignon, where he was nicknamed Mignard of Avignon, and then moved to Paris to paint for the royal court. He was the older brother of the painter Pierre Mignard and died in Paris in 1668.

Q1133777.bio: Cornelius Krieghoff was born in Amsterdam and moved to North America as a young man. He lived in Montreal and Quebec, where he painted lively scenes of French-Canadian farm life and winter. His humorous pictures made him one of Canada's most popular painters. He died in Chicago in 1872.

Q5432.bio: Francisco Goya was born in a small village in Spain and became the court painter to the Spanish kings in Madrid. After an illness left him deaf in his forties, his art grew darker and more personal. He witnessed war and cruelty and made powerful pictures about it. He spent his last years in Bordeaux, France, and is seen as a bridge between old masters and modern art.

Q262771.bio: Michael Wolgemut was a German painter and printmaker born in Nuremberg in 1434. He ran a large workshop that illustrated the famous Nuremberg Chronicle in 1493, and the young Albrecht Dürer was his apprentice. He worked in Nuremberg and died there in 1519.

Q207298.bio: Frédéric Bazille was born into a wealthy family in Montpellier, France, and moved to Paris to paint. He was a close friend of Monet and Renoir and shared a studio with them. He painted sunny outdoor scenes and portraits. He was killed in the Franco-Prussian War in 1870 when he was only 28.

Q40599.bio: Édouard Manet was born into a wealthy Parisian family and lived in Paris all his life. He painted modern city life — cafés, bars, and picnics — in a bold, flat style that scandalized critics. He never officially joined the Impressionists, but he inspired them, and they admired him as a leader. He died in 1883 at age 51.

Q5233531.bio: David Fairrington was an American artist born in 1940 who served as a member of the US Army's Vietnam combat art team in 1968. His paintings of soldiers, helicopters and Vietnamese people are in the US Army art collection.

Q1390614.bio: Eero Järnefelt was born in Vyborg and became a leading Finnish painter of rural life and landscapes. He studied in Saint Petersburg and Paris. His family included the composer Jean Sibelius, who was his brother-in-law. He died in Helsinki in 1937.

Q105320.bio: Berthe Morisot was born in Bourges, France, and studied painting with Corot. She exhibited in the first Impressionist show in 1874 and was one of the movement's leading figures. She married Eugène Manet, the brother of Édouard Manet, and lived in Paris. She painted women, children and gardens with a light, fresh touch.

Q1383101.bio: François-Auguste Biard was a French painter born in Lyon in 1799. He traveled widely to Lapland and Brazil, painted exotic scenes and political pictures, including one about the abolition of slavery in 1848. He died in Fontainebleau in 1882.

Q2958767.bio: Charles Comfort was a Canadian painter born in Edinburgh, Scotland, in 1900. He grew up in Winnipeg, served as an official war artist in World War II and later became the director of the National Gallery of Canada. He died in Ottawa in 1994.

Q2095810.bio: William Simpson was a Scottish war artist, born in Glasgow in 1823. He worked as a correspondent for the Illustrated London News and was sent to the Crimean War, drawing what he saw for newspapers at home, and later traveled to India, Abyssinia and elsewhere. He died in London in 1899.

Q388523.bio: Peter von Hess was a German painter born in Düsseldorf in 1792. He worked in Munich and became the leading battle painter of Bavaria, painting scenes of the Napoleonic wars and the Greek War of Independence. He died in Munich in 1871.

x-byzantine-mosaicists.bio: The mosaics of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople were made by Byzantine artists whose names are not known. They placed thousands of tiny pieces of colored glass and gold in the plaster, creating images that glitter in candlelight, over several centuries.

Q4113103.bio: Ivan Vladimirov was a Russian painter born in Vilnius in 1869. He worked in Saint Petersburg and made large paintings and drawings of the revolutions of 1905 and 1917 as an eyewitness. He died in Leningrad in 1947.

Q154349.bio: Odilon Redon was born in Bordeaux, France, and spent most of his life in Paris. He began with strange, dreamlike black-and-white drawings, then later painted flowers and myths in luminous color. His art was admired by Symbolists and later by the Surrealists. He died in Paris in 1916.

Q11705308.bio: William Brymner was born in Scotland and raised in Canada. He studied in Paris and became an influential teacher at the Art Association of Montreal, where he taught many of the country's best-known painters. His own paintings show women and children in warm, soft light. He died in 1925.

Q610971.bio: José María Velasco was born in a village in Mexico and became the country's most famous landscape painter. He was also a scientist who studied plants, animals and the sky. His paintings of the Valley of Mexico show its volcanoes and lakes. He died in Mexico City in 1912.

Q718474.bio: Panagiotis Zographos was a Greek painter from the Peloponnese who lived in the 1800s. He painted a famous series of scenes of the Greek War of Independence in a bright folk style, after the memories of the general Makriyannis, who hired him in the 1830s.

Q5586.bio: Katsushika Hokusai was born in Edo (now Tokyo) and worked as an artist for over 70 years. He made thousands of drawings and woodblock prints, including The Great Wave and the Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji. He changed his name dozens of times and said he hoped to get better until he was 110. He died in 1849, at about age 89.

Q918605.bio: Herbert James Draper was born in London and studied at the Royal Academy. He painted scenes from Greek and Roman myth with glowing color and graceful figures. His 'The Lament for Icarus' is his best-known work. He died in London in 1920.

Q41554.bio: Nicolas Poussin was a French painter born in Les Andelys in 1594. He moved to Rome as a young man and spent most of his life there, painting calm, well-planned scenes from ancient history and mythology that set the standard for classical painting. He died in Rome in 1665.

Q152233.bio: El Lissitzky was a Russian artist born in Pochinok in 1890. He worked as an architect, a painter and a designer, and made his famous poster of the Red Wedge in 1919. He lived in Vitebsk, Germany and Moscow, and died in Moscow in 1941.

x-anonymous-illuminator-vigiles-de-charl.bio: This miniature was painted by an unknown artist who illustrated the Vigiles du roi Charles VII, a French poem by Martial d'Auvergne about the reign of King Charles VII, in about 1484.

x-nasa-photograph-by-david-scott.bio: David Scott, born in 1932 in Texas, was an American astronaut who flew to the Moon as commander of Apollo 15 in 1971. He took photographs of his crewmate James Irwin on the surface and the lunar rover.

Q153746.bio: Albrecht Altdorfer was a German painter born near Nuremberg in about 1480 who lived in Regensburg, where he also served as a city councilor and architect. He was one of the first European artists to make landscapes the main subject of his pictures. He died in Regensburg in 1538.

Q128534.bio: Fredrik Kolstø was a Norwegian painter born in 1860 in the region of Haugesund and studied in Paris. He painted historical and landscape pictures. He lived in Trondheim for part of his life. He died in 1945.

Q32859679.bio: Manuel Ocaranza was born in Uruapan, Mexico, in 1841 and studied at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. He painted romantic scenes and portraits and was one of the best Mexican painters of his time. He died young, at 41, in 1882.

Q5080054.bio: Charles Landseer was an English painter born in London in 1799, the older brother of the animal painter Edwin Landseer. He painted historical scenes, especially from the English Civil War, and was the Keeper of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1879.

Q15433971.bio: Pierre-Charles Canot was a French engraver born around 1710 who moved to London. He engraved many sea scenes and battle pictures, and died in London in 1777.

Q204138.bio: Viktor Vasnetsov was born in a village in northern Russia, the son of a priest. He lived in Moscow, and became known for painting scenes from Russian folk tales and legends, with warriors, witches and firebirds. He also designed churches and theater sets. He died in Moscow in 1926.

Q578067.bio: Hendrick Cornelisz Vroom was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1562. He is often called the father of Dutch marine painting, and made pictures of ships and sea battles for admirals and the government. He lived in Haarlem and died there in 1640.

Q159758.bio: J. M. W. Turner was born in London, the son of a barber, and became a student at the Royal Academy at just 14. He traveled across Britain and Europe, painting storms, ships, and sunsets in swirling light and color. He called the sky his subject, and his late paintings are almost abstract. He left thousands of works to the British nation when he died in London in 1851.

Q766362.bio: William Etty was born in York, England, and spent his life training to paint like the Old Masters. He is best known for his rich colors and glowing skin tones. He worked in London but retired to his hometown of York. He died there in 1849.

Q282512.bio: Oscar Björck was born in Stockholm in 1860 and was a Swedish painter and teacher. He spent time in the Skagen artists' colony in Denmark. He painted portraits and landscapes. He died in 1929.

Q6503742.bio: Lawren P. Harris was a Canadian painter born in Toronto in 1910, the son of the Group of Seven painter Lawren Harris. He was an official Canadian war artist in World War II and later a teacher and painter. He died in Ottawa in 1994.

Q8009345.bio: William Franklin Draper was an American painter born in Hopedale, Massachusetts, in 1912. He was a combat artist for the US Navy in World War II and later a portrait painter in California. He died in 2003.

Q3424670.bio: Ole Peter Hansen Balling was born in Christiania and moved to the United States in 1856. He fought in the American Civil War and painted portraits of President Lincoln, Ulysses S. Grant and other leaders. He later returned to Norway. He died in 1906.

Q449519.bio: Richard Dadd was born in Chatham, England, and became a talented painter before he fell seriously ill in his twenties. He spent the rest of his life in hospitals, where he kept painting amazing, tiny, detailed fairy pictures. He lived in Bethlem and then Broadmoor Hospital. He died in 1886.

Q559559.bio: Fernand Khnopff was born in Belgium and became one of the leading Symbolist painters. He lived in Brussels and designed his own house. His quiet, mysterious pictures often show dreamlike women. He died in Brussels in 1921.

Q718975.bio: François-André Vincent was a French painter born in Paris in 1746. He won the Prix de Rome, studied in Italy and became a leading history painter in the Neoclassical style, a rival of Jacques-Louis David. He taught at the art academy in Paris and died there in 1816.

Q290407.bio: Gentile Bellini was an Italian painter born in Venice around 1429, the older brother of the painter Giovanni Bellini. He worked for the government of Venice and in 1479 was sent to Constantinople to paint the sultan Mehmed II. He returned to Venice and died there in 1507.

x-national-woman-suffrage-publishing-co.bio: The National Woman Suffrage Publishing Company printed posters, newspapers and flyers to win American women the vote. Its materials appeared around the country in the 1910s.

Q214957.bio: Thomas Nast was an American cartoonist born in Landau, Germany, in 1840. He moved to New York as a child and became famous in Harper's Weekly for his political cartoons, and is credited with creating the Republican elephant and the modern Santa Claus. He died in Ecuador in 1902, where he served as US consul.

x-henri-ambrosius-pacx.bio: Henri Ambrosius Pacx was a painter who made a picture of Prince Maurice of Orange at the Battle of Nieuwpoort in the 1800s, long after the battle itself. Very little is known about his life.

Q702272.bio: Johann Zoffany was born in Frankfurt, Germany, and moved to London. He painted 'conversation pieces' — groups of people in rooms and gardens — as well as theatrical scenes. He traveled to Italy and India, and became a favorite of the British royal family. He died in London in 1810.

Q41402.bio: Gilbert Stuart was born in Rhode Island and became America's best-known portrait painter. He painted George Washington and other leaders of the young United States. He lived for years in London and Dublin before returning to the U.S. He died in Boston in 1828.

Q1795226.bio: Walenty Wańkowicz was born in a village in what is now Belarus and studied in Vilnius. He became a Polish painter famous for portraits of poets, including Adam Mickiewicz. He lived in Saint Petersburg and in Paris. He died in Paris in 1842.

Q3659111.bio: Carlo Bossoli was an Italian-Swiss painter born near Lugano in 1815. He worked in Odessa and then Turin, where he painted detailed pictures of the battles and events of the Italian wars of independence. He died in Turin in 1884.

Q200798.bio: Utagawa Hiroshige was born in Edo (Tokyo) and became one of Japan's greatest print artists. He is known for his landscapes, such as the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō and One Hundred Famous Views of Edo. Van Gogh and Monet admired his work. He died in 1858.

Q433434.bio: Anne-Louis Girodet was born in Montargis, France, and studied under Jacques-Louis David. He became a leader of French Romanticism with dreamy, mysterious paintings. He lived in Rome and Paris. He died in Paris in 1824.

Q143595.bio: Stradanus, whose Flemish name was Jan van der Straet, was a painter and designer born in Bruges in 1523. He moved to Florence, where he designed tapestries for the Medici and many prints, including a famous series on the discovery of America. He died in Florence in 1605.

Q7325393.bio: Richard Edward Miller was born in St. Louis, Missouri, and studied in Paris. He joined the American art colony at Giverny, near Monet's home, and painted bright Impressionist scenes of women in sunlit rooms. He later lived in Provincetown, Massachusetts. He died in 1943.

Q2545507.bio: George Washington Lambert was born in Saint Petersburg to American parents and moved to Australia as a child. He became a famous portrait painter and an official war artist at Gallipoli and in the Middle East. He died in 1930.

Q273115.bio: Anna Bilińska-Bohdanowicz was born in Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire, to a Polish family and studied in Saint Petersburg, Munich and Paris. She lived in Warsaw and was one of the first Polish women to win international acclaim as a painter. She painted portraits and scenes in a modern style. She died young, in 1893, at age 39.

Q353008.bio: Alexei Savrasov was born in Moscow and taught at the Moscow School of Painting. His painting 'The Rooks Have Returned' is often seen as the start of the Russian landscape tradition. He painted ordinary rural scenes with deep feeling. He died in Moscow in 1897.

Q215073.bio: Moritz Daniel Oppenheim was born in Hanau, Germany, to a Jewish family and trained in Munich, Paris and Rome. He lived mostly in Frankfurt, where he became a favorite painter of the Rothschild family. He is best known for warm pictures of traditional Jewish family life. He died in Frankfurt in 1882.

Q43270.bio: Pieter Bruegel the Elder was a Flemish painter born near Breda in about 1525. He lived in Antwerp and Brussels and became famous for crowded paintings of village life, proverbs and landscapes. He died in Brussels in 1569.

Q1361950.bio: Pietro Rotari was an Italian painter born in Verona in 1707. He painted portraits and charming scenes of young women, worked in Vienna and Dresden, and in 1756 moved to Saint Petersburg to paint at the court of Empress Elizabeth. He died there in 1762.

Q1606630.bio: Henry Courtney Selous was an English painter and illustrator born in Deptford in 1803. He painted big historical pictures and illustrated books, including a famous painting of the opening of the Great Exhibition in 1851. He died in Devon in 1890.

Q271484.bio: Marguerite Gérard was born in Grasse, France, and moved to Paris as a teenager to train with her brother-in-law, Fragonard. She became a successful painter of elegant home scenes, often showing women reading, writing or playing music. She exhibited at the Salon and sold to the wealthy collectors of Europe. She died in Paris in 1837.

Q381248.bio: James Tissot was born in Nantes, France, and moved to London, where he painted fashionable scenes of Victorian life. Later he traveled to the Holy Land and made a famous series of illustrations of the Bible. He was a very successful artist. He died in France in 1902.

Q151803.bio: Piet Mondrian was born in the Netherlands and started out painting windmills and trees. He lived in Amsterdam, Paris, London and finally New York City. Over time he simplified his art into straight black lines and blocks of red, yellow and blue. He died in New York in 1944, and his style inspired architects and designers worldwide.

Q671883.bio: Théo van Rysselberghe was born in Ghent, Belgium, and was a leading painter in the pointillist style, which uses tiny dots of color. He painted portraits and summer landscapes. He spent his last years on the French Riviera. He died in 1926.

Q649390.bio: Carl Gustaf Pilo was born in Sweden in 1711 and worked for many years as a court painter in Denmark before moving to Stockholm. He painted portraits of royalty, and started a large painting of the coronation of King Gustav III. He died in 1793.

Q266415.bio: Isidor Kaufmann was born in Arad, then part of Hungary, to a Jewish family and trained in Vienna. He is best known for his warm, realistic portraits of Jewish people and religious scenes in Eastern Europe. He lived and worked in Vienna for much of his life. He died there in 1921.

Q93708.bio: Adolph Northen was a German painter born in Hann. Münden in 1828. He studied in Düsseldorf and became known for dramatic paintings of Napoleon's campaigns in Russia and of Prussian history. He died in Düsseldorf in 1876.

Q274298.bio: Edouard Louis Dubufe was born in Paris to a family of painters. He painted portraits and historical scenes for the French court and nobility. He was a successful society painter in the era of Napoleon III. He died in 1883.

Q7780.bio: Fra Bartolomeo was an Italian painter born in Prato in 1472 who lived in Florence. He became a Dominican friar after the death of his friend and hero Savonarola, and painted calm, majestic altarpieces. He died in Florence in 1517.

Q1273537.bio: Ephraim Moses Lilien was born in Drohobych, in the region of Galicia, then part of Austria, and grew up in a Jewish family. He studied art in Kraków and Munich, and later lived in Berlin. He was an early artist of the Zionist movement and illustrated books with beautiful Art Nouveau designs. He died in Germany in 1925.

Q3155327.bio: Isidore Stanislas Helman was a French engraver born in Lille in 1743. He moved to Paris, where he engraved scenes of the French Revolution after the paintings of other artists, and his prints were widely sold.

Q44032.bio: Egon Schiele was born in Tulln, Austria, and studied art in Vienna as a teenager. He was inspired by Gustav Klimt and developed a raw, angular and expressive drawing style. He lived in Vienna and in smaller Austrian towns. He died of the Spanish flu in 1918 at just 28, three days after his wife.

Q77132.bio: Albert Bierstadt was born in Germany and raised in Massachusetts. He traveled west with survey expeditions and painted vast landscapes of the Rocky Mountains and Yosemite. His work was admired by huge crowds in the East. He lived in New York and died there in 1902.

Q375926.bio: Rembrandt Peale was an American painter born in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, in 1778, the son of the painter Charles Willson Peale. He painted portraits of Thomas Jefferson and George Washington, and lived in Philadelphia, where he died in 1860.

Q183245.bio: George Frederic Watts was born in London and trained as a sculptor and painter. He painted portraits of the great and the good, as well as symbolic works on big themes like Hope and Love. In his later years he lived in the English village of Compton, where his gallery still stands. He died in 1904.

Q123757.bio: Jean-Étienne Liotard was born in Geneva, Switzerland, and traveled across Europe and to Constantinople. He is best known for pastel portraits with a precise, glowing look. He worked for royals and nobles in Vienna, Paris and England. He died in Geneva in 1789.

Q2965652.bio: Christian Skredsvig was a Norwegian painter and writer born in Modum in 1854, who studied in Paris and lived in Eggedal. His paintings show Norwegian farm life and rural people in soft light. He also wrote stories and novels. He died in 1924.

Q206820.bio: Anders Zorn was born in the Swedish region of Dalarna and became one of the most famous painters of his time. He was a master of watercolor and painted portraits of presidents, including Theodore Roosevelt. He made a home in Mora, Sweden, where his house is now a museum. He died in 1920.

Q34013.bio: Georges Seurat was born in Paris and studied at the École des Beaux-Arts. He invented pointillism, painting with tiny dots of pure color that blend in the viewer's eye. He worked slowly and carefully in his studio, making many sketches before big paintings. He died suddenly at only 31, leaving behind just a handful of masterpieces.

Q6238971.bio: John Henry Walker was an Irish-born illustrator, born in County Antrim in 1831, who moved to Canada. He lived in Montreal, where he drew historical and city scenes for books and newspapers, and he died there in 1899.

Q952938.bio: Ogata Kōrin was born in Kyoto into a rich family of fabric merchants and became one of Japan's greatest decorative painters. He founded the Rinpa style of bold shapes and gold leaf. His folding screens, such as 'Red and White Plum Blossoms', are national treasures. He died in Kyoto in 1716.

Q56660294.bio: Eugène Hamel was born in Quebec City and became a Canadian painter and a portrait artist. He painted people of Wendake and other communities, as well as religious paintings. He lived most of his life in Quebec. He died in 1932.

Q23380.bio: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was born in Montauban, in southern France, and trained under David in Paris. He spent many years in Italy and in the end died in Paris. He believed in the power of clean, elegant outlines and was a master of portraits. He was also a fine violin player, and the phrase 'Ingres's violin' came to mean a talented hobby.

Q271470.bio: Oda Krohg was born in Oslo and was a painter who became a leading figure of the Norwegian bohemian circle. She studied in Paris and Germany. She was married to the painter Christian Krohg. She died in Oslo in 1935.

Q734843.bio: Jean Le Tavernier was a painter and manuscript illuminator from Oudenaarde in Flanders, active between about 1434 and 1462. He worked in Brussels for the dukes of Burgundy, especially Philip the Good, painting richly detailed pictures in their chronicles and prayer books.

x-florentine-painter.bio: This picture was painted by an unknown Florentine artist, shortly after the events it shows, in the 1490s. Many Florentine workshops made pictures for sale, and artists did not always sign them.

Q3382963.bio: Pierre-Denis Martin was a French painter born in Paris in 1663. He painted battle scenes, including some for the Russian court in the 1720s, and spent his life in Paris, where he died in 1742.

Q216999.bio: Antoine-Jean Gros was born in Paris and was a student of Jacques-Louis David. He became Napoleon's war painter, traveling with the army to capture battles and heroic scenes. His lively, dramatic art influenced the Romantic painters. He died in 1835 near Paris.

Q37693.bio: Paul Gauguin was born in Paris and spent part of childhood in Peru. He worked as a stockbroker before turning to painting full-time. He lived in Brittany, in Arles with Van Gogh, and then in Tahiti and the Marquesas Islands in the South Pacific, seeking a simpler life. His flat, vivid colors influenced Picasso and Matisse.

Q3695965.bio: Robert Walter Weir was an American painter born in New Rochelle, New York, in 1803. He taught drawing for more than forty years at the military academy at West Point and painted the Embarkation of the Pilgrims in the US Capitol. He died in New York City in 1889.

Q457976.bio: Nikolai Ge was born in Voronezh, Russia, and studied in Saint Petersburg and Italy. He painted powerful scenes from history and religion with dramatic light and strong emotion. Later in life he lived on a farm in Ukraine. He died in 1894.

Q5944348.bio: José María Obregón was born in Mexico City and studied at the Academy of San Carlos. He painted historical scenes, including 'The Discovery of Pulque', and was a leading artist in his country. He died in 1902.

Q680528.bio: Joseph Légaré was born in Quebec City and was one of the first painters in Canada to paint landscapes and historical events. He collected European paintings and taught himself by copying them. He was also a politician and a businessman. He died in 1855.

Q1763678.bio: Henry Holiday was born in London and was a painter, designer and stained-glass artist. He was influenced by the Pre-Raphaelites. He also illustrated Lewis Carroll's poem 'The Hunting of the Snark'. He died in London in 1927.

Q727869.bio: Gustaaf Wappers was born in Antwerp and became the leading Belgian Romantic history painter. He painted scenes of the Belgian Revolution of 1830. He lived in Brussels and Paris. He died in Paris in 1874.

Q240526.bio: Lawrence Alma-Tadema was born in a village in the Netherlands and settled in London, England, in 1870. He became famous for sunny paintings of ancient Rome and Greece, filled with marble, flowers, and sea views. He was knighted and extremely popular during his lifetime. He died in Wiesbaden, Germany, in 1912.

Q159297.bio: John Constable was born in East Bergholt, in the English county of Suffolk, where his father owned mills.
