paintings.why: A dying miser lies in bed while Death stands in the doorway and a demon tempts him with a bag of money. Hieronymus Bosch painted this around 1500 to show how nothing can be taken to the grave, a popular message after the long years of plague.

The goddess Diana rests after her bath, with a servant tending to her feet and hunting gear scattered around. Boucher painted soft pink skin and silky fabric, in the playful French Rococo style. It is full of charm and decorative detail. It was owned by the French king's circle.

A giant goat stands in the dark in front of a crowd of witches with sallow faces. Goya painted it on his wall in his 70s. It may be about fear and superstition. It's among his strange, shadowy 'Black Paintings.'

paintings.t: Greece on the Ruins of Missolonghi
paintings.why: A woman, a symbol of Greece, stretches out her arms among ruins after a terrible siege during the Greek War of Independence. Delacroix painted it to raise money for the Greek cause. It's a cry for help made in paint. It shows how art can speak about real events.

paintings.t: The Execution of Lady Jane Grey
paintings.why: A blindfolded young queen feels for the block as she is about to be beheaded. Jane Grey was queen of England for nine days in 1553 and was only a teenager. Delaroche painted the moment with a hush that makes it moving. When it was shown in 1834, crowds were moved to tears.

A couple and their baby, huddled under a big umbrella, look out at the sea as they emigrate, leaving England behind. Brown based it on a friend who was leaving for Australia. The colors are painted outdoors in raw daylight, in a round frame. It's an emotional picture about leaving home.

Jesus stands at night in a garden with a lantern, knocking at an overgrown door that has no handle on the outside. Hunt painted it to show that you must open your heart from the inside. It toured the world and was seen by millions. It's one of the most reproduced religious paintings ever.

A wealthy lady in a pale flowered dress sits with an amazing calm gaze, in a gleaming gilt room. Ingres painted her twice; this is the seated one, with her chin on her hand. He labored for years to get the textures of silk and jewels perfect. It's one of the greatest portraits of the 1800s.

paintings.t: Symphony in White, No. 1: The White Girl
paintings.why: A young woman in a long white dress stands on a white fur rug against a white curtain. Whistler wanted a painting of harmony in color, like music. The model was Joanna Hiffernan, his partner. It was rejected from the Salon but exhibited at the 'Salon of the Rejected.'

A group of people gather around a violinist in a poor quarter of Paris, including children and a man in a top hat. Manet borrowed figures from old master paintings to tell a modern tale. The painting is about poor people on the edges of society, treated with respect. It's an early work showing his big ambitions.

A young woman in a flowing white summer dress stands in a sunny garden with her parasol and fresh flowers. Monet painted it in 1867, with strong contrast between light and shadow. Some experts think it was painted from the same model as 'Women in the Garden'. It's an early example of Impressionist sunshine.

A young woman in a white dress stands beneath a shady parasol, with sunlight sneaking in through the leaves. The model was Lise Tréhot, Renoir's girlfriend and favorite model. The Salon accepted it in 1868, and it was a hit. The dappled light is a hint of Renoir's later Impressionism.

paintings.t: Berthe Morisot with a Bouquet of Violets
paintings.why: A woman in black with large, dark eyes looks out, a small bunch of violets pinned to her dress. Berthe Morisot was a painter herself and Manet's friend. This is one of the most compelling portraits of an artist by another. She later married Manet's brother.

In the legend of King Arthur, the wizard Merlin is tricked by the enchantress Nimue into a trance. Burne-Jones painted the pair among a dark and tangled forest. The rich colors and details are like a medieval tapestry. It's a prime example of Victorian fantasy art.

A young woman in a flowery hat and a fresh dress stands in a garden of green. Manet painted it near the end of his life when he was ill. The model, actress Jeanne Demarsy, represents the season. It's a happy picture of renewal.

A smiling woman in a pink dress and straw hat twirls with a man in a straw boater, in a crowd of happy dancers. Renoir's wife Aline, who was his model, appears in one of the dance scenes. He painted it as a companion to the city dance scene. It's a joyous moment.

A man in a dark suit sweeps a woman in a long white ballgown across the dance floor, tropical plants behind them. Renoir painted this as a companion to his country dance painting, contrasting the formal and the casual. The woman is Suzanne Valadon, who became a famous painter. It's a chic image of city life.

A dark and empty ocean stretches to the horizon, with strange curls of cloud and one small ray of sun. Watts painted it as the end of the great Flood from the Bible, with no people in sight. It's a mysterious picture of nature before humans. It looks almost modern.

In the Bible, Adam and Eve are overcome with grief over their son Abel, who has died at the hand of his brother Cain. Bouguereau's painting is moving because of the tenderness of the mother cradling her son. It was done with the smooth, polished style he was famous for. It makes the first sadness in human history feel real.
l: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina

paintings.why: A young girl in a rough dress stands in a field with sheep in the background, gazing directly out. Bouguereau often painted peasant children in soft light. His technique makes the skin glow and the fabrics look real. The painting was popular with collectors in America and Europe.

Van Gogh's face looks intense and slightly orange against swirling blue-green strokes. This is one of his last self-portraits, painted in 1889. It's one of the only paintings he made without a beard. It sold for a record price in 1998.

Prisoners walk in a circle in a high-walled courtyard, with no way out. Van Gogh painted this in an asylum in 1890, copying an illustration by Gustave Doré. Many viewers feel he was thinking of his own confinement. The painting is a deep expression of being trapped.

A brooding, sad winged demon sits in a mountain landscape, with eyes full of longing. Vrubel was inspired by a poem by Lermontov. The faceted, mosaic-like paint looks like jewels. It became a great symbol of Russian art.

A tiger crouches amid lashing leaves, rain and lightning, hunting its prey. Rousseau's first jungle painting wasn't based on a real jungle trip but on books and plant gardens. The result is fantastically vivid. It made the art world see his 'naive' style as magical.
paintings.k: Feel the wind in the leaves! Where do you see the lightning flash?

paintings.why: A young Tahitian girl lies on a bed, looking back with fear, while a ghostly figure watches from behind. The title means 'the spirit of the dead is watching.' Gauguin painted it in Tahiti, mixing local beliefs with his own imagination. The bold, flat color helped inspire later modern art.

Guests of the famous Paris nightclub gather around a table, with a woman in the foreground lit with a ghostly green face. Toulouse-Lautrec was a regular there and painted the real people he knew. He flattened the space and used strong color. It's one of the most famous images of Paris nightlife.

A mother or nurse gently bathes a little girl's feet in a basin, seen from high above. Cassatt was influenced by Japanese prints and used simple shapes and bold lines. The tender moment between the two is full of warmth. It's among the most famous works by an American Impressionist.
paintings.k: What do you think the little girl is thinking?

paintings.why: A woman wraps her red hair and arms around a man, her head against his neck. Munch called it 'Love and Pain' at first. Other people thought it looked like a vampire, so the name stuck. It is one of his best-known works about the complexity of love.

paintings.t: Truth Coming Out of Her Well
paintings.why: The figure of Truth emerges from a well, holding a whip to punish liars. Gérôme painted this near the end of his life as a response to critics who disliked him. It's allegory, a picture in which a person stands for an idea. It's a funny and bold painting.

A baby, a young mother and an old woman appear together in Klimt's gold-and-pattern style. The painting shows the cycle of life. It won a gold medal at an exhibition in Rome. The old woman at the side shows Klimt's honest view of aging.
l: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea di Roma

paintings.why: A young woman with red hair and a black dress sits sideways, looking out in a thoughtful way. Schiele painted his model Wally Neuzil, who lived with him in Vienna. After World War II, the painting was involved in a long legal fight about stolen art. It ended in 2010.

A woman in a bold pattern of red and gold looks out with a graceful pose, holding a fan. It was one of Klimt's last portraits, painted in 1917, shortly before his death. It was rediscovered in 2023 and sold for around $85 million. Its bright palette and decoration show his later style.

A young woman with a long neck, tilted head and almond-shaped eyes sits in a simple blue-and-black dress. Modigliani painted this in 1918, near the end of his short life. The elongated style is his signature. It is a graceful example of his gentle, calm portraits.

Five men present a document to a room full of delegates in Philadelphia in 1776. Trumbull, who had served in the Revolution, painted it with portraits from life, hoping to get faces right. It's the image of the Declaration signing that many Americans know, and it appears on the two-dollar bill. It hangs in the U.S. Capitol Rotunda today.

Two men stand under twisted oak trees and gaze at the glowing crescent moon in the evening sky. Friedrich painted himself and a student or friend. The scene is quiet and thoughtful. It's a favorite Romantic image of friendship and wonder.

paintings.t: Salisbury Cathedral from the Bishop's Grounds
paintings.why: The spire of the cathedral rises into a stormy sky, framed by a dark arch of trees. Constable painted it for his friend the Bishop of Salisbury. There's a rainbow, which he used to show hope. It's a masterpiece of English landscape painting.

The god of war, Mars, is gently disarmed by Venus, goddess of love, as cupids remove his weapons. David painted it at the end of his career, when he was in exile in Brussels. The message, 'make love, not war', feels timeless. It's grand and calm in style.
l: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

paintings.why: A young girl sits alone in a graveyard, eyes wide and shoulders hunched, her face lit by a pale light. Delacroix painted it as a study for a larger work about misery and suffering. The fear and sadness in her large dark eyes feel startlingly real. It's one of the great emotional portraits of Romanticism.

A wedding party rows a boat full of people in traditional costume across a fjord, with mountains behind them. Tidemand painted the figures and Gude painted the landscape — a team effort. It became an icon of Norwegian identity. It's famous for making the country's culture proud.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A great valley in Ecuador, with waterfalls, mountain peaks, tiny villagers and tropical plants. Church painted this huge canvas after trips to South America. In 1859 New Yorkers paid to see it, and crowds used binoculars to look at details. It made him famous.

Monet planned this huge picnic scene as a challenge to Manet's famous painting of the same name, but this time with well-dressed friends in the forest. He worked on it outdoors in 1865–66, then left it unfinished and later cut it up; only pieces and the sketch survive. Dappled sunlight on the tablecloth made it a ground-breaking study of light. It shows how ambitious the young Impressionists were.

The writer Émile Zola sits at his desk surrounded by objects that tell us about him: a pamphlet by Manet's supporter, a Japanese print and an image of Olympia. Zola had defended Manet in print when critics attacked him. Manet painted this as a thank you. It's a portrait of friendship.

A huge pile of skulls stands in a barren desert, with crows circling above. Vereshchagin dedicated it 'to all conquerors, past, present and future.' He had seen war himself and wanted to show its cost. It's one of the most famous anti-war paintings.

A woman with closed eyes sits with her head tilted back, while a bird drops a poppy into her hands. Rossetti painted it after the death of his wife Elizabeth Siddal. The figure is Beatrice from Dante's poems. It's a picture of love and grief.

A woman holds a pomegranate, with a dark and sorrowful gaze. In the Roman myth, Proserpine ate pomegranate seeds in the underworld and was forced to return for part of each year. Rossetti's muse Jane Morris was the model. It's a symbol of winter and longing.

paintings.t: Nocturne in Black and Gold – The Falling Rocket
paintings.why: Fireworks fizzle in a dark sky above a London park. Whistler painted it with a few dabs, and the critic John Ruskin said he was 'flinging a pot of paint in the public's face.' Whistler sued him for libel and won a farthing in damages. It started a famous argument about what art should be.

A woman sits in a Paris café, a plum on the table in front of her, deep in thought. Manet painted it in the last years of his life. The painting is about waiting and thinking. It's famous for capturing a mood.

A huge crowd of people, rich and poor, follow a sacred icon down a dusty road under a hot sun. Repin painted hundreds of figures, and each one has a different face and story. The painting took him years, and he traveled to villages for sketches. It's a panorama of 19th-century Russia.

A woman in a shawl and dress sits with a basket of oranges on her lap, selling fruit in Warsaw. Gierymski painted her with great care and sympathy. It was a rare picture that gave a poor street vendor the dignity of a portrait. It's one of the most beloved Polish paintings.

A couple twirl across a café terrace — the man in a straw boater and the woman in a red-trimmed dress and hat. Renoir's model was Suzanne Valadon, who became a famous painter herself. The painting is full of energy, and her flushed cheeks are lifelike. It's one of the best-known dance paintings.

Young men relax and swim from a wooden platform at a pond. Eakins painted friends and students, and himself swimming in the water at the right. He was also a talented photographer and used it to study movement. It's a famous picture of American life.
l: Amon Carter Museum of American Art

paintings.why: Three models in a studio, shown in front, back and side views, with Seurat's own giant painting behind them. He used dots of color to prove that his method works for indoor scenes. The picture is partly a response to critics. It's a clever, calm and quiet painting.

Red poppies and blue cornflowers burst from a vase in a bright burst of color. Van Gogh painted this when he lived in Paris, discovering brighter colors from his Impressionist friends. The lively brushstrokes fill the canvas. In 2010, it was stolen from a museum in Cairo, and it's still missing.
l: Stolen from the Mohamed Mahmoud Khalil Museum in Cairo in 2010 and still missing

paintings.why: A young Japanese girl sits on a chair, with a flower in her hand, in a patterned jacket and a green and orange background. Van Gogh was obsessed with Japanese art, though he had never been to Japan. The word 'mousmé' was something he learned from a novel. It's a vibrant, joyful portrait.

A green Christ on the cross is shown in a Breton landscape, as women in traditional caps mourn. Gauguin used flat, symbolic color, in contrast to realistic painting. It's also called 'The Breton Calvary.' It's a key example of his style, known as Synthetism.
l: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

paintings.why: Crowds stream down the steps of Warsaw's Royal Castle to celebrate the first modern written constitution in Europe. Matejko painted it to remind Poles of their proud past when Poland was ruled by foreign powers. People throng the stairs and cheer. It's a symbol of hope and freedom for Poland.

A woman in a feathered hat and dress is painted with wild green, orange and purple stripes across her face. When Matisse showed it in 1905, critics were shocked and called the group 'les fauves' — 'the wild beasts.' He wanted color to express feelings, not match reality. It changed how modern artists thought about color.
l: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art

paintings.why: A family walks together in the countryside in warm, glowing sunlight. Sorolla was a master at painting light, especially bright, sunny scenes. His mix of loose brushwork and joyful mood made him famous in Spain and beyond. He painted it in Spain in 1909.

A group of young women float in a swirl of colorful patterns and flowers, as if dreaming. Klimt painted this when he was 51, using bright reds, blues and golds. The figures seem to melt into one another and into the decoration. It's famous for its dazzling rhythm.

A simple red rectangle tilts on a white background. Malevich called it 'a peasant woman in two dimensions.' It was part of his radical art movement, Suprematism. It's a milestone in the story of abstract art.

A slightly tilted white square floats on a white background. Malevich wanted to make pictures with no objects, only pure feeling. It's one of the most radical paintings ever created. People still discuss what it means and whether it's art.

A young man falls into Havana harbor while swimming and is attacked by a shark, and sailors desperately try to rescue him. Brook Watson, the real victim, lost a leg but later became Lord Mayor of London. Copley painted the tense moment with dramatic action. It's a thrilling, true-life adventure.

A young woman is nervously kissed by a lover, while a secret meeting is happening in a room full of beautiful satin. Fragonard and Gérard worked together on this scene of intrigue. The shiny dress is dazzling. It's a classic 18th-century romantic painting.

A man in black glides across an icy pond on one leg, arms crossed, wearing a black hat. Reverend Robert Walker was a member of a skating club in Edinburgh. Raeburn painted him in a lively pose, which made the portrait famous. It is one of the most popular paintings in Scotland.

A woman in a simple white gown reclines on a long Greek-style sofa in an empty room. David left it unfinished, and Madame Récamier was so annoyed that she hired another artist. The simple lines and clean look are ahead of their time. It's one of the most famous portraits of the 1800s.

paintings.t: Bonaparte Visiting the Plague Victims of Jaffa
paintings.why: Napoleon reaches out to touch a sick soldier during a plague outbreak in 1799, as others reel in fear. Gros painted it to show a brave leader, though the story is partly propaganda. The exotic setting with its arches and light is dramatic. It's a turning point from Neoclassical to Romantic painting.

The goddess Venus rises from the sea, wringing out her hair, as little cupids flutter around her. Ingres began this painting in the 1800s, and he finished it in 1848, in his sixties. It's a picture of a classic myth in a smooth, graceful style. It still hangs in a museum in Chantilly, France.

A rainbow glows over a misty mountain valley, with a cross on a rock. Friedrich painted nature as something sacred. The soft, delicate light makes it feel peaceful. It's an early example of his Romantic style.

A gigantic figure rises behind a mountain in the dusk as the tiny people below flee in fear. Goya's inspiration may be war or fear. Because experts now question whether he painted it, it's still a mystery. It's one of the most mysterious images in art.

A heavy-set man sits with his hands on his knees and a powerful gaze. Louis-François Bertin was the editor of a major newspaper, and Ingres captured his strong personality. When it was shown in 1833, it was admired as an image of the rising middle class. Edgar Degas later called it the portrait of the new age.

An architect lies on a giant column, dreaming of a huge city of classical buildings from all over the world. Cole painted it for an architect friend. It's a fantasy of great architecture. It's one of the most imaginative American paintings of its time.

A young man sits against a tree, half-conscious, with a sword by his side and blood on his shirt. Courbet painted himself in this dramatic role when he was 25. He changed the painting years later, removing a woman who was originally beside him. It's an early picture showing his ambition.

paintings.t: The Appearance of Christ Before the People
paintings.why: A crowd in the Roman Empire gathers by a river to hear John the Baptist, as Jesus approaches in the distance. Alexander Ivanov spent about 20 years painting it in Rome. He studied people from all backgrounds. It's one of Russia's most important religious paintings.

Huge powerful horses rear and parade at a horse market in Paris, held by their handlers. Bonheur sketched at the market for 18 months, even dressing in men's clothes to blend in. The painting is more than 5 meters wide. It made her an international star and the greatest animal painter of her day.
paintings.k: See how many horses are rearing up. Which one looks the strongest?

paintings.why: A man in a long black cape and top hat stands by a wall with an empty bottle beside him. Manet painted a ragpicker of Paris as if he were a noble. The Salon rejected it in 1859. It was his first major painting and shows an early sympathy for ordinary people.

A man in a Spanish costume sits on a bench, strumming a guitar, with his legs crossed. Manet's first big success, shown in the 1861 Salon, with strong light and dark. Critics admired its life-like quality. It's among his best works from the early period.

A young woman sits beside a mountain stream in a forest, with the cool, clear water flowing around her. Courbet painted her as a real person instead of an idealized goddess. The forest and water glisten. It's a rare nature scene painted with the same care as a portrait.

A young woman in a pink dress sits with her back turned, gazing at a village on a sunlit hill in southern France. Bazille painted it for his family, using bold light in the open air. The style looks forward to Impressionism. It's among his most famous works.

A group of Scandinavian artists in Rome gather in a tavern, laughing, drinking and playing music. Bloch lived in Rome as a student and painted his friends. It's lively and warm. It shows what the lives of young artists were like.

Napoleon, still a young general, sits on his horse before the Great Sphinx in Egypt. Gérôme painted the face of the Sphinx as if the two are staring at each other. The scene has a mysterious, silent feel. It's a famous image of the clash of old and new.

A hunter pulls a deer from a stream in a snowy forest, with a hunting horn and hound beside him. Courbet loved his native forest and painted many hunt scenes. The dark, rich shadows and glittering water show his skill. It's a bold, realistic image of country life.
l: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon

paintings.why: People in rowing boats and bathers fill a floating café in a bend of the Seine near Paris. Monet and Renoir painted side by side at this popular spot in 1869, inventing the Impressionist style. The water is painted with dabs of light and color. It's a landmark in art history.

A man and woman stroll in a sunlit wooded park, followed by a child, light dappled across her pale dress. Renoir painted this in 1870, before the Franco-Prussian War. It's an early example of his love of sunlit scenes. It reveals his talent for capturing a happy moment.

paintings.t: Self-Portrait with Death Playing the Fiddle
paintings.why: The painter pauses at his easel, as a skeleton with a one-stringed fiddle whispers in his ear. Böcklin painted this as a reminder that life is short and art is precious. The skeleton is slightly funny and slightly spooky. It's an important painting of Symbolism.

paintings.t: Astronomer Copernicus, or Conversations with God
paintings.why: A scholar stands on a balcony at night with a telescope and instruments, gazing at the sky. Matejko painted Nicolaus Copernicus, who showed that the Earth goes around the Sun. The painting celebrates a Polish genius. It's a tribute to curiosity and bold ideas.

Bathers splash in the water near a floating café on the Seine, painted with quick, sparkling dabs of paint. Renoir and Monet worked side by side here in 1869, and both made paintings of it. The water is painted in lively color. It's one of the first Impressionist paintings.

A girl with long red hair and bright blue eyes sits in a luxurious blue-and-white dress. Renoir painted her when she was eight, the daughter of a rich banker. Her family wasn't pleased with the picture and hung it in a back hall. Today it's treasured as one of his best portraits.

paintings.t: The Daughters of Edward Darley Boit
paintings.why: Four sisters pose in a tall, dark entry hall with huge Japanese vases — one on the floor, others standing in shadow. Sargent painted them at different distances, so the room feels deep and strange. Some people see it as a mysterious, dreamlike picture. It's one of the most famous American portraits.

Van Gogh sits at his easel, painting a vase of sunflowers, while Gauguin watches closely. Gauguin painted this picture when they lived together in Arles. Van Gogh said it looked like him, 'but gone mad.' It's a rare picture of one great artist painting another.

paintings.t: Memory of the Garden at Etten
paintings.why: Two women stroll in a garden of dahlias and flowers, remembering the garden where Van Gogh's family lived in the Netherlands. He painted it from memory in Arles, thinking of his mother and sister. The colors are bold and dreamlike. It's a tender family memory.

An elderly woman sits with her hands folded in a dark dress. Van Gogh painted it in 1888 from a black-and-white photograph. He used bold greens and reds to make it more alive. It's an affectionate portrait of the mother he loved.

Twisted roots and trunks spread across a forest bank, painted in swirling green, yellow and brown. It's thought to be the last painting Van Gogh made, in July 1890. The roots look alive, as if reaching for something. It's one of his most vivid late works.

Nude figures lounge, dance and play music in a meadow in bright, wild colors. Matisse painted it as a vision of a golden age, a paradise. The flat shapes and flowing lines were revolutionary. It changed the course of modern art.

paintings.t: The Dessert: Harmony in Red (The Red Room)
paintings.why: A woman arranges fruit and wine on a table in a room where everything is red: the walls and the tablecloth blend, patterned with blue vines. Matisse first painted it in blue and then changed it to red. The flat patterns and strong color changed how artists treat space. It's a landmark of modern art.

A skeleton in a dark robe stands beside a heap of people of all ages, wrapped up in dazzling, colorful patterns. Klimt painted the circle of life, with Death and the living side by side. It won a prize in Rome and Klimt later repainted it. It's a thoughtful picture about life's cycle.

paintings.t: Erasistratus Discovering the Cause of Antiochus' Disease
paintings.why: A doctor figures out that a prince is sick with love, as the prince's stepmother stands nearby. David painted it to win the Prix de Rome, the top art prize in France, in 1774. The clear composition and strong emotions won him the prize. It launched his career.

paintings.t: Portrait of a Lady in Blue
paintings.why: A woman in a shimmering blue gown, with a feathery hat, looks out at us with a gentle smile. Gainsborough painted with fluttery strokes that make the silk glow. We don't know who she is, but she has captured the world's attention. It is one of the best-loved portraits of the 18th century.

A little boy in a bright red suit holds a string tied to a pet magpie, while three cats watch with wide, hungry eyes. Goya painted him as a small child of a noble family. The cats lurk in the shadows, a hint at danger. It's among the most charming and beloved portraits of a child.
paintings.k: The boy has a pet bird. Count the cats watching it.

paintings.t: The Lictors Bring to Brutus the Bodies of His Sons
paintings.why: A Roman leader sits in the shadows, brooding, as his sons' bodies are carried in because he condemned them for treason. His wife and daughters are in anguish. David showed the hard cost of duty. It was exhibited in 1789 as the French Revolution began.

paintings.t: Portrait of Doña Isabel de Porcel
paintings.why: A confident woman in black lace stands with her hands on her hips, framed by a dark background. Goya painted this in 1805. The portrait is wonderfully direct and strong. It's one of the finest of his female portraits.

A cross rises on a mountaintop, surrounded by evergreen trees and glowing light. Friedrich painted it as an altarpiece, but it was more of a landscape than a typical religious painting, which caused a huge argument. It showed that nature could be a way to feel God. It was one of the most debated paintings of its time.

A young man faces a monster with a woman's head and a lion's body, who asks riddles of travelers. In the Greek legend, Oedipus solved the riddle and saved the city of Thebes. Ingres painted it as a student in Rome. It's a young artist's tribute to classical stories.

Queen Dido oversees the building of the city of Carthage by a glittering harbor in the golden light of sunrise. Turner was inspired by the paintings of Claude Lorrain, whom he admired. He wanted his work hung next to Claude's, and it still hangs there in the National Gallery. It is among the most beautiful sunrises in art.

A woman in a dress sits on a donkey, with a patch of light on her face, riding to market in Bordeaux. Goya painted this in exile near the end of his life, at age 80. The loose brushstrokes made him a forerunner of the Impressionists. It shows his youthful spirit even in old age.

The hero Ulysses is tied to the mast of his ship so that he can listen to the sirens' song without crashing into rocks. His sailors have their ears plugged with wax. Etty painted the swirl of sea nymphs in a tangle of sea and sky. It's a retelling of an adventure from the Odyssey.

A ship sails off into a fiery red sunset on a stormy sea, while in the foreground chains and the legs of drowning people float in the waves. Turner was inspired by a true story, in which enslaved people were thrown overboard. He used blazing colors to make people feel the horror of the slave trade. It's a powerful reminder that art can speak out against cruelty.

A young man tears at his hair, his eyes wide, staring straight at us. Courbet painted himself in an exaggerated expression of shock and fear, perhaps acting like a character on a stage. It was his early way to show he could paint strong emotions. It has become one of his best-known self-portraits.

paintings.t: Young Greeks Attending a Cock Fight
paintings.why: Young men and women in ancient Greece watch two roosters fighting. Gérôme's first big success at the Salon in 1847. He imagined the scene based on his studies of ancient Greece. The painting launched his career.

A family sits at a long dinner table, and the two lovers, Isabella and Lorenzo, are at the center, their feelings hidden. Millais based it on a poem by Keats, and he used his friends and family as models. He painted every detail with great sharpness, which was a daring approach in 1849. It marks the beginning of the Pre-Raphaelite movement.

Teams of strong white oxen pull ploughs through brown earth in central France. Bonheur spent time on farms, studying the animals. The painting was bought by the French government. It's a landmark in realistic animal painting.

A woman jumps up from her lover's lap in a fancy room, as if she suddenly realizes something. Hunt packed the painting with symbols, like a cat chasing a bird. He wanted to teach a moral lesson, in the Victorian way. It's famous for its fine detail.

Four girls in an orchard at twilight burn piles of fallen leaves, with a glowing red sky behind. Millais painted the smoky sunset after a quiet autumn evening in Scotland. The painting is about the passing of seasons and of time. It's known for its subtle glow.

A nymph, startled in a woodland pool, looks out at someone who has surprised her. Manet painted it as a young man, studying the old masters. It's an unusual painting in his early style. It shows how he began by learning from the past.
l: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina

paintings.why: A woman lies back on a bed in a quiet room, painted with soft light. Courbet was a Realist who painted real people, not fairy-tale goddesses. It shows his skill with textures and light. It's an example of his straightforward style.

A rolled-up carpet is unrolled at Julius Caesar's feet, and out peeks Cleopatra. The story says she was smuggled into his palace this way. Gérôme painted the moment of surprise in rich detail. It's a dramatic episode from ancient history.

Sailboats with white sails and flags dot a bright blue sea, as spectators in small boats watch the races. Monet painted the Normandy coast in simple blocks of bright color. The flat shapes show the influence of Japanese prints. It's a cheerful picture of a summer day by the sea.
A teenage girl with a baby on her lap smiles in a green meadow. Bouguereau's soft-focus style was widely loved. The baby plays with her hair. It's a tender picture of family.

paintings.t: Portrait of the actress Jeanne Samary
paintings.why: A smiling young woman in a gown of white and rose holds a smile that seems about to turn into a laugh. Jeanne Samary was a Comédie-Française actress and a friend of Renoir. His colors dance across the dress and the background. It's a lovely, lively portrait.

paintings.t: Morning of the Execution of the Streltsy
paintings.why: On Red Square in Moscow in 1698, Peter the Great watches as rebel soldiers, the Streltsy, are about to be executed. Surikov painted the crowds in a clash of faces and colors. The tension makes you feel as if you're in the crowd. It is one of the great Russian history paintings.
A man and woman sit in a sunny garden arbour, shaded by leaves. Gierymski painted the light dappling their faces. The work is relaxed and natural. It's a treasure of Polish art.

Fields of tulips and bulbs make broad stripes of color across the flat Dutch landscape, with a village in the distance. Van Gogh painted this in 1883 in the Netherlands, when his palette was still dark. The pattern of stripes anticipates his bolder style. It's a bright patch of flowers.

A young woman lies in the snow with a white dove rising from her lips, as a group of people gather at the back. Saint Eulalia was a young Christian girl from Spain who was martyred, according to legend. Waterhouse painted her peaceful face as the dove symbolizes her spirit. It is a haunting picture of courage.

A blindfolded woman sits on a globe, playing a lyre with one string left. In the dim, starry sky a single star shines. Watts painted this as a message about holding on to hope in hard times. It inspired later leaders, and a famous 2004 speech used its title.

A tall Pierrot and a Harlequin in costume stride arm in arm in a carnival masquerade. Cézanne's son Paul and a friend posed for it. The stiff, theater-like figures make a lively picture. It shows how Cézanne painted with simple shapes and blocks of color.

paintings.t: Harvest at La Crau, with Montmajour in the Background
paintings.why: A golden wheat field stretches across the plain under a blue sky, with farmers and wagons working in the sun. Van Gogh painted it in just a few days in June 1888, in the heat of the south of France. The colors are those of his beloved Provence. It's a bright celebration of harvest.

A small figure walks across a snowy field with a fence, with a peaceful purple-blue wash of color beyond. Van Gogh was fascinated by the winter in Arles. The painting uses crisp, simple lines like a Japanese print. It's a calm scene.

Waves of green wheat ripple around a tall cypress, against a swirling sky. Van Gogh painted it in the south of France at an asylum. Cypresses, to him, were as beautiful as Egyptian obelisks. It's a joyful, energetic image of nature.

Two cherubic children stand cheek to cheek, Cupid with wings and Psyche, holding a butterfly. Bouguereau retold a Roman myth of love in his sweet, polished style. It was extremely popular with collectors. It's an enchanting picture.

A Tahitian woman carries a child on her shoulder, with a glowing halo, as the angel greets them. The title means 'Hail Mary' in the Tahitian language. Gauguin blended Christian images with island life. It's a bright and unusual Nativity.

Women lie and sit in the sun on a Tahitian beach, with the sea behind. The title means 'What! Are you jealous?' Gauguin used flat areas of strong color. The picture is a colorful reflection of island life.

A sorceress leans over a pool, pouring poison into the water to turn her rival into a sea monster. Waterhouse captured the magic glowing in the water. Her swirling green robes are painted in vivid colors. It's a story from Greek mythology made vivid.
A woman sits reading in a quiet room, painted in warm yellows and browns. It is an early work by Matisse, painted before his famous wild colors. It's a calm moment of quiet concentration.

A woman's face is split by a vibrant green stripe down the nose, set against pink, orange and purple backgrounds. Matisse painted his wife Amélie in 1905, using color instead of ordinary shadows. Critics were baffled, but he said color could build a picture. It's a classic Fauvist work.

A tree with red-orange limbs twists against a blue background. Mondrian painted this early in his career, using color instead of realism. Later he would simplify trees into lines and grids. It's an important step on his journey to abstract art.

A woman reclines on a couch in the middle of a lush jungle, surrounded by lions, birds, snakes and a flute player in the moonlight. Rousseau said she was dreaming the whole scene. He painted it in his last year, in an amazing, flat style, with every leaf carefully shaped. It's one of the world's most famous dreamlike paintings.

A young girl stands with her arms around herself at the edge of a morning lake, in soft hazy light. Chabas painted it in 1912, and it became so famous that millions of copies were sold. A famous controversy in the U.S. made it even more popular. It's a great example of how a painting can become a pop-culture sensation.

A line of soldiers who have been blinded by poison gas each rest a hand on the shoulder of the man ahead, walking toward a medical station. Sargent saw this scene for real in 1918 during World War I. The painting is enormous, nearly seven meters wide. It's one of the most memorable pictures of the war.

A hundred horses graze, rest, swim and gallop across a long scroll, a mix of Chinese and Italian styles. Castiglione, an Italian monk painter at the Chinese court, painted it for the emperor. It shows how different art traditions can combine. It's one of the treasures of Chinese court art.
paintings.k: Find horses swimming, sleeping, and playing. Can you spot the one that looks naughtiest?

paintings.why: A maid carries a tray with a glass of water and a cup of hot chocolate, all painted with fine precision. Liotard worked in pastels and made this in Vienna. A Dresden collector bought it and it hangs in the Old Masters Gallery there. It's one of the most famous pastel paintings.

paintings.t: The Lady with a Fan, The Artist's Wife
paintings.why: A woman in a splendid blue satin gown holds a fan, with a calm smile. Roslin painted his wife Marie-Suzanne Giroust, a talented artist herself. The shimmering fabric is a marvel. It's one of the great portraits of the 1700s.

The Roman philosopher Seneca, ordered to take his own life by Emperor Nero, calmly dictates his last words to scribes as his friends weep. David painted a thoughtful, tragic scene early in his career. The story is about staying true to your values to the end. It's a powerful example of Neoclassical art.

Dozens of gentlemen crowd into a famous gallery in Florence, studying paintings and statues from the Renaissance. Queen Charlotte commissioned Zoffany to paint the picture, and he squeezed in masterpieces from all over the museum. He arranged the artworks and people as he liked. It's a picture of a museum filled with art.

A widow kneels at the bed of her husband Hector, a hero of the Trojan War, with her young son by her side. David painted this scene from Homer's Iliad. It has a stark, heartbreaking feeling. It helped earn him membership at the French Academy.

The Spartan king Leonidas sits in calm readiness with his soldiers at the mountain pass of Thermopylae, preparing for a last stand against a vast Persian army. David painted the Spartans with heroic simplicity. In 480 BC, 300 Spartans and their allies held off the Persians for days. It's one of history's most famous last stands.

Giant figures float through the sky, with one holding scissors to cut the thread of life, like the Fates of Greek myth. It's one of Goya's Black Paintings on the walls of his home. The picture is also known as 'The Fates.' It's a spooky reflection on time and destiny.

The Greek poet Homer sits at the center of a temple, crowned by a goddess of Victory, while the greatest writers, artists and thinkers from history gather around him. Ingres painted a tribute to the ancient world as a grand 'who's who.' The composition is very symmetrical and orderly. It was painted for a ceiling in the Louvre.

A young Courbet sits in the countryside with his dog, leaning against a rock, looking out with confidence. He painted this when he was 23. The dark landscape gives the picture a moody feeling. It's an early display of his talent.

Napoleon rides a mule on a mountain pass, looking rather calm, in a more realistic version of the heroic scene. Delaroche painted it in 1848 to show how it was in truth — a mule, not a prancing horse. It's a clever answer to David's famous idealized portrait. It reminds us that history can be told in different ways.

A woman stretches her back after hours of needlework, in a room of rich blue and gold, with a stained-glass window. The painting is inspired by a poem by Tennyson about a woman waiting for a lover who doesn't come. Millais used glowing colors. It's a gorgeous Pre-Raphaelite painting.

A large woman steps out of a pond as her companion watches, in a Realist take on a classical theme. When it was shown in 1853, critics and the emperor were scandalized. Courbet liked to shock. It's a famous painting about honesty and realism.

A woman holds a flower and an apple, with a golden background, her mouth beckoning. The title means 'the kissed mouth.' Rossetti used her red hair and rich fabrics in a daring new style. It started a new direction in his painting.

A young woman reclines on a wave, with a pearl in her hand, as the surf and spray curl around her. Baudry painted it at the Paris Salon of 1863. The Empress Eugénie bought it. It's a charming picture of a water spirit.

Oedipus stands face to face with the Sphinx in a rocky pass, the monster clinging to his chest. Moreau's picture shows two figures locked in a deep stare. It was his first success at the Salon, in 1864. It's among the most famous Symbolist paintings.

A man throws himself at the doorway, begging for Poland not to be divided, while the nobles in the room look away. Matejko painted a moment from 1773, when Poland's neighbors carved up the country. It's a harsh message about betrayal. It's a famous national symbol.

A young girl in a white dress sits in the shade of a tree, with a pretty village on a hill behind her. Bazille painted it at his family's home in Montpellier, in the south of France. The strong sunlight and shadows were new at the time. It's an early Impressionist masterpiece.

A man stands by a door, and a woman in a chemise sits sadly at the foot of a bed, in a dimly lit bedroom. Degas gave no title to explain the story, which makes people wonder. It's famous as a mysterious picture of tension between two people.

Dark birds perch in birch trees as a little church stands behind, and spring melts the snow. Savrasov painted this in a quiet village, and it became one of the most beloved Russian paintings. It's regarded as the start of a new feeling for Russian landscape. People love it for its quiet, simple beauty.

Young dancers stand and stretch in a practice studio, as the ballet master looks on. Degas loved to paint dancers behind the scenes, working hard. He painted many studies like this, with unusual views. It's one of his best-loved pictures.

Sailboats with bright white sails glide across the Seine on a sunny day, with their reflections wobbling in the water. Monet lived at Argenteuil and painted boating there for years. The water ripples with strokes of color. It's one of his bright, breezy summer scenes.

paintings.t: The Hanging of the Sigismund bell at the Cathedral Tower in 1521 in Kraków
paintings.why: In 1521 in Kraków, workers raise a giant bell by ropes into the cathedral tower, as the crowd and the king watch. The Sigismund Bell is still in the cathedral and still rings. Matejko painted the pride of the city. It's a lively picture of a big community project.

A stylish young woman in a deep blue dress and a flowered hat looks out with a confident smile. Renoir painted it in 1874 in the first year of Impressionism. The blue fabric glimmers in the light. It's an elegant picture of the modern city.

A famous surgeon pauses in an operating theater to explain a procedure to a room of students, his hand bloody. Eakins's honest picture showed modern science. Many in 1875 found the realism hard to look at. Today it's seen as one of the greatest American paintings.

A woman in a bright red Japanese kimono stands with a fan against a background of fans. Monet's wife Camille posed for it. Japanese art was a craze in Paris in the 1870s. It's a colorful, playful piece.

A man and woman sit on a bench in a glass-roofed garden room, surrounded by lush plants. Manet used the real-life couple, the Guillemets, who ran a shop. The woman wears a ring while the man leans toward her, with a gap between them. It's a subtle picture of two people.

The Duke of Prussia kneels to swear loyalty to the king of Poland in Kraków's central square in 1525. Matejko packed it with portraits of nobles and knights in rich costumes. It's a picture of a time when Poland was strong. It's a national treasure.

Two sisters in pink and blue dresses stand side by side, smiling softly. Renoir painted the daughters of a Parisian banker, Alice and Elisabeth Cahen d'Anvers. The soft colors and curls give them a sweet charm. It's a very sweet double portrait.

paintings.t: View of the Sea at Scheveningen
paintings.why: Dark waves roll under a gray sky, with a few small figures and boats on the beach. Van Gogh painted this on the Dutch coast in 1882, in the wind and sand. Tiny grains of sand are still stuck in the paint. It's an early, wild seascape.

paintings.t: The Favourites of the Emperor Honorius
paintings.why: A Roman emperor feeds his pet chickens, which he called by the names of cities, while an official brings news. In the legend, he cared more for his hens than for the news that Rome was falling. Waterhouse painted a rich scene of the late Roman Empire. It's a funny and surprising story.

Cupids and woodland figures dance in a flowery glade as spring returns. Bouguereau often painted fairy-tale scenes full of soft color and joyful movement. Nature wakes up after winter. It's a cheerful celebration of the season.

A crab lies on its back, its claws and legs curled, in a few strokes of orange and green. Van Gogh was inspired by Japanese prints and painted it in Paris. It's a quick but lively study. It shows he could find wonder in simple things.

A group of painters, writers and friends raise their glasses in a sunny garden in Skagen, in northern Denmark. Krøyer painted his colony of artist friends, including himself. The light is warm and the mood is joyful. It's one of the best-loved Danish paintings.

A long avenue of poplars glows with yellow and orange autumn light, with strolling couples. It was an ancient Roman cemetery in Arles, France. Van Gogh painted it in autumn 1888. The golden trees seem to dance.

Blossoming orchards line the foreground, with the old town of Arles and its stone towers behind them. Van Gogh was captivated by the spring in Provence. The painting glows with white and pink flowers. It's a happy picture of a fresh season.

A bush of lilacs stands in the garden of an asylum in Saint-Rémy, with a blue sky. Van Gogh painted this in the spring of 1889. The soft purples and blues contrast with the green leaves. It's a quiet picture of beauty in a hard time.

paintings.t: The Boy in the Red Vest
paintings.why: A young man in a red vest leans on his arm, painted in sculpted blocks of color. Cézanne painted this model, an Italian youth, several times. Look at his unnaturally long arm — it's deliberate, for the balance of the composition. It's one of the most famous modern portraits.

Van Gogh looks out with a bandage over his ear, wearing a fur cap and a thick coat, with a Japanese print behind him. He painted it after he hurt his ear in December 1888. It's a direct, honest picture of a difficult time. It's among the most famous self-portraits.

The goddess Venus rises from the sea, wearing a seashell like a hat, while cherubs frolic nearby. Gérôme was a great admirer of the classical world. He painted it late in his life. It's a lively picture of mythology.

Three Russian knights on horseback, from folk tales, scan the horizon for danger. Vasnetsov painted Ilya Muromets, Dobrynya Nikitich and Alyosha Popovich, famous heroes. It took him nearly 20 years. Many Russian kids know this painting from school.
paintings.k: Three knights ride on horses. Can you tell what each one is carrying?

paintings.why: A woman stands in the shadows with a large snake draped over her shoulders, her eyes glowing. Franz von Stuck painted this as a symbol of temptation. It was a huge success, and he painted several versions. It is a dark and dramatic Symbolist painting.

According to legend, Lady Godiva rode a horse through the town in protest of a harsh tax, and the townspeople kindly stayed indoors. Collier painted her in a hush of dignity. The tale is a famous English legend. It's a picture of courage.

A couple's faces merge into one in a dim room, beside a window with a glimmer of light. Munch painted several versions of the scene. The way the two become one is touching and mysterious. It's one of his best-loved paintings.

Two women stand close together, one holding a bowl of flowers or fruit, in bright colors. Gauguin painted this in his later years in the Marquesas Islands. The flat, rich colors are a sign of his love of the Pacific. It's one of his best-known island paintings.

A path leads through arches of irises, daylilies and roses in Monet's colorful garden. He designed the garden himself and painted it for decades. The mass of flowers is painted in joyful strokes. It's a glimpse of the paradise he built.

A crowd of workers marches steadily out of the shadows toward us. Pellizza spent years on this painting. He called it 'The Fourth Estate' because it showed the working class as a new force in society. It became a symbol of workers' rights in Italy.

An open window frames a view of boats in a harbor, with window boxes of flowers and bursts of pure color. Matisse painted this in the summer of 1905 at Collioure on France's southern coast. It's a famous Fauvist painting. It invites us to look out at a bright new view.

A dark silhouette of a snake charmer plays a flute in a moonlit jungle, with glowing eyes and snakes coiled around. Rousseau said it was inspired by a friend's story of India. The painting is full of lush leaves painted in dozens of greens. It's a dreamlike masterpiece.

Horses, workers and a rising city explode in a blur of color and movement. Boccioni painted it as a celebration of the energetic new industrial city of Milan. He was a leader of Futurism, which loved speed and machines. It's one of the key paintings of the movement.

A fashionable woman in a pink, patterned dress looks out in front of a bright, richly colored background. Klimt painted her a second time, years after his gold portrait. This one is colorful instead of golden. It sold for $88 million in 2006.

A tangle of colored rectangles and lines tilts and floats on a white ground, like objects in space. Malevich created Suprematism to show pure feeling in shapes. The painting seems to drift in all directions. It's an exciting piece of early abstract art.

A woman sits upright on a divan, painted with Modigliani's simplified, elegant, elongated shapes. He painted many such portraits in Paris in 1917. The curved lines and warm colors create a feeling of calm. It's an example of his unique style.

A wide-eyed angel with wings seems to look back in surprise, drawn in a childlike style. Paul Klee made this in 1920, and philosopher Walter Benjamin later owned it and wrote about it as an angel of history. Benjamin saw the angel being blown backward into the future, looking at the pile of wreckage of the past. It's a famous image about time.

A British general dies on the battlefield after winning the Battle of Quebec in 1759, as officers gather around him like figures in a religious painting. Benjamin West dressed the scene in contemporary clothes, which was bold at the time. The painting was a sensation in London. It changed how history painting was done.

A man draws back in surprise as a captive starling, which can only say 'I can't get out,' flutters in a cage. The painting was inspired by a story by Laurence Sterne. Wright of Derby used lamplight to bring the moment to life. It makes you think about freedom and kindness.

A man in a green coat holds a violin as he glances out, with a bow in his hand. Anne Vallayer-Coster was a French painter, and one of the few women admitted to the French Royal Academy of Painting. She was famous for still lifes, and this is an unusual portrait. It's a lovely picture of music.

A man locks a door with one arm, as a woman tries to push him away and to reach a table with an apple in the background. Fragonard painted it in 1777. The sparkle of the fabrics is dazzling. The meaning is mysterious, so viewers still debate it.

A group of boys march and play with toy drums and swords. Goya painted this as a design for a tapestry, with bright colors and lively movement. It's a charming glimpse of children at play in 1700s Spain. It captures the joy of imagination.

The queen of France sits proudly with her children, and an empty cradle. Vigée Le Brun painted it to improve the queen's image, at a time when people were angry with her. The empty cradle represents a baby daughter who had recently died. It's a sad and important portrait.

paintings.t: Portrait of Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier and his wife
paintings.why: A famous chemist sits at a table of scientific instruments, as his wife leans on his shoulder. Lavoisier helped create modern chemistry, and his wife Marie-Anne was his partner in science. David painted them as a pair of modern, smart people. It's a landmark portrait of science.

Young people in fancy clothes play the game of blind man's bluff in a ring, outdoors. Goya painted it as a design for a tapestry for the Spanish palace. The light and fun scene is full of charm. It's a happy picture from his early career.
paintings.k: Everyone plays a game of tag with a blindfold. Which player is it?

paintings.why: The prince Paris sits beside Helen of Troy, with Cupid close by, in a graceful chamber. According to legend, their love began the Trojan War. David painted it in 1788 in the elegant style of ancient Greece. It's a beautiful scene with a sad ending to come.

A little girl sits in a landscape, her head tilted, with a sweet look of curiosity. Reynolds was the first president of the Royal Academy, and he often painted children. The soft light and fluffy dress capture childhood. It's one of the best-loved child portraits in English art.
paintings.k: The girl looks to the side. What do you think she is listening to?

paintings.t: The Ambassadors of Agamemnon in the tent of Achilles
paintings.why: Greek messengers come to the tent of the hero Achilles, who sulks over a quarrel with his commander, begging him to return to the war. Ingres painted it at 20, as a prize piece in Paris. It's based on Homer's Iliad. It shows how well he'd learned the lessons of ancient sculpture.

A young girl in a white dress and a soft yellow shawl looks gently out of the canvas. Ingres painted her when she was about 13, and the smooth, curving lines and delicate details show his skill. She died only a year later, which adds a sad note to the portrait. It's one of the most loved portraits of a child.

The god Jupiter sits on his throne, with an eagle by his side, while the sea-goddess Thetis begs a favor. Ingres painted it at age 31 in Rome. The great size and the strict calm made some critics unhappy. It's a bold act of artistic ambition.

Two men sink up to their knees in mud, striking each other with sticks, as a dark landscape stretches behind them. Goya painted this on the wall of his house in his Black Paintings series. It's often seen as a picture of conflict that goes nowhere. It's a serious, thoughtful painting.

Four racehorses are stretched out in mid-gallop, all their legs off the ground, with jockeys in bright colors. Géricault painted the 'flying gallop' at a time before cameras could show how horses really run. We now know that this is not how horses really move! It's a thrilling picture of speed that influenced later artists.
paintings.k: All four horses have their legs stretched out in the air. Is this really how horses gallop?

paintings.why: A huge old oak stands in a meadow under a gloomy sky, with a pale village and hills beyond. Friedrich painted the tree like a hero, strong but alone. It's a symbol of survival. It's one of his best-known landscapes.

Great wooden ships fire their guns in a smoky sea battle, as sailors battle on deck and in the water. Turner painted this scene from the Royal Navy's 1805 victory, in which Admiral Nelson died. It was commissioned for King George IV. It's a record of a famous naval battle.

A boy kneels to drink from a pond, as sheep and a dog wait on a path, bordered by a golden cornfield. Constable painted the place he knew from his childhood. The rich greens and the glowing sky are full of life. It's a classic of English landscape.

paintings.t: Entry of the Crusaders in Constantinople
paintings.why: Crusader knights ride through a city in 1204, with crowds of people begging for mercy. Delacroix painted the wildness of history in swirling colors. The painting hangs in the Louvre. It's a tough scene, painted with deep emotion.

A young woman, Mary, sits on a bed in a plain white room as the angel Gabriel appears. Rossetti used only white and blue, a bold choice. The title means 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord.' It was a fresh, modern view of a very old story.

A Highland soldier, freed from prison, gives the jailer the order to release him, while his wife, with a baby in her arms, rests her head on his shoulder. Millais used his future wife as the model. The picture earned him the greatest success of his career. It's an emotional tale of reunion.

Sheep graze on a bright green cliff above a blue sea, with sunlight on their wool. Hunt painted every blade of grass and animal in close detail. It was meant as a warning of an invasion — the sheep, he joked, were unprotected. It's a beautiful look at the English coast.

paintings.t: Joséphine-Éléonore-Marie-Pauline de Galard de Brassac de Béarn (1825–1860), Princesse de Broglie
paintings.why: A French princess sits in a blue satin dress with a pearl necklace and elegant poise. Ingres took a long time to paint her, and the dress is exquisitely detailed. The portrait is one of the most admired of the 1800s. It hangs in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.

A lone goat stands on the salt shore of the Dead Sea, with a red cloth on its horns. In an old tradition, a goat carried the sins of the people into the wilderness. Hunt traveled to the Dead Sea to paint it on the spot. It's famous for its harsh, shimmering landscape.

A young woman in a blue gown and a young man kneel together with a trailing rose bush, a shy and sad moment. Hughes painted it in a very fine detail with rich color. The painting is based on a poem by Tennyson. It's a dreamy scene of first love.

paintings.t: Empress Eugenie Surrounded by her Ladies in Waiting
paintings.why: The Empress of France sits on a flower-strewn lawn, with her ladies in pastel gowns gathered around, like in a garden party. Winterhalter was the favorite portrait painter of royalty across Europe. The picture has a dreamy, fairy-tale glow. It's a glimpse into royal life.

Dancing figures in a circle, in a lively swirl of ancient costume. Bouguereau's graceful figures seem to move to music. It's a classical celebration of dance as part of life. The smooth surface and gentle poses are signatures of his style.

At dawn in the snow, a man in a white Pierrot costume is held by his friend after losing a duel. The story's details are uncertain, but the picture was a hit with the public. The harsh cold and the colorful costumes make it unforgettable. It's a fine example of dramatic storytelling.

Two nuns in a convent graveyard at twilight, one digging a grave, the other sitting nearby. Millais painted it near London, with a sunset sky. The still, silent mood is unforgettable. It's a haunting view of quiet devotion.

After being stabbed by senators in Rome, Julius Caesar's body lies in a theater, while the conspirators scatter. Gérôme painted an empty hall instead of the actual fight. The still, quiet scene is more haunting than a battle. It's a clever painting of a famous event.

A soldier in a black uniform says a tender, hasty goodbye to his sweetheart before riding off to battle, just before Waterloo. She holds the door shut as if she could keep him back. Millais painted every fold of her satin dress. It was one of the most popular paintings of its day.

A priest preaches to the king and nobles of Poland about their duties, warning them of dangers ahead. Piotr Skarga was a real preacher in the 1500s who warned of a decline. Matejko painted it to inspire Poles in a time of foreign rule. It's famous for its message of patriotism.

Two polar bears prowl through the wreck of an Arctic expedition, gnawing at a torn flag and scattered supplies. Landseer painted this after the lost Franklin expedition. The title means we make plans but nature has the final say. It's a famous and very dramatic image.
paintings.k: Find the polar bears in the ice. What are they looking at?

paintings.why: A woman sits in front of a mirror, brushing her long golden hair, in a rich red-and-white room. In old legend, Lilith was Adam's first wife. Rossetti's painting is full of beautiful details, like flowers and a glowing mirror. It's a dreamy picture of beauty and mystery.

A young girl in a ragged dress stands in a field of tall grass, with a pair of large eyes and a sad, direct look. Bouguereau made many pictures of poor children for rich collectors. It's meant to inspire compassion. It's still a famous image of childhood.

The holy city shines golden in the late sun, seen from the Mount of Olives. Gérôme visited the Middle East and painted the scene with great fidelity. Its calm and glowing mood makes the city feel timeless. It's a majestic view.

A young man in a hat stands by a table, in a studio with a suit of armor and a mother-and-child nearby. Manet's son Léon posed. The scene doesn't tell a clear story, which keeps people curious. It's a modern, mysterious indoor scene.

Artists and friends gather in a bright studio full of paintings, including Manet, Monet and Renoir. Bazille painted the group that would form the Impressionists. The painting shows his friends before they became famous. It's like a family snapshot of art history.

A young Jesus, working in a carpenter's shop, stretches out his arms, and the shadow forms a cross on the wall behind. His mother looks on, feeling fear. Hunt painted it in the Holy Land. It's one of the most famous images of Jesus as a boy.

Two men sit by a chessboard in a quiet room, thinking deeply. Eakins painted his father and friends and was mindful of the light on the wood and on their faces. It was a gift to his father. It's a nice study of concentration.

A merchant, Sadko, is walking along the sea bottom in a magical underwater kingdom, as the Sea King's daughters parade past in dresses. It's based on a Russian folk tale, which inspired an opera, too. Repin painted the sea princesses with different faces from many nations. It's a fairy tale full of beauty.
paintings.k: Sadko walks along the seabed. Which creature would you ask for directions?

paintings.t: Madame Georges Charpentier and her Children
paintings.why: A wealthy publisher's wife sits with her young son and daughter, and a large dog on a couch, in a room with Japanese decor. Renoir's painting won him new patrons when it was well received at the Salon. It's fabulously cozy. It's a portrait of a stylish Paris family.

A view over Paris rooftops in the snow, with chimneys and gray skies. Caillebotte painted it from the window of his home. The cool colors and unusual view are quiet and modern. It's a favorite of city landscapes.

paintings.t: Miss La La at the Cirque Fernando
paintings.why: A circus performer hangs by her teeth from a rope high in the air, as the audience looks up from below. Degas made it after seeing her perform in Paris. The dizzying angle and the geometry of the dome are daring. It's an exciting picture.
paintings.k: She hangs by her teeth from a rope. Why do you think the artist painted it from below?

paintings.why: Two girls in black dresses stand with rosy cheeks and shining hair. Renoir painted them with warm light, with a touch of the outdoors in the colors. They are two of his favorite young models. It's a charming picture of youth.

A woman with dignity and calm looks out at us, wearing a white head covering and a draped shawl. Bilińska, a Polish painter who trained in Paris, painted this in 1884. It was a portrait that treated its sitter with respect, at a time when that was uncommon. It's a striking example of 19th-century portrait painting.

paintings.t: Cleopatra Testing Poisons on Condemned Prisoners
paintings.why: The Egyptian queen watches closely as a poison is tested on prisoners, while her servants stand by. Cabanel painted a gripping scene of the ancient world. The details of the room are exquisite. It's a dramatic image of ancient power.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: Rooftops, chimneys and a cloudy sky stretch over Paris as seen from the apartment where Van Gogh lived with his brother Theo. Van Gogh painted the view in 1887 with fresh, quick strokes after learning from the Impressionists. It's one of the first signs of his bright palette. It's a city view with a feeling of home.

A woman with a snake wound around her body stands by a tree in a lush forest. John Collier painted Lilith, a character from old legends. The snake and soft light give it a dreamlike feel. It's an eye-catching Victorian painting.

A white farmhouse sits among golden fields and green trees under a bright blue sky. Van Gogh painted it in Arles in summer 1888. The bold color and clean lines show his Japanese influences. It's a sunny scene of country life.

People in bright clothes crowd the stands of a Roman arena for a bullfight, under a blue sky. Van Gogh was struck by the old structure and the festive crowd. The painting is made of bold dabs of color. It's a lively scene of Provençal life.

A sunny path curves through green fields lined with trees near the town of Arles. Van Gogh painted the bright scene in the summer light of southern France. The path draws the viewer into the picture. It's a peaceful stroll.

Dark, flame-shaped cypress trees twist up toward a swirling sky. Van Gogh said they were as beautiful as an Egyptian obelisk. He painted several versions during his stay in Saint-Rémy. They've become signature elements of his art.

A woman at a dressing table powders her face in front of a vase of flowers. Seurat painted his partner Madeleine Knobloch, and he later painted over a portrait of himself in the corner. It's made with fine dots, with a flat, decorative look. It's a quiet, witty picture.

Dancers kick up their legs in a lively Paris cabaret dance, with a musician and the audience. Seurat painted it with tiny dots of color, and the lines all lead upward for cheerfulness. The effect is a moving, energetic scene. It's one of the best examples of his method.

A young doctor sits in a swirling background of red, orange and green. Dr. Rey treated Van Gogh in the hospital in Arles. Van Gogh gave him the portrait, but the doctor wasn't a fan and used it to patch a chicken coop, the story goes. Today it's worth a fortune.

Two crabs, one on its back, scuttle on a pale green background. Van Gogh painted them in Arles in 1889, using bright orange and green. He loved Japanese prints, which have many pictures of sea life. It's a charming study.
paintings.k: One crab is upside down! Can you find its claws?

paintings.why: A man in a black coat and hat stands with a paintbrush and palette in front of a harbor and a ship decorated with flags. Rousseau painted himself as a proud artist in the world. The hot-air balloon and flags show his sense of fun. It's a charming self-portrait.
A smiling young woman in a colorful dress and headscarf leans her head on her hand. Bouguereau painted her with great care. It's a pleasant, charming portrait. It shows how popular his work was.

A girl in a white dress stands in a field of wheat in the sun, with her back slightly turned. Van Gogh painted it in Auvers-sur-Oise in 1890. The brushwork is lively and bright. It's a peaceful piece from his final weeks.

Moss-covered roofs of old cottages cluster together in a village, with trees and a cloudy sky. Van Gogh painted it in Auvers-sur-Oise, in northern France, in 1890. He loved these old thatched houses. It reminds you of simple country life.
A young girl with red hair looks out with soft, grave eyes, wearing a white dress. Bouguereau painted her in 1890. The soft realism is typical of his work. It's a sensitive portrait of a child.

A woman in a long white dress holds a flower to her ear, in warm tropical light. Gauguin painted it soon after arriving in Tahiti. The simple, strong figure and bold colors show his new direction. It's a famous image of his first stay on the island.

A crowd of 42 cats, each with a different personality, poses on and around a luxurious cushion. Carl Kahler painted the cats of a rich woman in San Francisco, and the painting took three years. The cats' names are known, and the painting is a world record in cat portraits. It's a delight for cat lovers.
paintings.k: There are 42 cats in this painting. Can you count ten of them? Which cat looks the grumpiest?

paintings.why: Two figures, one wading and one on the beach, are near the sea in Tahiti, with a pink tree arching overhead. The title means 'near the sea.' Gauguin built the picture out of flat, bold areas of color, like a Japanese print. It's a dreamy view of paradise.

A basket of apples sits tilted on a table with a bottle, a plate of biscuits and a cloth, painted from several angles at once. Cézanne wanted to show how we actually see, with our eyes moving around. The table looks tilted and the bottle too. It's a great example of his groundbreaking approach.

A crowd of people with ghostly faces walk toward us under a blood-red sky on a bridge. Munch made this just after his most famous painting, The Scream, with similar colors. The mood is one of unease. It's a picture of worry that many people recognize.

A pale man stares out in the foreground of a garden as a couple stands behind him. Munch painted jealousy as a green-faced mood. The painting is more about feeling than action. It's a revealing look at a strong emotion.

A skeleton gardener in a black cloak waters flowers as a boy and girl in white watch. Simberg's strange, gentle painting turns death into a friendly gardener. He was a Finnish Symbolist painter. It's both spooky and sweet.

A woman reclines on a bed in a Tahitian room, as a raven sits by the window and two people whisper in the background. Gauguin named it after a poem by Edgar Allan Poe. The mood is mysterious and moody. It's a rich picture of colors and symbols.

The boy Icarus, who flew too close to the sun, lies on the shore as sea nymphs mourn. In the Greek myth, his wax wings melted. Draper painted the beautiful, glowing scene in 1898. It's one of the most beloved paintings of Greek myth.

A knight leans down from his horse as his lady ties a scarf around his arm and wishes him luck before battle. Edmund Blair Leighton painted such romantic scenes from the Middle Ages with great detail. This one is among the most popular. It's a picture of love and courage.

Five red figures stand on a green hill under a deep blue sky, singing and playing. Matisse used just three colors: blue, green and red. The simplicity and boldness were revolutionary. It's a masterpiece of modern color.

A whirlwind of colors, shapes and lines swirls across the whole canvas. Kandinsky made dozens of studies for it and painted it in just four days. He believed that color and shape could move us like music. It's often called his masterpiece and one of the first great abstract paintings.

A young woman in a white dress stands before a background of Chinese-style patterns and figures. Klimt painted Elisabeth when she was around 17. The decorations are inspired by East Asian art. It's a stunning portrait filled with ornament.

A woman looks over her shoulder with a bold stare, wearing a patterned robe, set against a pale background. Klimt painted it at the end of his career. It was stolen from a museum in Italy in 1997 and mysteriously reappeared in 2019. It's one of the strangest art stories.

A magnificent chestnut horse rears up against a plain background, the size of life. Stubbs painted it for the Marquess of Rockingham, and it is thought that there was no background by design. His knowledge of horse anatomy is astonishing. It is the most famous horse painting in Britain.
paintings.k: This horse is life-size. Can you stand up as tall as his shoulder?

paintings.t: General Johnson Saving a Wounded French Officer from the Tomahawk of a North American Indian
paintings.why: In a scene from the French and Indian War, a British officer protects a wounded French soldier. Benjamin West, an American in London, painted it with dramatic action in the forest. It shows kindness in a time of war. It's an early work of American-born art.

Mary floats in a pale blue gown, standing on a crescent moon and surrounded by angels, in a cloud of golden light. Tiepolo painted it for a church in Madrid. The airy colors make the whole scene look like it's floating. It's one of the most graceful paintings of the Baroque era.

An old philosopher in a red hat sits reading by the light of a single lamp, which makes his face glow in the dark. Wright of Derby was a master of dramatic candlelight. The picture makes you think about the quiet joy of studying. It's a model of strong light and shadow.

A young woman sits on a grassy bank with a little dog on her lap, as a young man holds a bright green parasol over her. Goya designed this as a pattern for a tapestry for a royal palace. The colors are cheerful and bright. It's a delightful picture of leisure.
l: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía

paintings.why: An old, blind general, once a great hero, begs on the street as a soldier recognizes him in astonishment. In the story, Belisarius was Rome's top commander who was treated unfairly. David painted it with clear and strong emotions. It's a lesson that glory can vanish.

A group of figures, with pointed hats, fly through the sky as they hold up a man, in a swirl of eerie blue and gray. Goya painted a world of superstition and fear. It's meant to make people think about the foolish things people believe. It's a spooky picture.

A young noblewoman in a pale dress with a feathery hairdo sits with her hands folded, wearing a soft, thoughtful look. Goya painted her when she was about 20, a few years after she'd been forced into a marriage. He saw the sadness in her eyes, and the portrait is full of feeling. It's one of his greatest portraits.

paintings.t: Portrait of the Marchioness of Santa Cruz
paintings.why: A Spanish noblewoman lies on a couch, in a classical white dress, with a lyre, as if she were a Muse. Goya painted it with loose brushstrokes and with a cool and gentle mood. It's an original and fresh view of portraits. It's a favorite in Madrid's Prado Museum.

paintings.t: The Death of Leonardo da Vinci
paintings.why: The great artist Leonardo da Vinci lies on his deathbed in France, in the arms of the king, as friends look on. It's a legend, not a proven fact, but Ingres loved the story. The painting is a tribute to a genius. It reflects the great respect for artists in 1800s France.

The hero Achilles is furious as Agamemnon takes back a prize, in a scene from Homer's Iliad. David painted it late in his life, in exile, in a rich, sculpted style. The rage is felt in every face. It's a dramatic moment from the Trojan War.

A dark, ghostly crowd of people sing, stagger and stare out in a wild procession. Goya painted it on a wall of his house as part of the Black Paintings. It's a contrast with his earlier cheerful version of the same festival. It shows how his view of the world had darkened.
The elderly Goya, ill and pale, is held by his doctor, who offers him a drink. Goya painted it as thanks to Dr. Arrieta for saving his life. Dark shadows loom behind them. It's a touching tribute.

The Egyptian queen sails in a golden barge, dressed as the goddess Venus, to meet Mark Antony in Tarsus. Etty painted the shimmering scene with rich color and flowing movement. The sails, flowers and attendants are dazzling. It's a lush picture of ancient glamour.

The cathedral's slim spire rises beyond a stream and meadow beneath a stormy sky, with a bright rainbow. Constable painted it in 1831, when he was sad about the death of his wife. The dramatic clouds show his feelings. It's one of his grandest landscapes.

A curving river winds through a green valley as a storm clears. A tiny painter at an easel stands on the hillside in the corner. Thomas Cole showed that nature was big and beautiful, and humans were small. It's one of the most famous American landscape paintings.
