Attila the Hun feasts with his warriors and advisors in a great hall. The Hungarian painter Mór Than painted this in 1870, when many Hungarians looked at Attila as a figure from their own early history.

In 1066 King Harald Hardrada of Norway, the last great Viking king, is killed in a battle against the English at Stamford Bridge. Peter Nicolai Arbo painted this clash in 1870, only days before the Norman invasion.

paintings.t: Harald Fairhair in the Battle of Hafrsfjord
paintings.why: Harald Fairhair wins the sea battle of Hafrsfjord around the year 872, a victory the sagas say united Norway under one king. The Norwegian-American painter Ole Peter Hansen Balling painted it in 1870.

paintings.t: Party for New Year's Day in New Amsterdam, 1636
paintings.why: Dutch settlers in the colony of New Amsterdam on Manhattan, the future New York, celebrate New Year's Day in the snow. George Henry Boughton painted this cozy imagined scene in 1870.

A train crosses a bridge over the Seine at Argenteuil, a village near Paris where the railway brought city people for weekends. Claude Monet painted the modern age into the peaceful countryside in 1870.

paintings.t: The Battle of Gettysburg: Pickett's Charge
paintings.why: Confederate soldiers cross a wide field in Pickett's Charge, the last big attack at Gettysburg on July 3, 1863, which failed. Peter Frederick Rothermel painted this huge picture in 1870.

paintings.t: Chinese Railroad Workers in the Sierra Nevada
paintings.why: Thousands of Chinese workers built the Central Pacific Railroad through the Sierra Nevada, digging tunnels and clearing rock by hand, in very dangerous conditions. This print from the 1870s shows the railroad climbing through the mountains.

Paris, personified as a woman holding a flag, rises among dead soldiers during the German siege of the French capital in the winter of 1870 and 1871. Ernest Meissonier, who served in the siege, painted it in 1870.

After the emperor Caligula was killed in AD 41, soldiers found his uncle Claudius hiding behind a curtain and made him emperor. Lawrence Alma-Tadema, who loved Roman history, painted the moment in 1871.
A steam train rolls into a little suburban station in south London while the painter Camille Pissarro, who was staying in England to escape the Franco-Prussian War, looked on. He painted it in 1871.
Louise Michel, a teacher who fought for the Paris Commune, is arrested by soldiers in 1871 and later sent to a prison colony in the Pacific. Jules Girardet painted her capture in 1871.

paintings.t: Execution of Communards at the Lobau Barracks
paintings.why: Soldiers shoot captured members of the Paris Commune at the Lobau Barracks in May 1871, during the 'Bloody Week' that ended the Commune. Frédéric Théodore Lix drew it in 1871 for a French newspaper.

According to tradition, on October 31, 1517, Martin Luther nailed his 95 Theses, complaints against the Church's sale of pardons, to the church door in Wittenberg, which launched the Reformation. Historians debate how it happened, but this scene from 1872 is the famous image.
A young woman in white sits among ruins, holding a green branch, as a symbol of hope after France's defeat in the war of 1870 and 1871. Pierre Puvis de Chavannes painted it in 1872.

paintings.t: A Scene in the White Mountains
paintings.why: Mountains rise above a quiet valley, with the soft light of dawn or dusk. Aaron Allan Edson painted landscapes in Quebec and the White Mountains of New Hampshire. He was part of a generation of Canadian painters who showed the beauty of the land. It's a peaceful wilderness view.

paintings.t: Ojibwa Camp, Northern Shore of Lake Huron
paintings.why: An Ojibwe camp sits on the shore of Lake Huron, with tents and canoes under a wide sky. Frederick Arthur Verner painted Indigenous people and the northern landscape. The scene records a way of life by the Great Lakes. It's an important image of 19th-century Canada.

paintings.t: The Charge of the 9th Cuirassiers at Morsbronn
paintings.why: French armored cavalry charge through the narrow streets of the village of Morsbronn on August 6, 1870, in a brave but hopeless attack against Prussian infantry. Édouard Detaille painted this charge in 1873.

paintings.t: The Burning of the Hôtel de Ville, 24 May 1871
paintings.why: The great Paris city hall, the Hôtel de Ville, burns on May 24, 1871, during the last week of the Paris Commune, the radical government of Paris. Léon Sabatier painted the fires in 1873.

Guests recline at a dinner party in ancient Athens, taking turns to give speeches about love, in a scene from Plato's dialogue The Symposium. Anselm Feuerbach, who loved ancient Greece, made two versions of it and painted this second one in the early 1870s.

paintings.t: Charge of the French Cuirassiers at Waterloo
paintings.why: Armored French cavalry charge up the slope at the Battle of Waterloo on June 18, 1815, the battle where Napoleon was finally defeated. Henri Félix Emmanuel Philippoteaux painted this charge in 1874.
Eugène Thirion shows Joan of Arc, in a simple red dress, listening to the angels and saints whose voices, she said, told her to save France. He painted it in 1876.

paintings.t: A Visit from the Old Mistress
paintings.why: A white woman visits former slaves on a plantation in Virginia after the Civil War, and the women's faces show different feelings. Winslow Homer painted this quiet scene about freedom and its limits in 1876.

In 1212 thousands of European children, many in poor families, set off on a march to the Holy Land, and most never got there. Gustave Doré drew this scene for a famous illustrated history of the Crusades in 1877.

paintings.t: Bohemond Alone Mounts the Rampart of Antioch
paintings.why: The Norman leader Bohemond climbs the walls of Antioch in 1098 in one of the crusaders' most daring moments. Gustave Doré drew it in dark, dramatic black and white.
The aged and blind Doge of Venice, Enrico Dandolo, speaks in front of the cathedral to stir up the Fourth Crusade. Gustave Doré illustrated it in 1877.

paintings.t: Luther at the Diet of Worms
paintings.why: In 1521 Martin Luther stands in front of the Emperor Charles V in Worms and refuses to take back his writings, saying 'Here I stand.' Anton von Werner painted this scene in 1877 as a founding moment of the Reformation.
The Pilgrims row ashore at Plymouth in December 1620, in a famous painting by Henry Bacon of 1877. The idea of the Pilgrims stepping onto Plymouth Rock is a later tradition.
In 1714 Peter the Great's new navy won its first big victory over the Swedish fleet at Gangut in the Baltic Sea. Alexey Bogolyubov painted the battle in 1877.

paintings.t: Arrival of the Normandy Train, Gare Saint-Lazare
paintings.why: Steam from a train fills the glass-roofed Gare Saint-Lazare in Paris in this painting by Claude Monet. He painted a series of the station in 1877 and fell in love with how smoke and light swirled around the engines of the new age.
Monet turns a busy train station into a cloud of blue and gray steam and sunlight. He painted this view of the Gare Saint-Lazare in 1877 and saw the railway as a modern wonder.

Tired, silent Grenadier Guards trudge back after the Battle of Inkerman in 1854. Elizabeth Thompson, later Lady Butler, painted this sad picture of the cost of war in 1877, when she was becoming one of Britain's best-known battle painters.

paintings.t: The Remorse of the Emperor Nero after the Murder of his Mother
paintings.why: The emperor Nero, who has just had his own mother Agrippina killed, lies on a couch filled with guilt while his attendants look away. John William Waterhouse painted this dark moment in 1878.

paintings.t: And When Did You Last See Your Father?
paintings.why: A small boy, the son of a Royalist, is questioned by Parliament's officers about where his father is hiding. William Frederick Yeames painted this tense scene from the English Civil War in 1878, and it became one of the most famous pictures in Victorian Britain.

paintings.t: Bismarck and Napoleon III after Sedan
paintings.why: The captured French emperor Napoleon III sits with the Prussian chancellor Otto von Bismarck after the Battle of Sedan in September 1870, the defeat that ended the French Empire. Wilhelm Camphausen painted it in 1878.

paintings.t: A Coming Storm in the Adirondacks
paintings.why: Dark storm clouds roll over a mountain valley, with trees swaying in the wind. Homer Watson was a self-taught painter from Ontario, whom Oscar Wilde admired. He painted dramatic skies and landscapes. The painting shows nature's power.

A sailing ship glows in dim, hazy light near the harbor of Saint John, New Brunswick. Henry Sandham painted Atlantic Canada's ports and coasts in a clear, careful way. The soft light on the water gives the scene a quiet mood. It's a calm harbor view.
The Visigoth king Alaric enters Athens in 396 AD, and the city's people stand before him in fear. Ludwig Thiersch painted this scene of the later fall of the classical world in 1879.

The poet Dante, in exile from Florence, passes some women in Verona while they whisper that he has been to hell, a joke on his great poem the Inferno. Antonio Cotti painted this famous scene in 1879, long after the Renaissance he helped start.

Hernán Cortés, the Spanish conqueror who led the fall of the Aztec empire in 1519 to 1521, in a 19th-century portrait by the Mexican painter José Salomé Pina. His conquest is still a deeply debated chapter of Mexican history.

paintings.t: Grand Duchess Sofia at the Novodevichy Convent
paintings.why: Peter the Great's half-sister Sofia, who ruled Russia in his place before he took over, was locked in a convent in 1689. Ilya Repin painted her in 1879 looking angry and trapped.

French troops attack in the snow at Champigny in December 1870, trying to break out of besieged Paris. Édouard Detaille painted this battle in 1879, as part of a wave of paintings in France remembering the war of 1870.

paintings.t: Muslim Troops Leaving Narbonne to Pepin the Short, 759
paintings.why: Pepin the Short, Charlemagne's father, finally takes the city of Narbonne in 759, driving out the Muslim garrison. This black-and-white illustration by Émile Bayard was made in 1880 for a history of France.

The famous Viking hero Ragnar Lodbrok sits beside his clever wife Kráka in this scene from the Norse sagas. The Swedish painter August Malmström made it around 1880, when Scandinavians were falling in love with their Viking past.

paintings.t: The Last Voyage of Henry Hudson
paintings.why: Henry Hudson, his son and a few others sit in a small boat in the icy northern sea after the crew turned against him in 1611 and cast them adrift. They were never seen again. John Collier painted it in 1881.

The 93rd Highlanders stand in a thin line against the Russian cavalry at Balaclava on October 25, 1854, refusing to retreat, and a newspaper called it the 'thin red line'. Robert Gibb painted the famous moment in 1881.

paintings.t: The Driving of the Last Spike
paintings.why: On May 10, 1869, the last spike joined the Union Pacific and Central Pacific railroads at Promontory, Utah, creating the first railroad across America. Thomas Hill painted the crowd at the ceremony in 1881.

French soldiers defend a village cemetery at Saint-Privat against German attackers during the Franco-Prussian War in August 1870. Alphonse de Neuville painted it in 1881 in a lifelike style meant to show how fiercely they fought.

The worn-out French army of General Bourbaki, starved and half frozen, crosses into Switzerland in February 1871 to escape the Germans, and Swiss people took the soldiers in. Édouard Castres, a Swiss painter who was there as a Red Cross volunteer, painted it in 1881.

Woods and hills spread out in the Laurentian Mountains of Quebec, painted in rich greens and browns. Homer Watson was called Canada's greatest landscape painter of his day. He painted what he saw around him in Ontario and Quebec. It's a calm, natural scene.
The Mayflower, the ship that carried about 100 Pilgrims to America in 1620, rests in the harbor at sunset while a boat heads to shore. William Halsall painted it in 1882.

paintings.t: The Favorites of the Emperor Honorius
paintings.why: The weak emperor Honorius was told that Rome had fallen and said it couldn't be, he had just fed her. He meant his pet chicken, which he had named Roma. John William Waterhouse shows the emperor with his birds in 1883.

At the sea battle of Svolder in the year 1000, King Olav Tryggvason's famous ship the Long Serpent was surrounded by enemy ships. According to the sagas he leapt overboard rather than be captured. Otto Sinding painted it in 1883.

Alexander Menshikov, once Peter the Great's best friend and the second most powerful man in Russia, sits in a hut in Siberia with his family after his fall from power. Vasily Surikov painted this sad scene in 1883.
French General Louis Faidherbe rides on a white horse at the Battle of Bapaume in January 1871, one of the few French successes in the late war. Charles Édouard Armand-Dumaresq painted it in 1883.

A group of men stand and sit in a conference room in Quebec City in 1864, planning a new country: Canada. The painter Robert Harris created it long after the meeting, and it shows 33 delegates gathered at the Quebec Conference. It became a symbol of the birth of Canada. The original burned in a fire in 1916, and this is a copy of the lost painting.

paintings.t: Morning of the Battle of Agincourt, 25th October 1415
paintings.why: King Henry V of England, with a small tired army, waits for the French on the morning of the Battle of Agincourt in 1415. John Gilbert painted the muddy scene in 1884.

paintings.t: The Meeting of Antony and Cleopatra
paintings.why: In 41 BC Cleopatra of Egypt arrives to meet the Roman general Mark Antony and wins him over with a spectacular show. Alma-Tadema paints her waiting under a golden canopy on her barge as Antony approaches, a meeting that changed Rome's history.
Titus's soldiers parade through Rome in AD 71 with treasure from the conquest of Jerusalem. Lawrence Alma-Tadema painted the great procession passing on a staircase of the city in 1885.
Steelworkers pour white-hot metal in a Belgian steelworks in a glowing picture by Constantin Meunier of about 1885. Meunier painted workers in factories and mines with great respect.

paintings.t: The Proclamation of the German Empire
paintings.why: On January 18, 1871, in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, the German princes proclaim King Wilhelm I of Prussia Emperor of Germany, with Bismarck in white at the center. Anton von Werner painted this third version in 1885.
Union ships under Admiral Farragut steam into Mobile Bay in August 1864, where he is said to have shouted 'Damn the torpedoes!' Julian Davidson made this color print in 1886.

Ulpiano Checa, who loved painting wild horses and chariots, shows hordes of mounted warriors charging across a snowy plain. The picture imagines the peoples who pushed into the Roman Empire at the end of antiquity.

paintings.t: Joan of Arc, Victorious over the English, Enters Orléans
paintings.why: On May 8, 1429 Joan of Arc rides into Orléans as a hero after the English siege is broken, and the crowd cheers her. Jean-Jacques Scherrer painted the triumph in 1887.

Smoking factory chimneys rise over green fields in Clichy, on the edge of Paris, in a painting by Vincent van Gogh of 1887. It shows how the city and its factories were spreading into the countryside.
Union and Confederate soldiers clash at Antietam on September 17, 1862, the bloodiest single day in American history. Thure de Thulstrup made this scene for a famous set of Civil War prints in 1887.
The Union army holds a long ridge while the Confederates attack across the fields at Gettysburg in July 1863, the turning point of the Civil War. Thure de Thulstrup made this view in 1887.

A mother cuddles her baby in a loving embrace, with a warm and tender mood. Paul Peel was a Canadian painter from London, Ontario, who became a star in Paris. He is known for tender pictures of mothers and children. It's a sweet, gentle family picture.

paintings.t: Fulvia and Mark Antony, or Fulvia's Revenge
paintings.why: Fulvia, the fierce wife of Mark Antony, takes revenge on the dead Cicero, the great speaker who had attacked her husband, in this gruesome scene from the civil wars after Caesar's death. The Spanish painter Francisco Maura y Montaner made it in 1888.
The sixteen-year-old Edward, called the Black Prince, stands among the dead after the Battle of Crécy in 1346, where English archers beat the French. Julian Russell Story painted it in 1888.

paintings.t: A Lost Cause: Flight of King James II
paintings.why: King James II, who had lost his throne in the Glorious Revolution of 1688, waits on the shore for a boat to take him into exile in France. Andrew Carrick Gow painted the sad moment in 1888, 200 years later.
Soldiers fight through smoke and trees at the Battle of Shiloh in Tennessee in April 1862, an early and very bloody battle of the Civil War. Thure de Thulstrup painted it in 1888.

A farm sits at the edge of a ravine, with trees and rolling land. Homer Watson, from Doon, Ontario, painted the farms and woods near his home. His quiet, thoughtful pictures became symbols of Canadian landscape. It's a gentle country view.

Colorful Japanese dolls and a fan are laid out together, with a bright patterned cloth. Paul Peel loved to paint beautiful objects, and Japanese goods were popular in Paris. The bright colors and rich textures are charming. It's a lovely still life.

paintings.t: Cicero Denounces Catiline in the Roman Senate
paintings.why: In 63 BC the great speaker Cicero stands and accuses Catiline of plotting against Rome, and the other senators move away from him. Cesare Maccari painted this fresco in the 1880s for the Italian Senate.
In March 1862 the ironclad warships Monitor and Virginia fought the first battle between armored ships, changing sea warfare forever. This color print was made in 1889.

A mother in a dark dress holds her small daughter on her lap in a quiet, tender moment at the end of the day. Paul Peel, a Canadian painter who became a star in Paris, was famous for warm pictures of home and childhood. The soft light and gentle pose make it feel cozy. It's a sweet picture of love at bedtime.
paintings.k: A mother holds her little girl. What bedtime story would you tell?

paintings.t: The Sack of Rome by the Visigoths on 24 August 410
paintings.why: In 410 the Visigoths under Alaric broke into Rome, the first time in about 800 years that an enemy had taken the city. Joseph-Noël Sylvestre's big painting of 1890 shows the invaders pulling down the statues of the old gods.

paintings.t: Joan of Arc at the Siege of Orléans
paintings.why: Joan of Arc, a teenage peasant girl who said saints told her to save France, rides into battle with her banner to lift the siege of Orléans in 1429. Jules Eugène Lenepveu painted this scene around 1890 for the Panthéon in Paris.

paintings.t: Cortés and Montezuma at Mexico City
paintings.why: The Spanish conqueror Hernán Cortés and the Aztec ruler Montezuma meet in the great city of Tenochtitlan in 1519, followed by war. This colorful print was made in the 1890s by the American lithographers Kurz and Allison.

In 1618 angry Protestant nobles threw two Catholic officials out of a window of Prague Castle. They survived by landing in a pile of rubbish, but it started the Thirty Years' War. The Czech painter Václav Brožík painted the dramatic scene in 1890.
Otto von Bismarck, the Prussian chancellor who united Germany under Prussia in 1871, in a portrait of 1890 by Franz von Lenbach. Bismarck was nicknamed the Iron Chancellor.

Confederate and Union soldiers fight in the woods at Chickamauga, Georgia, in September 1863, one of the largest and bloodiest battles of the Civil War in the West. This color print was made around 1890.

John Singer Sargent paints the soaring inside of the great church of Hagia Sophia, built by Justinian in 537 and turned into a mosque after the Ottoman conquest of 1453. He painted it on a trip to Istanbul in 1891.
A Union line holds against waves of Confederate attackers at the Battle of Franklin in Tennessee in 1864, one of the last big Confederate attacks of the war. This color print was made in 1891.

Edmund Blair Leighton shows Lady Godiva before her famous ride through Coventry, which in the legend she made to persuade her husband to lower the town's taxes. She lived in the years before the Norman Conquest.

A sunny, dry riverbed in the oasis town of Biskra in Algeria, with a faraway ridge and a few small figures. Maurice Cullen, a Montreal painter, traveled to North Africa and painted its vivid colors. He is best known for his snowy Canadian winter scenes. It's an unusual desert view by a painter of snow.
German officers rest in a smart French parlor during the siege of Paris, one with his boots on the table beside a piano. Anton von Werner, a German painter who was at the siege, painted it in 1894.

paintings.t: John, 7th Earl of Aberdeen, Later 1st Marquess, Montreal
paintings.why: A distinguished gentleman in formal dress sits in a stately pose. Robert Harris, who was born in Wales and grew up in Prince Edward Island, was one of Canada's top portrait painters. The Earl of Aberdeen was a governor general of Canada. It's a formal portrait of a public figure.

paintings.t: The Trial of Joan of Arc
paintings.why: Joan of Arc stands before her judges at her trial in 1431, after she was captured by the English allies. The French artist Louis-Maurice Boutet de Monvel painted her in a wide scene in the 1890s for a children's book.

Napoleon watches the huge Battle of Borodino in 1812 from a hill, looking small and uncertain among his generals. The Russian painter Vasily Vereshchagin painted him in 1897 as a worn, anxious commander.
Two cowboys race on horses to catch a runaway steer, in a scene full of speed and dust. Charles M. Russell painted it in 1897, drawing on his years working as a cowboy in Montana.

Two girls snuggle together on a sofa over a big book, absorbed in an exciting story. Laura Muntz Lyall was a Canadian painter from Toronto who became well known for her gentle pictures of children. She painted in a soft, delicate style and exhibited in Paris and London. It's a cozy picture of reading together.

Death, a skeleton on a winged creature, swoops over a plague-stricken city in this chilling painting. Arnold Böcklin made two versions in 1898, in the years after great epidemics had struck cities across Europe.

paintings.t: Vercingetorix Throws Down His Arms at the Feet of Julius Caesar
paintings.why: The Gaulish chief Vercingetorix surrenders to Julius Caesar in 52 BC after the siege of Alesia, ending a big revolt against Rome. Lionel Royer painted it in 1899, when French people thought of Vercingetorix as their first national hero.

paintings.t: The Captured King Gryting Is Brought Before King Harald
paintings.why: The conquered king Gryting is brought before Harald Fairhair in a scene from the Viking sagas. Erik Werenskiold drew it in 1899 for an illustrated edition of Snorri Sturluson's Heimskringla, the saga of the Norwegian kings.

The men of the Mayflower sign an agreement to make fair laws and govern themselves in the new colony. The Mayflower Compact of 1620 is one of the earliest steps toward self-government in America. Jean Leon Gerome Ferris painted it in 1899.

In June 1876 the Lakota and Cheyenne warriors defeated General Custer's soldiers at the Battle of the Little Bighorn, one of the greatest victories for Native Americans in the Plains Wars. Edgar Samuel Paxson painted this version in 1899.

paintings.t: Millicent Fawcett and Louisa Garrett Anderson
paintings.why: Millicent Fawcett, the leader of Britain's peaceful suffrage societies, sits with her niece Louisa Garrett Anderson. Fawcett believed in persuading Parliament by law-abiding campaigns, and she led the movement for decades.

paintings.t: Labour aux premières lueurs du jour
paintings.why: A farmer with oxen plows a field at dawn, in a misty light that shines on the earth. Horatio Walker, a Canadian painter from Ontario who lived on Île d'Orléans near Quebec City, painted the farmers and animals of rural Quebec. He admired the French painter Millet. It's a noble picture of work on the land.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: Children and a woman gather nuts in a forest in autumn, in warm light. Homer Watson was known for his landscapes but occasionally included people. The picture feels peaceful and golden. It's a cozy autumn day.

paintings.t: The Wounded Montcalm Is Brought Back to Quebec
paintings.why: The French commander Montcalm, mortally wounded on the Plains of Abraham, is carried back into Quebec City on horseback in 1759. Louis Bombled painted the sad moment in 1900.
Viking-age traders, called Varangians, sail a dragon-headed ship into a Slavic harbor in this glowing scene. The Russian painter Nicholas Roerich, who loved ancient history, painted it in 1901.
Cowboys, also called buckaroos, ride in the open West in this lively painting by Charles M. Russell, who worked as a cowboy himself before he became an artist. He painted it in 1902.

paintings.t: In the shade of the apple tree
paintings.why: A young woman sits quietly in the dappled shade of an apple tree on a sunny day. Horatio Walker painted the countryside of Quebec, where he lived much of the year. The soft light and calm mood are typical of his peaceful style. It's a restful country scene.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: Sultan Mehmed II rides in triumph through the gates of Constantinople after its fall in 1453, with red banners overhead. The Italian painter Fausto Zonaro, who worked for the Ottoman court, painted it in 1903.

The Ottoman army marches toward Constantinople in 1453 in a painting by Fausto Zonaro, an Italian artist who worked for the Ottoman sultans. The city fell after a siege of 53 days, ending the Byzantine Empire.

Swedish soldiers charge in a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva in 1700, where young King Charles XII beat the larger Russian army of Peter the Great. Peter lost the battle but learned from it and built a better army. Gustaf Cederström painted it in 1905.

On January 22, 1905, soldiers fired on peaceful workers marching to the Winter Palace to ask the tsar for help, killing and wounding many, an event that started the Revolution of 1905. Wojciech Kossak painted this scene of Bloody Sunday.

A portrait of a Huron-Wendat man, painted by Eugène Hamel, a Quebec artist. The Huron-Wendat have lived in the Quebec area for centuries. Painters of the time often recorded the faces of Indigenous people they knew. It's a quiet, dignified portrait.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: A stone church stands in a village in Brittany, France, painted in warm, soft colors. Emily Carr, a Canadian painter from British Columbia, studied in France in the early 1900s. She was inspired by the strong colors and shapes of French painting. It's from the years before she became known for her Pacific Coast paintings.

A dancer in a bright red dress stands with her arm raised in a flamenco pose, while a guitarist plays beside her. Clarence Gagnon, a Quebec painter, traveled widely in Europe and painted scenes from Spain. The title is the Spanish shout of praise, 'Olé!' It shows that Canadian artists also painted the world.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: Ilya Repin's lively early study for his painting of the crowds celebrating Tsar Nicholas II's October Manifesto of 1905, with swirls of red flags.

paintings.t: Leaders of the Women's Social and Political Union, about 1906
paintings.why: Women's Social and Political Union leaders meet around 1906. Founded by Emmeline Pankhurst in 1903 with the motto 'Deeds, not words,' the WSPU used marches and protests to demand votes for women in Britain.

People stroll and rest on a sunny beach with colorful parasols and striped beach tents at the seaside resort of Dinard in France. Clarence Gagnon painted this in his early career, when he was studying in Paris. The bright sand and sea are lively. It's a happy summer day at the beach.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.t: Pocahontas at the Court of King James
paintings.why: Pocahontas, dressed as an English lady, is presented to King James I in London in 1616. Richard Rummell made this colorful picture in 1907, three hundred years after the founding of Jamestown.
Tsar Peter the Great strides ahead so fast that his courtiers struggle to keep up in this lively painting, which shows his energy and force of will. Valentin Serov painted it in 1907.

paintings.t: Washington and Lafayette at Valley Forge
paintings.why: George Washington and the young French marquis de Lafayette ride through the snow at Valley Forge in the winter of 1777–1778, when the American army nearly starved but became a stronger force. John Ward Dunsmore painted it in 1907.

A church leader in rich robes sits in a dignified pose. Charles Huot was a well-known Quebec painter who made historical paintings and large decorations for the Quebec legislature. This portrait shows his skill with serious, formal subjects. It's an example of French-Canadian portraiture.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: A cow stands beside a fence in a soft, misty farmyard in the early morning. Horatio Walker was known as the painter of Quebec farm life, and he sold many paintings in the United States. The gentle light and quiet mood are typical of his style. It's a peaceful rural scene.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: Nellie McClung, the Canadian writer and activist who led the campaign that made Manitoba the first province to give women the vote in 1916. This portrait is from about 1910.

A farmyard in Brittany, with old buildings and the glow of sunlight. Emily Carr painted this during her time in France. The bright colors show she was learning from the modern painters there. She would later bring these lessons home to Canada.

Trees in fall colors line a country lane in France. Emily Carr studied in Paris and Brittany, and learned about the bright colors of Post-Impressionism. She painted this with a bold, free brush. It shows her artistic growth before returning to Canada.

A woman in a stylish dress sits in a gentle, modern style. James Wilson Morrice was a Canadian painter who lived mostly in Paris and was friends with Matisse. He painted with soft, bright colors and simplified shapes. He's now seen as Canada's first great modern painter.

Crowds joyfully wave flags and red banners in the streets after Tsar Nicholas II promised civil rights and a parliament in October 1905. Ilya Repin painted this big crowd scene, which captures the hope, and the tension, of Russia's first revolution.

paintings.t: First Nations War Canoes in Alert Bay
paintings.why: Large carved canoes sit on the beach of Alert Bay, a First Nations village on the coast of British Columbia. Emily Carr traveled to Indigenous villages along the Pacific Coast to paint and to record carvings and village life. She wanted to preserve what she saw. It's an important record of the West Coast in the early 1900s.

A city street scene of tall buildings and giant signs, in a bold, simple style. David Milne was a Canadian painter who lived in New York and later in Ontario. He made pictures of cities, signs, and nature with clean shapes and a light touch. It's an early work from his time in New York.

A big carved canoe from the Pacific Northwest Coast, with bold shapes and strong colors. Emily Carr, a painter from Victoria, British Columbia, visited Indigenous villages to record their carvings and canoes. She was one of the first non-Indigenous artists in Canada to take this art seriously. The picture shows her respect for the beauty of what she saw.

A big wooden community house stands in the village of Ucluelet on the west coast of Vancouver Island. Emily Carr visited the village in 1912 and painted the building with bold, simple shapes. She wanted to record the Indigenous villages that were changing quickly. It's an important historical record as well as a painting.

paintings.t: Lewis and Clark Meeting Indians at Ross' Hole
paintings.why: The explorers Meriwether Lewis and William Clark, who crossed the continent in 1804 to 1806, meet the Salish people at Ross' Hole in what is now Montana. Charles M. Russell painted it in 1912 for the Montana Capitol.

paintings.t: Official Program, Woman Suffrage Procession, March 3, 1913
paintings.why: A colorful program for the great Woman Suffrage Procession held in Washington on March 3, 1913, the day before Woodrow Wilson became president. About 5,000 women marched down Pennsylvania Avenue demanding the vote.

A Life magazine cover from the suffrage-themed issue of February 1913, in black and gold, by Rea Irvin, who later designed the New Yorker's first cover. Magazines like Life helped bring the vote debate to every living room.

A quiet, simple painting in dark tones, with bold shapes. David Milne painted both in New York and in the Canadian woods, always using a thin, delicate touch. He is now considered one of Canada's most important modern painters. It's an early example of his inventive style.
The Pilgrims and the Wampanoag people share a harvest meal in the autumn of 1621, the event we remember as the first Thanksgiving. Jennie Augusta Brownscombe painted this friendly gathering in 1914.

paintings.t: Emmeline Pankhurst Arrested outside Buckingham Palace
paintings.why: Police carry the British suffragette leader Emmeline Pankhurst away on May 21, 1914, after she tried to bring a petition to King George V at Buckingham Palace. She was arrested many times for the cause of women's votes.

A small bouquet of wildflowers bursts with orange, yellow and blue against a dark background. Tom Thomson is best known for landscapes, but he also painted flowers as small sketches. The glowing colors have a joyful energy. It's a rare and cheerful still life.

A white house with a red roof stands in the sunny Caribbean, painted in a few clean, bright colors. James Wilson Morrice traveled to Cuba and the Caribbean in the winter. His light, simple style was ahead of its time. It's a sun-filled picture.

A camp in the woods is lit by the first rays of sunrise, with smoke rising from a campfire. Homer Watson painted this late in his career, with softer colors. The warm light is magic. It's a quiet and calm early morning.

Bright red and orange autumn leaves stand out against the dark woods, painted on a small panel. Tom Thomson loved the Ontario fall, when the maples blaze with color. His small sketches captured the feeling of the season. It's a vivid example of Canadian autumn.

Charred tree trunks stand on a hill after a forest fire, with new green growth rising beneath them. Tom Thomson saw the burnt land in Algonquin Park and made it the subject of a powerful sketch. Despite the damage, the spring colors show hope. It's a famous image of nature recovering.

paintings.t: Blue Lake: Sketch for "In the Northland"
paintings.why: A deep blue lake is surrounded by bright trees in a quick, colorful study. Tom Thomson made it as a first idea for his painting 'In the Northland.' The sketch is full of fresh, direct feeling. It shows how he worked outdoors, painting fast.

A woman in a golden gown, a symbol of Liberty, strides across a map of the United States in which the states where women could vote glow in gold. Henry Mayer's cartoon, published in 1915 in Puck magazine, shows the suffrage movement spreading from the West.

paintings.t: Vote for the Woman Suffrage Amendment
paintings.why: A map shows in yellow the states where women already had equal suffrage in 1915, and the poster urges voters to approve the woman suffrage amendment in November. New York's vote failed that year but passed two years later.

paintings.t: I Didn't Raise My Girl to Be a Voter
paintings.why: An anti-suffrage poster from 1915, made by opponents of women voting, borrows the title of a famous song. It shows what the suffragists were up against.

Boats rest by the shore of a lake in dappled light. Tom Thomson often painted on Canoe Lake in Algonquin Park, where he lived and worked as a guide. The little sketch is relaxed and bright. It's a happy picture of life on the water.

paintings.t: President Wilson Says Votes for Women
paintings.why: A cartoon by Nina Allender, the cartoonist of Alice Paul's National Woman's Party, shows suffragists behind bars after being arrested for picketing outside the White House in 1917. They had held signs asking President Wilson 'How long must women wait for liberty?'

A map of North America, with the states and provinces where women could vote marked, on a suffrage poster from 1917. By then women could vote in many western states, and the poster urges the rest to follow.

Canadian gunners push and pull an artillery piece through deep mud at Passchendaele in late 1917, one of the worst battles of the war. Alfred Bastien, a Belgian painter working for the Canadian War Memorials, painted this.
A print of a cemetery on Vimy Ridge, the French hill where Canadian soldiers won a famous victory in April 1917. It was made as a record of the war as soon as it ended.

paintings.t: A Grave and a Mine Crater at La Boisselle, August 1917
paintings.why: A huge crater from a mine explosion and a lonely grave mark the old battlefield at La Boisselle, on the Somme. William Orpen, a British official war artist, painted it in 1917.

paintings.t: The Pogrom of the Winter Palace
paintings.why: Soldiers and workers rush into the Winter Palace, the home of the Russian government, on the night of October 25, 1917, when the Bolsheviks seized power. Ivan Vladimirov painted it in 1917 as an eyewitness.

Rows of simple huts painted in camouflage patterns stand in a muddy World War I camp. Maurice Cullen was a Canadian official war artist who went to France in 1918. His paintings record what soldiers' daily lives were like. It's a quiet record of wartime.

A gray dawn light shines over a battlefield, with trenches and bare ground. Maurice Cullen painted this as an official Canadian war artist. The quiet colors seem to show both beauty and sadness. It's a thoughtful war landscape.

The ruined village of Ablain-Saint-Nazaire in France sits in rubble after the fighting of World War I. Maurice Cullen painted the ruins after Canadian troops fought near here at Vimy Ridge. The broken buildings show the cost of war. It's a record of a village changed by history.

A scene of a French town damaged by war, with broken walls and a quiet sky. Maurice Cullen painted the places where Canadian soldiers served in 1918. The painting is quiet and respectful. It's part of a series that preserves the memory of the war.

paintings.t: We Are Making a New World
paintings.why: A broken, twisted forest of shattered tree stumps stands in a landscape ripped by shell craters, under a bitter-sounding title. Paul Nash painted this in 1918 as an official war artist, and its irony made it one of the best-known pictures of World War I.
A.Y. Jackson, a founding member of Canada's Group of Seven, painted the green haze of a gas attack over the town of Liévin in 1918, while he was a Canadian war artist.

A bare, shell-torn hill called the Pimple glows red in the evening light near Vimy Ridge, where Canadian troops had fought in 1917. A.Y. Jackson, who later helped found the Group of Seven, painted it in 1918.
A single aeroplane sails among huge clouds in a dreamy, modern view of the war in the sky. C. R. W. Nevinson painted it in 1918 for Canada's war memorial collection.
Women work in a roaring factory filling shells for the war effort in 1918. Stanhope Forbes painted this scene of the many women who took on jobs once done by men while the soldiers were away.

Soldiers gather in a candlelit American Red Cross canteen at the front in France. Henry Ossawa Tanner, a Black American painter who lived in France, volunteered with the Red Cross and painted this in 1918.

paintings.t: Amiens, the Key of the West
paintings.why: The Australian war artist Arthur Streeton paints the soft green countryside around Amiens, the city that the Allies defended and then used for their big attack of August 1918.

A huge crowd with flags and banners packs a Toronto street to celebrate the end of World War I. George Agnew Reid was a Canadian painter who was a leader in Toronto's art world. He painted this on the first Armistice Day in 1918 or 1919. It's a great record of public joy.

paintings.t: Forging 6-inch Shells - Cluff Ammunition Company, Toronto
paintings.why: Factory workers hammer glowing red-hot metal into shells in a busy, smoky factory. George Agnew Reid was commissioned to paint Canada's wartime work, including women and men in factories. The orange glow of the hot metal lights up the dark room. It's a record of the home front in World War I.

Paul Nash paints a wrecked, muddy landscape near Ypres in Belgium, with flooded craters and splintered trees. Made for the British government's war memorial project, it shows the destruction of the battlefield in 1919.

Wyndham Lewis shows an artillery position under fire in sharp, blocky shapes, like a machine of broken glass. He had served as a gunner himself before becoming an official war artist, and he painted this in 1919.

paintings.t: Le Pont de glace à Québec
paintings.why: People cross the frozen St. Lawrence River at Quebec on an ice bridge in winter. Clarence Gagnon loved to paint Quebec's snow, villages and winter life. In cold winters the river froze solid, and people could walk across. It's a cheerful picture of Canadian winter.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: A woman and a child stand in front of the Capitol on a poster for the League of Women Voters. The League was founded in 1920, the year the 19th Amendment gave American women the right to vote.

A huge worker holding a red flag strides over the crowded rooftops of a Russian city in this symbol of the Bolshevik revolution. Boris Kustodiev painted it in 1920, three years after the Bolsheviks took power.

paintings.t: Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge
paintings.why: A red triangle slices into a white circle in El Lissitzky's famous poster, a symbol of the Red Army defeating the White Army in the Russian Civil War. It was made in 1919 and 1920 and mixes politics with modern abstract art.
A Soviet poster of 1920 uses bold colors and cartoon figures in the style of the revolution's propaganda posters, which taught people about the new government in a country where many could not read.

A poster compares life before October 1917 and after it, using simple pictures so that everyone could understand the Bolshevik message. It was made by Stepan Mukharsky in 1920, during the Russian Civil War.

Emily Carr is shown at her easel in a room with strong, simple shapes and bold colors. She was one of Canada's greatest painters, who lived much of her life in British Columbia with her pet monkey, dogs and her paintbrushes. She wasn't widely recognized until she was in her fifties, when the Group of Seven discovered her art. It's a picture of an artist at work.

Pilgrims and Wampanoag people gather for the harvest feast of 1621, which later became Thanksgiving. Jennie Augusta Brownscombe painted this version in 1925 after she had painted the subject many times.
Vladimir Lenin, the leader of the Bolshevik Revolution, lies in his coffin surrounded by red flags and officials in January 1924. Isaak Brodsky painted this memorial scene in 1925.

Ghostly soldiers rise out of the fields near the Menin Gate, the great memorial at Ypres to the missing of World War I. Will Longstaff painted this in 1927 and it became one of Australia's most famous war paintings.

Tall carved totem poles stand against a dark forest and a sky in a First Nations village in northern British Columbia. Emily Carr visited Kitwancool (Gitanyow) in 1928 and painted the poles with great power and respect. She felt she was recording a culture that deserved to be remembered. It's one of her strongest paintings of the Northwest Coast.

A still, dark pool in the forest of Temagami in northern Ontario, with trees and rocks. David Milne painted the Canadian wilderness in thin, delicate watercolors. The mirror-like pool is quiet and mysterious. It's a peaceful picture of northern Ontario.

Florence Owens Thompson sits in a pea-pickers' camp in California in 1936, with her children turned away. Dorothea Lange's photograph for the government became the best-known image of the Great Depression.

paintings.t: Farmer and Sons Walking in the Face of a Dust Storm, Cimarron County, Oklahoma
paintings.why: A farmer and his sons walk bent against a huge dust cloud in Oklahoma in April 1936, during the Dust Bowl. Arthur Rothstein took this photograph for the government, which hired photographers to show how hard the Depression was.

paintings.t: Allie Mae Burroughs, Hale County, Alabama
paintings.why: Allie Mae Burroughs, the wife of a cotton sharecropper, looks straight at the camera in 1936. Walker Evans took this photograph for a project that became the book Let Us Now Praise Famous Men, about poor farming families during the Depression.

paintings.t: Frank Tengle, Bud Fields, and Floyd Burroughs, Cotton Sharecroppers
paintings.why: Three cotton sharecroppers sit together on a porch in Alabama in 1936. Walker Evans photographed families in Hale County for the government and a magazine, and the dignity in the faces made the photographs famous.

paintings.t: Floyd Burroughs, Cotton Sharecropper, Hale County, Alabama
paintings.why: Floyd Burroughs, a cotton sharecropper in Alabama, looks into the camera in 1936. Walker Evans photographed him and his family for a famous project about rural poverty in the Great Depression.

A man and woman carry their bags along an empty road in California in 1937, with a billboard above them that says 'Next time try the train.' Dorothea Lange's photo shows the ordeal of families who moved west to look for work.

A poster from the Works Progress Administration, the New Deal program that put millions of Americans back to work building roads, bridges and schools, as well as paying artists and writers. The workers and a wheat stalk show the idea that work lifts up the whole country.

paintings.t: Power Farming Displaces Tenants, Childress County, Texas
paintings.why: An empty farmhouse stands in a wide field of plowed furrows in Texas in 1938, a farm where tractors had taken the place of families who once worked the land as tenant farmers. Dorothea Lange photographed it for the government to show how the Depression and new machines pushed families off the land.

paintings.t: Ex-Slave with a Long Memory, Alabama
paintings.why: An elderly woman in Alabama who was born into slavery stands in front of her house in 1938. Dorothea Lange's photograph, taken during the Great Depression, honors a person who remembered a very different time in American history.

paintings.t: Jim Norris, Homesteader, Pie Town, New Mexico
paintings.why: Jim Norris, a homesteader in Pie Town, New Mexico, in 1940, photographed in rare color film by Russell Lee for the government. The color makes it feel as if the Depression is happening now.

paintings.t: School Children Singing, Pie Town, New Mexico
paintings.why: Children sing together in a school in Pie Town, New Mexico, in 1940, in a color photograph by Russell Lee. Pie Town was a farming community in the Depression years.

paintings.t: Gun Crew Loading a 5-inch 38 Caliber Gun
paintings.why: A sailor strains to load a big gun aboard a navy ship in 1940 in a powerful, poster-like painting. McClelland Barclay, an American illustrator who joined the US Navy as an artist, painted the sailors at work.

Ella Watson, a cleaning woman at a government office, stands with a mop and broom in front of an American flag in 1942. Gordon Parks, then a young photographer on his first assignment for the government, named it American Gothic as a tribute to Grant Wood's painting.

paintings.t: Ella Watson at Home, Washington, D.C.
paintings.why: Ella Watson with her family at home in Washington, D.C., in 1942, in a photograph by Gordon Parks. He followed her through her day to show the life of a working mother in the Depression years.
American soldiers crouch among tropical trees during an assault in the Pacific in 1943. Aaron Bohrod was an official US Army war artist who painted the war in the Pacific.

The great steel bridge at Nijmegen, which the Allies captured in September 1944 in the failed Operation Market Garden, arches across the river. Alex Colville, a Canadian war artist, painted it in 1944.
Army trucks roll along a road in the green hills of Yorkshire, England, where Canadian soldiers trained in 1944 before D-Day. Alex Colville was an official Canadian war artist.

paintings.t: Landing Craft Assault off Southern France
paintings.why: Landing craft head toward the coast in the Allied invasion of southern France in August 1944, in a painting by the Canadian war artist Alex Colville.
A Canadian tank rolls through the shattered streets of Ortona, Italy, where Canadian troops fought a fierce street battle in December 1943. Charles Comfort was an official Canadian war artist.
A line of Canadian tanks rolls over a green landscape in 1944. Bruno Bobak served as a Canadian war artist and made sketches and paintings of what he saw.
A dark London street during the wartime blackout, when all lights were turned off so that bombers could not find the city. Molly Bobak, a Canadian war artist, painted it in 1944.
An LVT, a tracked amphibious vehicle, drives up a beach on Saipan in June 1944 during the fighting in the Pacific. William F. Draper was a US Navy combat artist who went into battle with the troops.
Landing boats, soldiers and equipment fill Utah Beach in Normandy after the D-Day landings of June 6, 1944. Joseph Gary Sheahan, a combat artist, painted the scene in watercolor.

paintings.t: Loading of the Vultee Vengeance Planes
paintings.why: Ground crews load Vultee Vengeance dive-bombers in a busy scene from the war. Julien Binford painted it in 1944 as one of the US Army's combat artists.
Fire sweeps through a battlefield in the Pacific in 1944 in a painting by William F. Draper, a US Navy combat artist, who painted battles he had seen.

Trucks and landing craft sit on a muddy beach in the Netherlands in 1945, painted by the Canadian war artist Alex Colville. Canadian troops helped liberate the Netherlands in the last year of the war.

paintings.t: Night Air Attack before the Hitler Line
paintings.why: Flares and searchlights light up the sky over the Italian hills before an attack on the Hitler Line in 1944. Lawren P. Harris, an official Canadian war artist whose father was the famous Group of Seven painter Lawren Harris, painted it.

paintings.t: Canadian Women's Army Corps Brass Band
paintings.why: Women of the Canadian Women's Army Corps play in a brass band in 1945. Molly Bobak was a Canadian war artist who painted women's role in the armed forces.

paintings.t: Formal Japan Surrender aboard the U.S.S. Missouri
paintings.why: On September 2, 1945, aboard the battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, Japanese officials signed the surrender that ended World War II. Sidney Simon, a US Army artist, painted it.

A quiet field with open pits near the huts of Bergen-Belsen shows the horror of the Nazi concentration camp, which British and Canadian troops reached in April 1945. Alex Colville, a Canadian war artist, painted what he saw there, and the painting is a record of the Holocaust.

paintings.t: Alan Shepard in the Freedom 7 Capsule
paintings.why: Astronaut Alan Shepard sits in the tiny Freedom 7 capsule before his flight on May 5, 1961, when he became the first American in space. The flight lasted only 15 minutes.

Medics rush a wounded soldier to a waiting helicopter in a swirl of blue, in a painting of 1967 by Ronald A. Wilson, a US Army combat artist in Vietnam. Medical evacuation helicopters saved thousands of lives.
Ronald A. Wilson painted this night scene in purple shades in 1967, as a US Army combat artist. The name refers to the starlight scopes that helped soldiers see in the dark.
Flares light up the night sky while glowing lines of tracer fire cross the dark in this blue painting of 1967 by Ronald A. Wilson. It shows a night when a base answered a mortar attack.
A swirling, almost abstract picture of a trail through the jungle in Vietnam by James Pollock in 1967. He was one of the Army's combat artists, who were sent to record the war in their own style.

Our blue Earth rises over the gray edge of the Moon in this photograph taken by astronaut William Anders on Christmas Eve 1968 during Apollo 8, the first time people had seen the whole Earth from another world. It changed how many people thought about the planet.
Soldiers work on a big artillery gun in Vietnam in 1968 in a painting by David Fairrington. Fairrington was a member of the US Army combat art team, which sent artists to Vietnam to record the war.
A soldier carries a radio, the lifeline of a patrol, in a tall, bold painting by David Fairrington. He painted it in Vietnam in 1968 as part of the US Army's combat art program.
A soldier strides through golden grass in Vietnam in a painting of 1968 by David Fairrington. The Army's combat artists tried to show both the work and the feelings of the soldiers.
Vietnamese women in cone-shaped hats gather in a colorful, patterned scene by David Fairrington in 1968. The Army's combat artists also painted the Vietnamese people they met.
Two Vietnamese girls lean close to each other in a gentle painting by David Fairrington from 1968. It shows the everyday life of civilians alongside the war.
A Cobra attack helicopter, one of the most important aircraft of the Vietnam War, is painted in dark glassy shapes by Stephen H. Randall in 1968 as part of the US Army combat art program.
A helicopter waits on the ground in a muddy field in Vietnam, in a watercolor by Stephen H. Randall in 1968. Helicopters were everywhere in the Vietnam War, carrying troops and supplies.
Two soldiers lean over the edge of a bunker in Vietnam in a sketchy watercolor by Stephen H. Randall in 1968, made as part of the US Army's combat art program.
Medics treat a wounded soldier in a busy scene by Stephen H. Randall from 1968, one of the US Army combat artists sent to record the war in Vietnam.
Soldiers in dark, heavy shapes struggle in a tense scene by Stephen H. Randall from 1968. The US Army combat artists painted both the action and the feelings of the war.

paintings.t: A Man on the Moon (Buzz Aldrin, Apollo 11)
paintings.why: Buzz Aldrin stands on the Moon on July 20, 1969, in a photograph taken by Neil Armstrong, whose reflection you can see in Aldrin's gold visor. It is one of the most famous photographs ever taken.
A Saturn V rocket rises on a pillar of fire and smoke at the Kennedy Space Center on July 16, 1969, carrying the Apollo 11 crew to the Moon.

paintings.t: Buzz Aldrin's Bootprint on the Moon
paintings.why: A single bootprint in the gray Moon dust, taken by the Apollo 11 astronauts to study the lunar soil. This close-up has become a symbol of the first human steps on the Moon in July 1969.

paintings.t: Aldrin Looks Back at Tranquility Base
paintings.why: Buzz Aldrin looks back at the landing site, Tranquility Base, in the bright gray landscape of the Moon, with the lunar module Eagle behind him. Neil Armstrong took the photograph in July 1969.

paintings.t: Buzz Aldrin Descends the Lunar Module Ladder
paintings.why: Buzz Aldrin climbs down the ladder of the Apollo 11 lunar module Eagle onto the Moon in July 1969. Neil Armstrong took the picture, and Aldrin was the second person to walk on the Moon.

paintings.t: Buzz Aldrin and the U.S. Flag on the Moon
paintings.why: Buzz Aldrin stands beside the American flag on the Moon on July 20, 1969. The flag was held out by a wire so that it would look like it was flying in the airless Moon.

paintings.t: The Apollo 11 Crew: Armstrong, Collins and Aldrin
paintings.why: The crew of Apollo 11: Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins and Buzz Aldrin, in their white space suits. Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the Moon in July 1969 while Collins stayed in orbit.

paintings.t: Apollo 11 Rolls Out to the Launch Pad
paintings.why: The huge Saturn V rocket for Apollo 11 is carried slowly toward the launch pad on a giant crawler in May 1969. At 110 meters tall, it was the most powerful rocket ever built at the time.

paintings.t: Astronaut James Irwin Salutes the Flag, Apollo 15
paintings.why: Astronaut James Irwin salutes the flag beside the lunar module and the moon buggy, the lunar rover, in 1971. Apollo 15 was the first mission to use a rover on the Moon, and David Scott took the picture.
The whole Earth, round and blue and shining, photographed by the Apollo 17 astronauts on their way to the Moon in December 1972. The Blue Marble is one of the most reproduced images in history.
